And God records what they plan.” He said: These are the hypocrites who say, when they are present with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he orders them to do something, they say, We obey. But when they leave him, a party of them will change what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, says. And God records what they plan. He said: What they say. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said, his statement: And they say, ‘We obey,’ but when they depart from you, a party of them will say something other than what you say, he said: They change what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And they say, ‘We obey,’ but when they leave you, a party of them will say something other than what you say, and they are people who used to say in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, We believe in God and His Messenger, so that their blood and property would be safe. But when they left the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would say something other than what they said in his presence, so God criticized them and said, A party of them will say something other than what you say, meaning they would change what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: A group of them have a house other than what you say, they are the people of hypocrisy. As for raising obedience, it is by the omitted word that is indicated by the apparent meaning of the statement, which is: Your command is obedience, or: From us is obedience. As for his saying: A group’s house, the ta’ of house is moved with a fatha in all the readings of Medina, Iraq, and all other readings, because it is a lam of action. Some of the Iraqi readers would pronounce it silently, then merge it with the letter taa, because they are similar in their point of articulation. Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading in this regard is to omit the assimilation, because they - I mean the ta’ and the ta’ - are two different letters. If this is the case, then omitting the assimilation is the more eloquent of the two languages among the Arabs, and the other language - I mean the assimilation in this regard - is permissible and reported. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So turn away, O Muhammad, from these hypocrites who say to you in what you command them: Your command is obedience, but when they leave you they disobey what you command them to do and change it to what you forbade them from doing, and leave them to what they are doing of misguidance, and be satisfied with me as a vengeance against them, and trust, O Muhammad, in God, meaning: and you entrust your matter to God, and trust in Him in your affairs, and entrust them to Him, and God is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs, meaning: and God is sufficient for you - that is: and God is sufficient for you - as a Disposer of affairs, that is: in what He commands you, and a Guardian for it, and a Defender of you and a Supporter.
4:82: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: Do they not ponder the Qur’an? Do not those who spend the night ponder over what you say to them, O Muhammad, is the Book of God, so that they may know God’s proof against them in obeying you and following your command, and that what you have brought them of revelation is from their Lord, because its meanings are consistent, its rulings are in agreement, some of it supports others in belief, and some of it testifies to others in verification. If that were from someone other than God, its rulings would differ, its meanings would contradict each other, and some of it would reveal the corruption of some, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Do they not then consider the Qur’an carefully? Had it been from other than God, they would surely have found within it much discrepancy. That is, God’s statement does not differ, and it is the truth, there is no falsehood in it, even though people’s statement differs. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: The Qur’an does not contradict some parts of it, nor does it contradict some parts of it. Whatever people are ignorant of, it is only due to the shortcomings of their minds and their ignorance! And he recited: And if it had been from other than God, they would have found within it much discrepancy. He said: So it is incumbent upon the believer to say: All is from God, and to believe in what is ambiguous, and not to compare some parts with others. And if he is ignorant of a matter and does not know it, he should say: What God said is true, and he should know that God did not say a statement and then contradict it. He should believe in the truth of what came from God. Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an? He said. Focus upon means to look into it.
4:83: Abu Ja'far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: And when there comes to them report of security or fear, they spread it around, and if this group that had gone to bed had something other than what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, a report of security, then the ha' and the mim in His statement: And when there comes to them, are from mentioning the group that had gone to bed, He, the Most High, says: And when report comes to them about a raiding Muslim company that they have become safe from their enemy by defeating them, or fear, he says: or their fear of their enemy by their enemy being afflicted by them, they spread it around, he says: they spread it and disseminated it among the people before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and before the arrival of the raiding companies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the ha' in His statement: they spread it around, is from mentioning the matter. Its interpretation is that they spread the matter of security or fear that had come to them. It is said: So-and-so spread this report, and spread it. From this is the saying of Abu Al-Aswad: He spread it among the people until it was as if there was a fire lit in the high places with holes. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it, meaning: they hasten to spread it and diffuse it. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And if there comes to them report of security or fear, they spread it around, meaning: If there comes to them report that they are safe from their enemy, or that they are afraid of them, they spread the report around until their enemy hears about them. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it, meaning: they spread it and spread it widely. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And if there comes to them report of security or fear, they spread it around. He said this in the report, if a group of Muslims went out to war and informed the people among themselves and they said: The Muslims suffered such and such from their enemy, and the enemy suffered such and such from the Muslims, so they spread it around among themselves, without the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, being the one who informed them. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said, They spread it around, he said: They announced it and spread it around. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, They spread it, he said: They disseminated it. He said: And those who spread it were al-Nas 114:either hypocrites, or others who were weak. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: They spread it and circulated it, and they are the people of hypocrisy. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: And if they had referred it, the matter that befell them from their enemy and the Muslims, to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those in authority over them - meaning: and to their leaders - and remained silent and did not spread the report that came to them, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or those in authority over them, were the ones who would take charge of the report about that, after they had established its authenticity or length, and they would correct it if it was authentic, or invalidate it if it was false, because those among them who extract it would know it, meaning: because the truth of that report that came to them, those who search for it and extract it, from them, meaning: those in authority, and the ha’ and the mim in His statement: from them, are from the mention of those in authority, meaning: because those in authority would know that from those in authority who extract it. And whoever extracts something that was hidden from the sight of the eyes or from the knowledge of the hearts, then it is for him: extracted. It is said: he extracted the well, if he extracted its water, and he extracted it, and the extract is the water extracted from the ground, and from it the saying of the poet: Close to his land, his enemies cannot reach him, he is a stubborn, stubborn man Meaning: Nabatean, extracted water. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And if they had referred it back to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, he says: And if they had been silent and referred the hadith back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those in authority among them so that he would speak about it, those who extract it would have known it, meaning: from the report, and they are those who investigate the report. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And if they had referred it back to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, he says: to their scholars, those among them who investigate it would have known it, those who investigate it and are concerned with it would have known it. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And if they had referred it back to the Messenger, so that he would be the one to inform them, and to those in authority among them, jurisprudence in religion and reason. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah: And if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, knowledge, who deduce it from among them, they would have followed it up and investigated it. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Laith told us, on the authority of Mujahid: For those of them who seek to deduce it from Him, he said: Those who ask about it and feel it out. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: They deduce it, he said: Their saying: What was it? What did you hear? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: Those who deduce it, he said: They sense it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For the knowledge of those among them who seek to deduce it, he said: For the knowledge of those among them who seek to discern it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: They deduce it from them, he said: They follow it. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it, until he reached, and to those in authority among them, he said: The rulers who are in charge of war against them, who think and consider what report comes to them: Is it true or false? Is it false so they invalidate it, or is it true so they verify it? He said: This is in war, and he recited, and they broadcast it, and if they had done otherwise, and referred it back to God, to the Messenger, and to those in authority among them, the verse. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Had it not been for the favor of God upon you, O believers, through His grace, guidance, and mercy, and had He not saved you from what He has afflicted these hypocrites with, who say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he commands them to do something: Obedience, and when they leave him, a group of them does something other than what he says, you would have been like them, and you would have followed Satan, except for a few, just as those whose description He has described followed him. And He addressed with His Most High’s words: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, those whom He addressed with His Most High’s words: O you who have believed, take your precautions and go forth in companies or go forth all together (An-Nisa’: 17). Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the few whom He excluded in this verse: Who are they? And from what attributes did He exclude them? Some of them said: They are the inferrs among those in authority. He excluded them from his statement: For His knowledge is for those among them who infer it, and he denied that they know by inferring what others among the inferrs know of the report that comes to them of security or fear. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It is only: Those who extract it from among them know it - except for a few of them - and had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few, he said: you would have all followed Satan. As for his statement: except for a few, it is like his statement: those who seek to extract it from among them would have known it, except for a few. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, reading, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few, he said, he says: you would have all followed Satan. As for except for a few, it is like his saying: those who extract it from among them would have known it, except for a few. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, something similar to it - meaning something similar to what Qatada said - and he said: They would have known it except for a little. Others said: Rather, they are the group that God described as saying to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Obedience, and when they left him, they planned something other than what they said. The meaning of the statement is: And when something came to them about security or fear, they spread it around, except for a few of them. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few, is at the beginning of the verse about the hypocrites, he said: And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it. What is meant by a few are the believers, like the statement of God the Almighty: Praise be to God, who has sent down upon His Servant the Book and has not made therein any crookedness * [[right]] (al-Kahf 18:1-2) He says: Praise be to God, who sent down the Book as justice and uprightness, and has not made therein any crookedness. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: This verse is presented and followed, it is: They spread it, except for a few of them, and had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, neither few nor many would have been saved. Others said: Rather, this is an exception to His statement: You would have followed Satan. They said: Those who were excluded were people who did not intend to do what the others intended to do, which was to follow Satan. So God recognized those whom He saved from that and the place of His grace towards them, and He excluded the others who did not do what the others did. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say, regarding His statement: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few, he said: They are the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They had told themselves about matters of Satan’s matters, except for a group of them. Others said that the meaning of this is: And had it not been for the grace and mercy of God upon you, you would all have followed Satan. They said: His statement, except a few, was used as an exception in the wording, and it is evidence of all and comprehensiveness, and that had it not been for the grace and mercy of God upon them, no one would have been saved from misguidance. So His statement, except a few, was made evidence of comprehensiveness, and they cited as evidence for that the statement of Al-Tirmah bin Hakim, in praise of Yazid bin Al-Muhallab: I smell a lot of generosity, but few faults and faults They said: The apparent meaning of this statement is describing the praised one as having faults and defects, and it is known that its meaning is that he has no faults or defects. Because whoever describes a man as having faults, even if he describes the faults he has as few, is only criticizing him and not praising him. But that is based on what we have described of denying all faults from him. They said: Likewise, his statement: You would have followed Satan, except for a few, means: You would all have followed Satan. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these statements in my opinion is the statement of the one who said: On my authority, except for a little of the broadcasting. He said: The meaning of the statement is: And if something of security or fear comes to them, they broadcast it except for a little, even if they refer it back to the Messenger. We said that this is more correct, because the statement on this matter is not without one of the statements we mentioned. And it is not permissible for it to be from his saying: You would have followed Satan, because whoever God has favored with His favor and mercy, it is not permissible for him to be from the followers of Satan. It is not permissible to interpret the meanings of the Book of God in a way other than what is most commonly understood from the apparent meaning of the discourse in the speech of the Arabs. We have a way to interpret that in the most common sense of the speech of the Arabs, so we direct it to the meaning that was directed to it by those who said: The meaning of that is: You would all follow Satan. Then he claimed that his saying: Except a few is evidence of encompassing everyone. This is despite it being outside the interpretation of the people of interpretation. Likewise, there is no reason to direct that to an exception from his statement: For the knowledge of those among them who deduce it, because if the knowledge of that is returned to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, explains it to those in authority among them after it is clear to them, then everyone who deduces its reality is equal in his knowledge of that, so there is no reason to exclude some of those among them who deduce it, and to single out some of them with his knowledge, while all of them are equal in his knowledge. Since there is no statement on this except what we have said, and these three statements include what we have explained of the defect, it is clear that the correct statement on this is the fourth, which is the statement that we have decided is correct in terms of the exception from broadcasting.
4:84: Abu Ja`far said: What He meant by His Most High’s words: “So fight in the cause of God. You are not charged with anything except yourself,” is that you strive, O Muhammad, against the enemies of God among the polytheists, in the cause of God, meaning: in His religion that He has prescribed for you, which is Islam, and fight them in it with yourself. As for his saying: You are only charged with yourself, it means: God does not charge you with what He has imposed upon you in terms of jihad against His enemy and your enemy, except what He has charged you with, not what others have charged you with. That is, you are only subject to what you have acquired, not what others have acquired, and you are only subject to what you have been charged with, not what others have been charged with. Then he said to him: And urge the believers, meaning: and urge them to fight those whom you have ordered to fight with you, perhaps God will restrain the violence of those who disbelieve, meaning: perhaps God will restrain the fighting of those who disbelieve in God and deny His oneness and reject your message, from you and from them, and their harm. We have previously explained that may from God is obligatory, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And God is more severe in punishment and more severe in retaliation, meaning: God is more severe in punishment of His enemy than the disbelievers in Him, than they are in you, O Muhammad, and your companions, so do not refrain from fighting them, for I am watching them with punishment, retaliation, retaliation, and chastisement, to weaken their plot, weaken their strength, and make the truth prevail over them. And the word tankil is derived from the saying: I punished so-and-so, so I punish him with tankil, if I inflicted pain on him, as in: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: and more severe punishment, meaning punishment.
4:85: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it, is whoever, O Muhammad, intercedes for the sake of your companions, so he intercedes for them in the struggle against their enemy and fighting them in the way of God, which is the good intercession, will have a share of it, meaning: he will have from that intercession a share - which is a portion - of God’s reward and abundant honor, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession, meaning: whoever intercedes for the sake of the unbelievers in God against the believers in Him, so he fights them with them, which is the evil intercession, will have a share of it. Meaning: By the guarantor, the share and portion of the burden and sin. It is taken from the guarantor of the camel and the mount, which is the cloak or the thing that is prepared for it, similar to the saddle on the animal. It is said from it: So-and-so came mount-bound, if he came on a mount that had been prepared for him - as we have explained - for him to ride. It has been said that what he meant by his saying: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it verse is the intercession of people for one another. It is not surprising that the verse was revealed in the context we mentioned, and then it included every intercessor, whether good or bad. We chose what we said about that because it is in the context of the verse in which God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to urge the believers to fight. This was a promise to whoever responded to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a threat to whoever refused to respond to him. This is more similar to the urging of people to intercede for one another, which was not mentioned before, nor will it be mentioned after. It was mentioned that he said: This is about people interceding for one another: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it, but whoever intercedes with an evil intercession, he said: The intercession of some people for others. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have two rewards for it, and because God says: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it, and He did not say intercede. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession, its reward will be written for him as long as its benefit continues. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd was asked about the statement of God: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share in it, he said: The righteous intercession in which he intercedes and acts upon it, is between you and him, they are partners in it, And whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will have a share in it, he said: They are partners in it, just as its people were partners. It was mentioned that: The guarantee is the share. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it, meaning a portion of it, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will have a share of it, and the share is the sin. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: He will have a share of it. As for the share, it is the portion. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: He will have a share of it. He said: A share of it, and that is a bad share. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: The guarantee and the share are one. And he recited: He will give you a double portion of His mercy (al-Hadid 57:8). Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: And God is ever watchful over all things. Some of them said: Its interpretation is: And God is a Guardian and Witness over all things. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And God is ever Watchful over all things, meaning: Guardian. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Muqytaan, meaning a martyr. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man named Mujahid, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Muqitan, he said: a witness, a reckoner, a guardian. Ahmad bin Othman bin Hakim told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Sharik told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid Abu al-Hajjaj: And God is over all things a Guardian, he said: The Guardian is the Reckoner. Others said: The meaning of this is: the one who is in charge of everything through management. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abdullah bin Katheer said: And God is a Sustainer of all things, he said: The Sustainer is the One who sustains. Others said: He is the Almighty. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And God is over all things a Guardian. As for the Guardian, He is the All-Powerful. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And God is over all things a Guardian, he said: He is over all things powerful, the Guardian is the Powerful. Abu Ja`far said: The correct one of these sayings is the one who said: The meaning of Al-Muqit is Al-Qadir. This is because, as is mentioned, this is also in the language of Quraysh. And it is recited by Al-Zubayr ibn `Abd Al-Muttalib, the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And I held a grudge against him and was hateful of his wrongdoing. Meaning: Able. It has been said that this is derived from the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is enough of a sin for a man to waste those he provides for. In the narration of the one who narrated it, he is fed, meaning: whoever is under his hand and in his authority from his family and children, so he estimates his sustenance. It is said from him: So-and-so fed the thing, he feeds him, he feeds him, he feeds him, and sustenance is the noun. As for the one fed in the house of the Jew, he says about it: I wonder what would happen if they brought it out and invited me! Is it for me or against me if I am held accountable? I am hated for my actions. Its meaning is: I am held accountable, but it has a different meaning.
4:86: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: And when you are greeted with a greeting, if you are prayed for a long life, survival, and safety, then greet with one better than it, or return it, meaning: then pray for the one who prayed for you with something better than what he prayed for you, or return it, meaning: or return the greeting. Then the people of interpretation differed about the description of the greeting that is better than what the one who is greeted is greeted with, and what is like it. Some of them said: What is better than it is that the one being greeted should say when it is said: Peace be upon you, and upon you be peace and the mercy of God, and he should add to the supplication of the one who supplicated for him. And the response is that he should say: Peace be upon you, like it, as it was said to him, or by saying: And upon you be peace, so he supplicates for the one who supplicated for him as he supplicated for him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or return it equally, meaning: If someone greets you, you say: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God, or break off to “Peace be upon you,” as he said to you. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it or at least return it equally, he said: Regarding the people of Islam. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, in what was read to him, on the authority of Ata’, he said: Among the people of Islam. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Shureih, that he would respond: “Peace be upon you,” as he would greet him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn and Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he used to reply: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that he used to reply: And upon you. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: So greet the people of Islam with something better than it, or return it to the people of disbelief. Who said that? Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me, he said, Hamid bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saleh, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If anyone of God’s creation greets you, greet him back, even if he is a Zoroastrian, because God says: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or at least return it equally. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Salim bin Nuh told us, he said, Saeed bin Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, for the Muslims, or return it, for the People of the Book. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, for the Muslims, or return it, for the People of the Book. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, he said: Greet in return with one better than it, meaning: to the Muslims, or return it, meaning: to the People of the Book. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it or return it equally, he said: My father said: It is the right of every Muslim who is greeted with a greeting to greet with one better than it, and if a non-Muslim greets him, to return the same to him. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the statement of the one who said: That is in the people of Islam, and the meaning of it is that he returns the greeting of a Muslim if he greets him with a greeting better than his greeting or similar to it. This is because the authentic narrations from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, state that it is obligatory upon every Muslim to return the greeting of every disbeliever with a greeting worse than his. God has commanded that the better and similar be returned in this verse, without distinguishing between the one who is obligated to return the better greeting to him and the one who is returned with the same, by an indication that the correctness of the statement of the one who said: The better return means the Muslim, and the similar return means the disbelievers. The correct view - since there is no evidence in the verse that this is correct, nor is there any evidence from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - is that the choice in this matter is up to the one being greeted: between returning the best greeting or the same, except in the case where a Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has specified something of this, in which case he is a Muslim. The Sunnah has specifically prohibited the disbelievers from returning the best greeting of theirs or the same, except by saying: And upon you, so no one should transgress what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has set in this regard. As for the Muslims, the one who greets them has the choice in returning the best greeting, as God has given him in that. It was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in an interpretation of that in a manner similar to what we have said, a report. And that is what: Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli told me, he said, Abdullah bin al-Sarri al-Antaki told us, he said, Hisham bin Lahiq told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on the authority of Salman al-Farsi, he said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. He said: And upon you be the mercy of God. Then another came and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God, and the mercy of God. The Messenger of God said to him: And upon you be the mercy of God and His blessings. Then another came and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God, and the mercy of God and His blessings. He said to him: And upon you. The man said to him: O Prophet of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, so-and-so and so-and-so came to you and greeted you, and you responded to them more than you responded to me! He said: You did not leave anything for us, God said: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or return it equally, and we responded to you. If someone says: Is it obligatory to return the greeting according to what God has commanded in His Book? It was said: Yes, and this is what a group of the ancients said. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abu al-Zubayr told me: He heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: I never saw him except that he made it obligatory, his saying: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it or return it equally. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Peace is voluntary, and the response is obligatory. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God is watching over everything you do, O people, of deeds, of obedience and disobedience, until He rewards you for it with His reward, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Haseeban, he said: Hafeez. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. The origin of the word hasib in this context, in my opinion, is a noun derived from hisab which means counting. It is said from it: I held someone accountable for such-and-such, and so-and-so held him accountable for such-and-such, and he is his hasib, meaning he is the one who holds him accountable. Some of the linguists from Basra claimed that the meaning of al-Hasib in this context is sufficient. It is said: I think that something is sufficient for me, meaning it is sufficient for me, from their saying: Sufficient for me is such and such. This is a mistake and an error. It is not said in the case of I think that I have something that I think about something and that he is responsible for it. Rather, it is said: He is his responsibility and his accountant. And God says: Indeed, God is ever, over all things, a Reckoner.
4:87: Abu Ja`far said: By His saying, “God, there is no god but He. He will surely gather you together,” He means the worshipped One to whom worship is due, the One to whom all things are to be worshipped and all obedient are to be obeyed. And His statement: He will surely gather you together on the Day of Resurrection, meaning: He will resurrect you after your death, and will gather you all together to the place of reckoning in which people will be rewarded for their deeds, and He will judge between those who obey Him and those who disobey Him, and those who believe in Him and those who disbelieve. There is no doubt about it, meaning: There is no doubt about the truth of what I say to you about that and what I tell you of My report: that I will gather you on the Day of Resurrection after your death. And who is more truthful than God in statement? meaning by that: So know the truth of what I have told you of the report, for I will gather you on the Day of Resurrection for recompense, presentation, accounting, reward, and punishment with certainty, so do not doubt its authenticity or question its truth, for My statement is the truth in which there is no lie, and My promise is the truth that cannot be broken. And who is more truthful than God in statement? meaning: And who is more truthful than God in statement? That is because the liar only lies in order to bring benefit to himself through his lie, or to ward off harm from himself. God, the Most High, is the Creator of harm and benefit, so it is not permissible for Him to lie, because there is no one who calls Him to bring benefit to Himself or ward off harm from Himself. And there is no one who is not called to bring benefit to himself or ward off harm from Himself, except Him, the Most High, so it is permissible for Him to have a counterpart in the impossibility of lying, as He said: And who is more truthful than God in statement and report.
4:88: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement: So what is the matter with you that you are two groups concerning the hypocrites? So what is your concern, O believers, regarding the people of hypocrisy being two different groups, And God has brought them back to what they have earned, meaning by that: And God has returned them to the rulings of the people of polytheism, in permitting the shedding of their blood and the taking of their children as captives. And the reflex is the response, and from it is the saying of Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt: So they will be thrown into the boiling fire. Indeed, they were disobedient and told falsehood and lies. It is said: he made them fall and he made them fall. It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah and Abi it is: And God made them kneel, without an alif. The interpreters differed about those about whom this verse was revealed. Some of them said: It was revealed regarding the disagreement of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud and returned to Medina, and they said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to his companions: If we had known there would be fighting, we would have followed you (Al Imran 3:167). Who said that? Al-Fadl bin Ziyad Al-Wasiti told me, he said, Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, he said: I heard Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Ansari narrating, “On the authority of Zaid bin Thabit: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Uhud, a group of those who were with him returned, and the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were divided into two groups, one group saying: We will kill them, and the other group saying: No. So this verse was revealed: “What is the matter with you that you are two parties concerning the hypocrites? And God has driven them back for what they have earned. Do you wish to be guided?” The verse, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in Medina: It is good, and it removes its impurities as fire removes the impurities of silver.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Usama told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, and he mentioned something similar. Zurayq bin Al-Sakht told me, he said, Shababah told us, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, he said: The hypocrites were mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group said: We will kill them, and a group said: We will not kill them. So God Almighty revealed: Then what is the matter with you that you are two factions concerning the hypocrites? to the end of the verse. Others said: Rather, it was revealed regarding a disagreement that occurred among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a group of people who had come to Medina from Mecca, and had shown the Muslims that they were Muslims, then had returned to Mecca and shown them polytheism. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, he said, Abu Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Then why are you divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites? He said: A people left Mecca until they came to Medina, claiming that they were emigrants, then they apostatized after that, so they asked the Prophet’s permission to go to Mecca to bring their goods to trade with. The believers differed about them, some saying: They are hypocrites, and others saying: They are believers. So God revealed their hypocrisy and ordered that they be fought, so they came with their goods intending to go to Medina, and they were met by Ali ibn Uwaimir, or Hilal ibn Uwaimir al-Aslami, and there was a covenant between him and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was the one who had a firm belief that he should fight the believers or fight his people, so he defended them, because they were following Hilal, and there was a covenant between him and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar to it, except that he said: Then God revealed their hypocrisy and ordered that they be fought, but they did not fight that day, so they came with their merchandise, intending to go to Hilal ibn Uwaimir al-Aslami, and there was a covenant between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: Rather, their disagreement was over a group of polytheists who had declared Islam in Mecca, and who were helping the polytheists against the Muslims. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then why are you divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites? That is because there were people in Mecca who spoke about Islam, and they were supporting the polytheists, so they left Mecca seeking a need of theirs, and they said: If we meet the companions of Muhammad, peace be upon him, then we will not be harmed by them! And when the believers were informed that they had left Mecca, a group of the believers said: Ride to the wicked ones and kill them, for they are supporting your enemy against you! And another group of the believers said: Glory be to God - or something like that - do you kill people who spoke the same as you spoke? Is it because they did not emigrate and leave their homes that their blood and wealth become permissible for that reason? So they were two groups, and the Messenger, peace be upon him, did not forbid either group from anything, so the verse was revealed: Then why are you two groups concerning the hypocrites, while God has driven them back for what they have earned? Do you want to guide one whom God has led astray? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Then why are you divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites? The verse, he mentioned to us that they were two men from Quraysh who were with the polytheists in Mecca, and they had spoken about Islam but had not migrated to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of the companions of the Prophet of God met them while they were on their way to Mecca, and some of them said: Their blood and wealth are lawful! And some of them said: It is not lawful for you! So they argued about them, and God revealed about that: Then why are you divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites while God has driven them back for what they have earned? until he reached: And if God had willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar bin Rashid, he said: It reached me that some people from Mecca wrote to the Prophet, saying that they had converted to Islam, and that was a lie on their part. So they met them, and the Muslims differed about them. One group said: Their blood is permissible! And another group said: Their blood is forbidden! So God revealed: Then why are you divided into two factions concerning the hypocrites, while God has driven them back for what they have earned? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj who said, I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, Then why are you in two groups concerning the hypocrites? They are people who stayed behind from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and stayed in Mecca and declared their faith but did not emigrate. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, differed concerning them. Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supported them, while others disavowed their support and said, “They stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and did not emigrate!” So God called them hypocrites and disavowed the believers from their support, and He commanded them not to support them until they emigrated. Others said: Rather, their disagreement was over a group of people who were in Medina and wanted to leave it out of hypocrisy. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi: Then why are you divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites, while God has made them fall back for what they have earned? He said: Some hypocrites wanted to leave the city, so they said to the believers: We have been afflicted with pain in the city and have become saturated with it, so perhaps we should leave until noon until we recover and then return, for we were people of the wilderness. So they set out, and the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, differed concerning them. A group said: “They are enemies of God, hypocrites! We wish that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given us permission so that we could fight them!” A group said: No, rather they are our brothers who have become saturated with the city, so they have become saturated with it. So they went out until noon to enjoy themselves, and when they recovered, they returned. So God said: Then why are you divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites? He said: Then God has made them fall back for what they have earned. Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed regarding the disagreement of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the matter of the people of slander. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Why then are you divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites while God has made them fall back for what they have earned, until he reached So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the cause of God, he said: This is regarding the matter of Ibn Abi when he spoke about Aisha as he spoke. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: When this verse was revealed: Why then are you divided into two parties concerning the hypocrites? and he recited until he reached So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the cause of God, Sa`d ibn Mu`adh said: Then I declare before God and His Messenger that I am innocent of his party! He means `Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: This verse was revealed regarding the disagreement of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a group of people from Mecca who had apostatized from Islam after their conversion to Islam. We said that this is more correct, because the difference of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding this is based on two opinions: One of them is that they were people from Mecca, according to what we have mentioned in the narration from them. The other: They were people from the city. In the words of God the Most High: So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate, is the clearest evidence that they were not from the people of Medina. This is because emigration was during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his home and city from all the lands of disbelief. As for those who were in Medina in the land of emigration and residing from among the hypocrites and polytheists, then emigration was not obligatory upon them, because in the land of emigration it was their homeland and residence. The Arab scholars differed about the accusative case of his saying: two groups. Some of them said: It is in the accusative case as a state, just as you say: Why are you standing? Meaning: Why are you standing? This is the opinion of some of the Basrans. Some Kufi grammarians said: It is in the accusative case based on the verb Malik. He said: Do not care whether the accusative in Malik is definite or indefinite. He said: It is permissible in speech to say: Malik is the one who is walking with us, because it is like the verb that is in the accusative case with Kan and Ithnaan and the like. He said: And in every place where the verb and yaf’il are suitable from the accusative case, it is permissible to inflect the definite and indefinite from it, just as you inflect Kan and Ithnaan, because they are deficient in meaning, even if you think they are complete. This statement is more correct in this regard, because what is required in the statement of the speaker: Why are you standing? Standing. This is in the doctrine of kana and its sisters, and I think its companions. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of his saying: And God has made them fall back. Some of them said: It means: He returned them, as we said. Who said that? Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And God has sent them back for what they have earned, He has sent them back. Others said: The meaning of this is: God made them fall. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told me, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And God has made them fall for what they have earned, meaning: He has made them fall. Others said: The meaning of this is: He led them astray and destroyed them. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And God has destroyed them, he said: He has destroyed them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And God destroyed them for what they earned, He destroyed them for what they did. Muhammad bin Al-Muhsin told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And God destroyed them for what they earned, He destroyed them. We have already explained the meaning of this before, so there is no need to repeat it. Abu Ja`far said: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying, Do you want to guide one whom God has led astray? Do you want, O believers, to be guided to Islam and be guided to acknowledge it and enter into it, one whom God has led astray from it - meaning by that: one whom God has let down from it - and has not guided him to acknowledge it? Rather, this is a speech from God, the Most High, to the group that defended these hypocrites whose characteristics God described in this verse. He, the Most High, says to them: Do you seek to guide those whom God has led astray and let them down from the truth and following Islam, by defending against fighting those believers who want to fight them? And he whom God leaves astray - you will never find for him a way, meaning: And he whom He has let down from his religion and following what He has commanded him to do, from acknowledging Him and His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what He brought from Him, and He has led him astray from it, you will never find for him, O Muhammad, a way, meaning: You will never find for him a path that will guide him to attain what God has let him down from, nor a method by which he can reach the matter that He has forbidden him to reach.
4:89: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved, is that these hypocrites, among whom you, O believers, are divided into two groups, wished that you would disbelieve and deny the Oneness of your Lord and the belief in your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as they disbelieved, meaning: as they denied that, so that you would be equal, meaning: so that you would be disbelievers like them, and you and they would be equal in associating partners with God, so do not take from them allies until they emigrate in the cause of God, meaning: until they leave the abode of polytheism and leave its people who are polytheists with God, to the abode of Islam and its people, in the cause of God, meaning: in seeking the religion of God, which is His path, so that they would then become like you, and they would then have your ruling, as: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “They wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be equal. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate,” he said: until they do as you did, meaning emigrating for the sake of God. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: If these hypocrites turn away from acknowledging God and His Messenger, and turn away from emigrating from the land of polytheism to the land of Islam, and from disbelief to Islam, seize them, O believers, and kill them wherever you find them, in their lands or elsewhere, wherever you find them on God’s land, and do not take from them a friend, meaning: Do not take from them a friend who will be your friend in your affairs, nor a supporter who will aid you against your enemies, for they are disbelievers who will not spare you, and they wish you would suffer. This report from God, may He be glorified, is a clarification of the truth of the hypocrisy of those about whom the believers differed, and a warning to those who defended them against defending them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: But if they turn away, seize them and kill them. If they turn away from migration, seize them and kill them. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: But if they turn away, seize them and kill them wherever you find them, meaning: If they show their disbelief, then kill them wherever you find them.
4:90: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Except those who reach a people between you and whom there is a treaty, is that if these hypocrites, over whom you differed, turn away from faith in God and His Messenger, and refuse to emigrate and do not emigrate in the way of God, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, except for those of them who reach a people between you and whom there is a truce, a covenant, and a treaty, and they enter among them, and become one of them, and are satisfied with their judgment. For whoever reaches them and enters among them from the people of polytheism, satisfied with their judgment in sparing their blood by his entering among them: that their women and children are not taken captive, and their wealth is not taken as booty, just as: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: Except for those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty, meaning: If they openly declare their disbelief, then kill them wherever you find them. If one of them enters a people between you and whom there is a treaty, then treat him as you treat the People of the Covenant. Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Except those who reach out to a people between you and whom there is a treaty, they reach out to those people between you and whom there is a treaty, and they have the same security as these people. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Except for those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty, he said: It was revealed about Hilal bin Uwaimir Al-Aslami, Saraqa bin Malik bin Ja’sham, and Khuzaymah bin Amir bin Abd Manaf. Some Arabists have claimed that the meaning of his statement, except those who are connected to a people, is except those who are connected in their lineage to a people between whom and you there is a covenant, from their saying, the man connected, meaning: he belonged and was related, as Al-A’sha said in describing a woman who was related to a people: If she called, she would say: Abkar bin Wael! And Bakr cursed her, and the noses were downcast! He means by his saying: I called, I joined. Abu Ja`far said: There is no basis for this interpretation in this context, because if affiliation with a people of truce or covenant would have given those who ascribe to them what they have, if they did not have the covenant and security that they have, then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) would not have fought the Quraysh, even though they were relatives of the first predecessors. And the people of faith have more right by virtue of their faith than the people of a covenant have by virtue of their covenant. And in the Messenger of God’s (may God bless him and grant him peace) fighting the polytheists of the Quraysh, by their not entering into what the people of faith among them entered into, despite their close lineage to the lineage of the believers among them - there is clear evidence that the affiliation of one who has no covenant to one of them who has a covenant does not give him the covenant that the one of them who has a covenant has by virtue of his affiliation. If a ignorant person thinks that the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fighting against those who fought from the relatives of the believers from the polytheists of Quraysh only happened after his statement was abrogated: Except those who join forces with a people between you and whom there is a treaty, then the people of interpretation have agreed that the abrogator of that was Bara’ah, and Bara’ah was revealed after the conquest of Mecca and the entry of Quraysh into Islam. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement: Or they come to you with their hearts restrained from fighting you or fighting their people, “But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them” - Except those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty - or: except those who come to you with their hearts restrained from fighting you or fighting their people, so they enter among you. What he means by his saying: Their chests are constricted is that their chests are too narrow to fight you or to fight their people. The Arabs say to anyone who is unable to do or say something: he has been restricted, and from this comes the restriction in reading. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: Or they came to you with their chests constricted, meaning: they returned and entered among you, with their chests constricted, meaning: their chests became narrow, that they should fight you or fight their people. In his saying: Or they came to you, their hearts constrained from fighting you or fighting their people, it is omitted. It was omitted because the speech indicates it. That is because its meaning is: Or they came to you, their hearts constrained, so the mention of qad was omitted because it is the custom of the Arabs to do something like that. You say: So-and-so came to me, his mind gone, meaning: his mind has gone. And it is heard from them: I began to look at the one with the skirts, meaning: I looked. And because of the omission of qad with the past tense, it is permissible to put the past tense of verbs in the place of the state, because when qad is added to it, it brings it closer to the state, and resembles nouns. And according to this reading, I mean I confined it, it is the reading of the reading in all countries, and it is read according to the consensus of the argument on it. It was mentioned about Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read it: Or they came to you with their hearts grieved, in the accusative case. It is correct and eloquent in Arabic, but I do not accept reading it with it, because it is anomalous and deviates from the reading of the reading of Islam. Abu Ja`far said: He, the Most High, means: And if God had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. And if God had willed, He would have given power over these people - those who come to a people with whom you have a treaty, and enter into their protection and covenant, and those who come to you with their hearts restrained from fighting you and fighting their people - over you, O believers, so they fought you along with your enemies from the polytheists, but God, the Most High, mentioned Him, restrained them from you. God, the Most High, says: So obey the One Who has bestowed favor upon you by restraining them from you along with all the other favors He has bestowed upon you, in what He has commanded you to restrain from them if they come to a people with whom you have a treaty, or they come to you with their hearts restrained from fighting you and fighting their people. Then He, the Most High, said: If they withdraw from you, meaning: If these hypocrites whom I ordered you to refrain from fighting withdraw from you, by entering into your covenant with them, or by coming to you, their hearts will be closed from fighting you and fighting their people, “and they do not fight you and offer you peace,” meaning: and make peace with you. And "peace" means surrender, and this is an example, as when a man says to another man: I gave you my reins, and I threw my bridle to you, if he surrenders to him and obeys his command. So it is the same. His statement: "And they threw you peace" means: They threw their reins to you and surrendered to you, as a peace and reconciliation from them to you. And from "peace" is the saying of Al-Tirmaah: That is because Tamim left every horse and every fur moth in peace for the lion. He means by his saying: Peace, submission. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`: “If they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace,” he said: peace. As for his statement: God has not made for you a way against them, he is saying: If these hypocrites whose description he described surrender to you, as a peace treaty from them to you, God has not made for you a way against them, meaning: God has not made for you a way against themselves, their wealth, their children, and their women, to kill, take captive, or take booty, by permitting that to you or by giving permission, so do not expose yourself to them in that, except for a way that is good. Then God abrogated all the rulings of this verse and the one after it by saying, may He be exalted: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them until His saying: “Then let them go on their way. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful” (al-Tawbah 9:5). He mentioned the same thing that we said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan, they said, he said: “But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. And do not take from among them any friend or helper, except those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty” to His saying: And those We have given you over them a clear authority. And He said in al-Mumtahanah 60:“God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.” And He said in it: God only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes to For those are the wrongdoers (al-Mumtahanah 60:8-9). So He abrogated these four verses concerning the polytheists, saying: “A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. So travel freely through the land for four months and know that you cannot cause failure to God and that God will disgrace the disbelievers” (al-Tawbah 9:1-2). So He made four months for them to travel through the land, and nullified what came before that. And He said in the next verse: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. Then He abrogated and made an exception, saying: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah until His saying: Then escort him to a place of safety (al-Tawbah 9:5-6). Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: But if they withdraw from you, he said: It was abrogated by: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammam bin Yahya told us, he said, I heard Qatada say regarding His statement: Except those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty until His statement: Then God has not given you a way against them, then He abrogated that later in Bara’ah, and He commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight the polytheists with His statement: So kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush (al-Tawbah 9:5). Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Except those who join a people between you and whom there is a treaty, the verse, he said: All of this was abrogated altogether, it was abrogated by jihad, a period of four months was set for them: either they submit, or there is jihad.
4:91: Abu Ja'far said: These are another group of hypocrites, who used to pretend to be Muslims to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and his companions so that they would be safe from being killed, taken captive, and having their money taken, while they were disbelievers. Their people knew that about them. Whenever they met them, they would be with them and worship what they worshipped instead of God, so that they would be safe from them regarding their lives, their money, their women, and their children. God says, Every time they were returned to trial, they relapsed into it, meaning: Every time their people called them to associate partners with God, they apostatized and became polytheists like them. The interpreters differed about who was meant by this verse. Some of them said: They were people from Mecca who converted to Islam - as God described them in terms of taqiyya - while they were disbelievers, so that they would feel safe for themselves, their money, their children and their women. God says: Every time they were returned to temptation, they relapsed into it, meaning every time their people called them to associate partners with God, they apostatized and became polytheists like them, so that they would feel safe with these and those. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They want to make you feel safe and their people feel safe. He said: People used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and convert to Islam out of hypocrisy, then return to Quraysh and indulge in idolatry, seeking thereby to feel safe here and there. So he ordered that they be fought if they did not withdraw and reform. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: “You will find others who desire to be secure from you and secure their people. Every time they are returned to a trial, they fall back into it.” He said: Every time they wanted to emerge from a trial, they fell back into it. That is because a man would be found who had spoken about Islam, so he would bring a stick, a stone, a scorpion, or a beetle, and the polytheists would say to that one who had spoken about Islam: Say, ‘This is my Lord,’ to the beetle and the scorpion. Others said: Rather, they are a group of polytheists who sought safety from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they would feel safe with him, his companions, and the polytheists. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: You will find others who want to be safe from you and their people, he said: They were a tribe in Tihamah, they said: O Prophet of God, we will not fight you nor will we fight our people, and they wanted to be safe from the Prophet of God and their people, but God refused that to them, so He said: Every time they are returned to trial, they are thrown into it, he said: Every time a calamity befell them, they perished in it. Others said: This verse was revealed about Naim bin Masoud Al-Ashja’i. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: Then he mentioned Na’im ibn Mas’ud al-Ashja’i, who was safe among the Muslims and the polytheists, and he transmitted the conversation between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists, and he said: You will find others who want to be safe from you and their people, whenever they are returned to the trial, meaning: to polytheism. As for the interpretation of his saying: Whenever they are returned to the trial, they fall into it, it is as follows: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, regarding his statement: Every time they are returned to trial, they are plunged into it, he said: Every time they are afflicted with it, they are blinded by it. Bishr bin Mu`adh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada: Every time a trial befell them, they perished in it. The statement on this is what I have explained before, which is that fitna in the speech of the Arabs means a test, and irkas means a return. The interpretation of the statement: Whenever they were returned to the test to return to disbelief and polytheism, they returned to it. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: If those who want to give you security and give security to their people, and whenever they are called to polytheism, they respond to it, “and offer you peace,” and do not surrender to you, giving you the reins and making peace with you, do not withdraw from you, O believers, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`: “If they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace,” he said: Peace. And they restrain their hands, meaning: and they restrain their hands from fighting you, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, meaning: If they do not do so, then seize them wherever you find them on earth and encounter them, and kill them, for their blood will then be lawful for you.
