And those We have given you a clear authority over, meaning: And those who want to be secure from you and their people while they are still in disbelief, and do not withdraw from you and offer you peace and restrain their hands, We have given you a clear argument to kill them wherever you find them, by their remaining in their disbelief and their abandoning the migration from the land of polytheism, clear, meaning: that it shows that they deserve that from you, and that you have attained the right to kill them. This is the saying: a clear authority, and the authority is the proof, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Of what was in the Qur’an of authority, it is: proof. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: a clear authority. As for the clear authority, it is the proof.
4:92: Abu Ja`far said: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His statement: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, is that God did not give permission to a believer nor did He permit him to kill a believer. He says: That was not for him in what his Lord made for him and permitted him to do of things at all, such as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, meaning: He did not have that right in what he was given by his Lord, from the covenant of God that He entrusted to him. As for his saying: Except by mistake, he is saying: Except that a believer may kill a believer by mistake, and he has no right to what his Lord has given him and permitted him to do. This is from the exception that the Arabs call the discontinuous exception, as Jarir ibn Atiyah said: From the eggs, she did not travel far, and she did not step on the ground except a thread of cold, passing wind. Meaning: You did not step on the ground except by stepping on the tail of the hail, and the tail of the hail is not from the ground. Then, the Most High, informed His servants of the ruling on the one who kills a believer by mistake, saying: And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave, meaning: he must free him, a believing slave, from his wealth, and a blood money to be paid by his family, to be paid by his clan, to his family unless they give up, meaning: unless the family of the one killed by mistake gives up the blood money to the one who is obligated to pay it to them, so they pardon him and overlook his sin, and it is dropped from him. The position of that in his statement: unless they believe, is in the accusative case, because its meaning is: then he must do that, unless they believe. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah Al-Makhzumi, who had killed a Muslim man after he had converted to Islam, and he did not know that he had converted to Islam. The effects of this are mentioned: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, he said: Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah killed a believing man who was torturing him with Abu Jahl - who was his brother on his mother’s side - so he followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, thinking that the man was as he was. Ayyash had migrated to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a believer. Abu Jahl, his brother on his mother’s side, came to him and said: Your mother is asking you to return to her - and she is Asma bint Mukhriba - so he came with him, and Abu Jahl tied him up until he arrived in Mecca. When the infidels saw him, it increased their disbelief and temptation, and they said: Abu Jahl can do whatever he wants to Muhammad and seize his companions. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly, except that he said in his hadith: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed that man, and Ayyash thought he was an unbeliever as he was. Ayyash had migrated to Madinah as a believer, then Abu Jahl - who was his brother from his mother - came to him and said: Your mother asks you by her kinship and her right to return to her. He also said: And he takes his companions and ties them up. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Al-Harith bin Yazid bin Anisa - from Banu Amir bin Luay - was torturing Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah with Abu Jahl. Then Al-Harith bin Yazid went out migrating to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ayyash met him in Al-Harrah, so he struck him with the sword until he was silent, and he thought he was an unbeliever. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, and the verse was revealed: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, and he recited it to him, then he said to him: Get up and set him free. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, he said: It was revealed about Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah al-Makhzumi, who was a brother of Abu Jahl ibn Hisham on his mother’s side. He had embraced Islam and emigrated with the first emigrants before the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Jahl and al-Harith ibn Hisham sought him out, and with them was a man from Banu Amir ibn Lu’ay. They brought him to Madinah, and Ayyash was the most beloved of his brothers to his mother. They spoke to him and said: Your mother has sworn that no house will shade her until she sees you lying down in the sun. Go to her so that she may look at you, then return, and give him a pledge from God that they will not agitate him until he returns to Madinah. So one of his companions gave him a fine camel of his and said: If you fear anything from them, then sit on the fine camel. So when they took him out of Madinah, they took him and bound him, and the Amiri flogged him, so he swore to kill the Amiri. He remained imprisoned in Mecca until he came out on the day of the conquest. Al-Amiri met him and he had converted to Islam, but Ayyash did not know that he had converted to Islam. He struck him and killed him. Then God revealed: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, meaning that he did not know that he was a believer. And whoever kills a believer by mistake - then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation payment to be made to the deceased’s family unless they give up, in which case they would not pay the blood money. Others said: This verse was revealed about Abu Darda. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about the words of God: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, the verse, he said: This was revealed about a man killed by Abu Darda’, all of this was revealed about him. They were on a military expedition, and Abu Darda’ went to a valley to need something, and he found a man from the people with his sheep, so he charged him with his sword and said: There is no god but God! He said: So he struck him, then he came with his sheep to the people. Then he felt something in himself, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Why did you not split open his heart? He said: What do you think I find? Is it, O Messenger of God, anything but blood or water? He said: He told you with his tongue and you did not believe him? He said: What about me, O Messenger of God? He said: What about There is no god but God? He said: What about me, O Messenger of God? He said: What about There is no god but God? I even wished that this was an Islamic beginning. He said: And the Qur’an was revealed: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, until it reached unless they believe, he said: Unless they fabricate it. Abu Ja`far said: The correct thing to say about this is that God informed His servants with this verse of the expiation and blood money that is due to whoever kills a believer by mistake. It is possible that the verse was revealed about `Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi`ah and his victim, or about Abu al-Darda` and his companion. Whichever of these was the case, what God meant by the verse was informing His servants of what we have mentioned, and those of His servants who have reason to believe in its revelation have known this, and their ignorance of the person about whom it was revealed does not harm them. As for the believing neck, scholars differ regarding its description. Some of them said: The slave is not considered a believer until he has chosen faith after reaching puberty, prayed and fasted, and the child does not deserve this description. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, he said: I asked Al-Sha’bi about his saying: Then the freeing of a believing slave, he said: She prayed and knew faith. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Then the freeing of a believing slave, meaning a believing woman, who has attained the faith, fasted, and prayed. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki` told us, on the authority of Al-A`mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Whatever is mentioned in the Qur’an as a believing slave, then it is not sufficient except for the one who fasts and prays. And whatever is mentioned in the Qur’an as a slave who is not a believer, then a boy is sufficient. It was narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Everything in the Book of God: Then the freeing of a believing slave, is the one who fasts, prays, and pays his mind. And if he says: Then the freeing of a slave, then whatever he wants. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Al-Thawri informed us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Everything in the Qur’an: Then the freeing of a believing slave, is the one who has prayed. And as for the one who is not a believer, then the freeing of the one who has not prayed. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then the freeing of a believing slave, and the believing slave according to Qatada is the one who has prayed. And he disliked freeing this child who had not prayed and had not reached that age. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: Then the freeing of a believing slave, he said: If he understands his religion. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Then the freeing of a believing slave, a boy is not sufficient for that. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then the freeing of a believing slave, meaning by a believing slave: someone who has understood the faith, fasted, and prayed. If he cannot find a slave, then he must fast for two consecutive months, and he must pay blood money to his family unless they give it to him in charity. Others said: If he was born to Muslim parents, then he is a believer, even if he is a child. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, who said: Every slave born in Islam is sufficient. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the statement of the one who said: It is not permissible to kill a slave by mistake except for one who has believed and is sane of faith, from among the adult men and women, if he is one of those whose parents are of a religion other than Islam, and he was born to them while they were also, then neither of them converted to Islam until he was freed as an expiation for a mistake. As for the one who was born to Muslim parents, all of the people of knowledge have agreed that even if he has not reached the age of choice and discernment, and has not reached puberty, he is governed by the ruling of the people of faith in inheritance, and praying over him if he dies, and as is obligatory upon him if he commits a crime, and is obligatory upon him if a crime is committed against him, and in marriage. So since this was unanimously agreed upon by all of them, then it is obligatory for him to have the ruling, in what is permissible as an expiation for a mistake if he is freed in it, from the ruling of the people of faith, in what is permissible for him... in all the meanings that we have mentioned and others. And whoever rejects this, the matter is reversed to him in this regard, and then he is asked about the difference between that from the origin or analogy. So he will not say a statement in any of that except that he is obligated in something else like it. As for the blood money paid to the family of the murdered person, it is paid to them according to what is due to them, in full and without diminishing the rights of its people. It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to say: It is the one who provides. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement: A blood money paid to his family, he said: Ample. As for his saying: unless they give charity, he means by it: unless they give charity as blood money to the killer, or to his family, so the ta’ in his saying: they give charity was assimilated into the sad, so they became sad. It was mentioned that this is in Abi’s reading, unless they give charity. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bakr bin Al-Sharud told us in the letter of Abi: Unless they are truthful. Abu Ja`far said: What God Almighty means by His statement: But if he is from a people who are enemies to you and he is a believer, is that if this person who was killed by a believer by mistake was from a people who are enemies to you in religion, polytheists who have waged war against you because of your disagreement with Islam, and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave, meaning that if a Muslim kills by mistake a man from among the polytheists, and the person killed is a believer, and the killer thinks that he is a disbeliever, then he must free a believing slave. The interpreters differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said: Its meaning is: If the one killed was from a people who are your enemies and he was a believer - that is, he was among them and did not emigrate - and a believer killed him, then there is no blood money on him, but he must free a believing slave. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: But if he is from a people hostile to you while he is a believer, he said: He is the man who converts to Islam in a land of war and is killed. He said: There is no blood money for it, but there is expiation for it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: But if he was from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, he said: meaning the one killed is a believer and his people are disbelievers. He said: Then there is no blood money for him, but the freeing of a believing slave. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, he said: The man is a believer and his people are infidels, so there is no blood money for him, but the freeing of a believing slave. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer in the land of disbelief, he says: Then the freeing of a believing slave, and he is not entitled to blood money. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave, and there is no blood money for his family, because they are infidels, and there is no covenant or protection between them and God. Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hajjaj told us: Hammad told us: Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said regarding the statement of God: But if he is from a people hostile to you while he is a believer to the end of the verse: A man would convert to Islam and then come to his people and stay among them while they were polytheists, and the army of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass by them and he would be killed among those who were killed, and his killer would free a slave, but he would not be entitled to blood money. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Munira, on the authority of Ibrahim: But if he is from a people who are your enemies and he is a believer, then the freeing of a slave. He said: This is if the Muslim man is from a people who are your enemies, meaning: he has no covenant with them, and he is killed by mistake, then the one who kills him must free a believing slave. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: But if he was from a people who are enemies to you and he is a believer, if he was among the people of war and he was a believer, and he killed him by mistake, then his killer must atone by freeing a believing slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, and there is no blood money on him. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: But if he was from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, the one killed was a Muslim and his people were infidels, so he should free a believing slave, and he should not pay them the blood money so that they would gain strength against you. Others said: Rather, it means a man from the people of war who goes to the land of Islam and converts to Islam, then returns to the land of war. When the army of the people of Islam passes by them, his people flee, and that Muslim among them stays there, and the Muslims kill him, thinking him an infidel. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave, he is a believer who is among the enemy from the polytheists, and they hear about the secret mission from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they flee and the believer stands firm and is killed, so in that is the freeing of a believing slave. Abu Ja`far said: What God Almighty means by His statement: And if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, because the one killed by mistake was from a people between you, O believers, and between whom there is a treaty, meaning a covenant and a pledge, and they are not people of war with you, a ransom paid to his family, meaning: then his killer must pay a blood money paid to his family, to be borne by his clan, and the freeing of a believing slave, as expiation for killing him. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of this murdered man who was from a people between whom and us there is a covenant. Was he a believer or an unbeliever? Some of them said: He is an infidel, but his killer must pay his blood money, because he and his people have a covenant, so it is obligatory to pay his blood money to his people because of the covenant between them and the believers, and it is money from their money, and it is not permissible for the believers to take anything from their money without their consent. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, meaning: If he is an unbeliever under your protection and he is killed, then his killer must pay blood money in advance to his family, and free a believing slave, or fast for two consecutive months. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said, I heard Al-Zuhri say: The blood money of a dhimmi is the same as the blood money of a Muslim. He said, and he used to interpret: And if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, then the blood money is to be paid to his family. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of Isa bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, then a ransom shall be paid to his family, he said: From the people of the treaty, but he is not a believer. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, and he is not a believer. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, then a ransom must be paid to his family and a believing slave must be freed, by killing him, meaning: by what he killed from among the people of his covenant and protection, But whoever cannot find [any means], then a fast of two consecutive months as repentance from God, the verse. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, then a ransom shall be paid to his family, he said: Then pay them the blood money based on the treaty. He said: The People of the Covenant are included in this, “and the freeing of a believing slave. But whoever cannot find one, then a fast of two consecutive months.” Others said: Rather, he is a believer, so his killer must pay blood money to his polytheist people, because they are people of the covenant. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told me, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, then a ransom is to be paid to his family and a believing slave is to be freed. He said: This is a Muslim man and his people are polytheists with whom they have a treaty, so his blood money is for his people, and his inheritance is for the Muslims, and his people pay blood money for him, and they have his blood money. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Kufi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, regarding his statement: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, he said: And he is a believer. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, he said: All of them are believers. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two opinions in interpreting the verse is the opinion of those who said: This refers to the one killed from among the people of the covenant. Because God made this ambiguous when He said: And if he is from a people between you and them, and He did not say: and he is a believer, as He said about the one killed from among the believers and the people of war, and He meant the one killed from among them who is a believer. So in leaving out the description of him with the faith with which He described the two killed people mentioned earlier, there is clear evidence of the correctness of what we said about that. If someone thinks that in the words of God the Most High: A ransom paid to his family, there is evidence that he is from among the people of faith, because according to Him, blood money is only for a believer, then he has thought wrong. This is because the blood money of the dhimmi and the people of Islam is the same, because they all agree that the blood money of their unbelieving slaves and the slaves of the believers from among the people of faith are the same. Likewise, the ruling on the blood money of their free people is the same, although if their blood money were as those who disagreed with us said, making it half of the blood money of the people of faith or a third, this would not be evidence that what is meant by his statement, And if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, is from the people of faith, because there is no disagreement among all of them - except those who do not consider disagreement - that the blood money of a believing woman is half of the blood money of a believer, and that does not exclude it from being blood money. Likewise, the ruling on the blood money of the People of the Covenant, if it were less than the blood money of the people of faith, this would not exclude it from being blood money. So how is it that the matter is different in this regard, and their blood money and the blood money of the believers are the same? As for the covenant, it is the pledge and the covenant. We have explained in other places that this is the case, and the origin from which it was taken, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, he said: a covenant. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding his statement: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, he said: It is a treaty. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And if he is from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, a covenant. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, similarly. If someone says: What is the nature of the mistake, if a believer or a person with a covenant is killed, he is obligated to pay blood money and expiation? It was said: It is what Al-Nakha’i said about that, and that is what: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: A mistake is when one wants something and gets something else. Abu Kuraib and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, they said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: A mistake is when someone throws something and it hits a person without intending it, so it is a mistake and it is the responsibility of the family. If he said: What is the blood money required for that? It was said: As for killing a believer, one hundred camels are due, if he is a camel owner, on the blood money of his killer. There is no disagreement among everyone about that, although there is a difference of opinion among scholars about the amount of its teeth. Some of them say: They are quarters: twenty-five of them are one-year-old camels, twenty-five are two-year-old camels, twenty-five are two-year-old camels, and twenty-five are two-year-old camels. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding semi-intentional error: thirty-three one-year-old camels, thirty-three two-year-old camels, and thirty-four two-year-old camels, up to the age of one year. Regarding error: twenty-five one-year-old camels, twenty-five two... and twenty-five two-year-old camels. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Firas and al-Shaibani, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Damrah, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, something similar. Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Suwar, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said regarding accidental killing: The blood money is one hundred quarters, then he mentioned something similar. Others said: They are fifths: twenty one-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, and twenty two-year-old camels. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: For a mistake, there are twenty one-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, and twenty two-year-old camels, and twenty two-year-old camels. Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, regarding accidental killing: One hundred camels are divided into fifths: five young camels, five young camels, five two-year-old camels, five two-year-old camels, and five two-year-old camels. Mujahid bin Musa told us, Yazid told us, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The blood money is divided into fifths: the blood money for accidental death: five young female camels, five two-year-old female camels, five three-year-old female camels, five two-year-old female camels, and five two-year-old male camels. The authors of this article based their argument on the hadith: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i narrated to us, saying: Yahya bin Abi Zaydah and Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar narrated to us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Zayd bin Jubayr, on the authority of Al-Khashf bin Malik, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the blood money for an accidental killing is divided into fifths. Abu Hisham said: Ibn Abi Zaydah said: Twenty one-year-old camels, twenty two... and twenty two-year-old camels. Abu Hisham told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah: that he ruled thus. Others said: They are quarters, but they are thirty one-year-old camels, thirty two-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, and twenty two-year-old male camels. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told me, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abd Rabbih, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Uthman and Zaid ibn Thabit, they said: In the case of a semi-intentional mistake: forty two-year-old camels, thirty three-year-old camels, and thirty two-year-old camels. In the case of a mistake: thirty three-year-old camels, thirty three-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, and twenty two-year-old male camels. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit: Concerning the blood money for an accident: thirty one-year-old camels, thirty two-year-old female camels, twenty two-year-old female camels, and twenty two-year-old male camels. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Uthma told us, he said, Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abd Rabbih, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him. He said, and Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, similarly. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement on this matter is that everyone agrees that in the case of a pure mistake on the part of the camel owners: one hundred camels. Then they differed about the amounts of her teeth, and they agreed that he should not fall short of the minimum of the teeth we mentioned of those we mentioned whose differences we mentioned, and that he should not exceed the maximum of the maximum of the teeth for whom she was obligated. Since that was a consensus from all of them, it is obligatory that the one who is obligated to pay the blood money for someone killed by mistake, that is, these teeth about which the differing scholars differed, should pay it to the one for whom it was obligatory. Because God Almighty did not set a limit for that which he should not exceed or fall short of, nor did His Messenger, except what I mentioned of their consensus in what they agreed upon, for the imam does not have the right to exceed that in the ruling by shortening or increasing, and he has the choice between that according to what he sees is good for both groups. If the killer's family is from the people of gold, then the heirs of the murdered person are required to pay us a thousand dinars. And the scholars of the countries agree on this. Some of them said: This is a valuation by Omar, may God have mercy on him, of camels for the people of gold in his time. It is obligatory to evaluate their value in every era, if the camels are not available to the killer’s blood money, and they based their argument on what: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Musa, on the authority of Makhul, he said: The blood money used to rise and fall, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and it was eight hundred dinars, so Umar feared after that, so he made it twelve thousand dirhams and one thousand dinars. As for those who have made it obligatory in every era on the people of gold, a thousand dinars in gold, they said: This is an obligation that God has imposed on the names of His Messenger, just as He imposed camels on the people of camels. They said: And in the consensus of the scholars of the countries in every age and time, except for those who deviated from them, that it is not increased over a thousand dinars nor decreased from it, the clearest evidence that it is obligatory on the people of gold is the obligation of camels on the people of camels, because if it were the value of a hundred camels, that would differ with the increase and decrease due to the change in the prices of camels. This statement is correct, because we mentioned the consensus of the argument on it. As for the paper money owed to the people of paper among us, it is twelve thousand dirhams, and we have explained the reasons for that in our book, A Nice Book on the Rulings of Islamic Laws. Others said: The people of the paper are only required to pay ten thousand dirhams of the paper. As for the blood money of a person with whom we have a treaty, between whom and his people there is a covenant, the scholars differed on its amount. Some of them said: His blood money is the same as that of a free Muslim. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Sarri told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Saad, on the authority of Al-Zuhri: That Abu Bakr and Uthman, may God be pleased with them, used to make the blood money of a Jew or a Christian, if they had a treaty, the same as the blood money of a Muslim. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Sarri told us, on the authority of Al-Dastawai, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah: That Ibn Masoud used to make the blood money of the People of the Book, if they were protected by a covenant, like the blood money of the Muslims. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Hammad, who said: Abd al-Hamid asked me about the blood money of the People of the Book, so I told him that Ibrahim said: Their blood money and our blood money are the same. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim and Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, that they both said: The blood money for a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian is like the blood money for a free Muslim. Ya’qub Ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: It was said: The blood money for a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian is like the blood money for a Muslim, if he has a covenant. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’ that they said: The blood money of a protected person is the same as the blood money of a Muslim. Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, al-Masoudi told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said: The blood money for a Muslim and a person under a covenant is the same. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said: I heard Al-Zuhri say: The blood money of a dhimmi is the same as the blood money of a Muslim. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Amer, he said: The blood money of a dhimmi is the same as the blood money of a Muslim. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, similarly. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, similarly. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Amer, and it reached him that Al-Hasan used to say: The blood money for a Zoroastrian is eight hundred, and the blood money for a Jew or Christian is four thousand, so he said: Their blood money is one. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said: The blood money of a protected person and a Muslim are the same in their expiation. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The blood money for a protected person and a Muslim is the same. Others said: Rather, his blood money is half of the blood money of a Muslim. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb regarding the blood money of a Jew and a Christian, he said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, made it half the blood money of a Muslim, and the blood money of a Zoroastrian is eight hundred. So I said to Amr ibn Shu’ayb: Al-Hasan says: Four thousand! He said: That was before the youth. And he said: The blood money of a Zoroastrian was made like that of a slave. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abdullah Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, who said: The blood money of a protected person is half the blood money of a Muslim. Others said: Rather, his blood money is one-third of the blood money of a Muslim. Who said that? Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu Uthman - he said: He was a judge for the people of Marv - he said: Umar, may God be pleased with him, made the blood money for a Jew or a Christian four thousand, four thousand. Ammar bin Khalid Al-Wasiti told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said, Omar said: The blood money for a Christian is four thousand, and for a Zoroastrian is eight hundred. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Samad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Thabit, he said: I heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say: Umar said: The blood money of the People of the Book is four thousand, and the blood money of the Magian is eight hundred. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab: that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-Malih: That a man from his people shot a Jew or a Christian with an arrow and killed him, so that was reported to Umar ibn al-Khattab, so he paid him his blood money, four thousand. And on his authority, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: Omar said: The blood money for a Jew or a Christian is four thousand, four thousand. Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, some of our companions told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Omar, similarly. He said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Umar, similarly. He said: Hisham told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar, that he said: The blood money for a Jew or a Christian is four thousand, and for a Zoroastrian it is eight hundred. Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’, similarly. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak regarding his statement: But whoever cannot find [a slave], then a fast of two consecutive months, fasting is for the one who cannot find a slave, but as for the blood money, it is obligatory and nothing can nullify it. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty meant by His statement: But whoever cannot find one, then a fast of two consecutive months, that whoever cannot find a believing slave to free as expiation for his mistake in killing someone who killed a believer or a covenanted person, because he is unable to pay for her price, then a fast of two consecutive months, meaning that he must fast for two consecutive months. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: But whoever cannot find [a slave] - then a fast of two consecutive months, he said: Whoever cannot find a slave - or a slave, Abu Asim was not sure - in killing a believer by mistake, he said: And it was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah, he killed a believer by mistake. Others said: Fasting for two months for blood money and a slave. They said: The interpretation of the verse is: Whoever does not find a believing slave, nor a beast to hand over to its people, must fast for two consecutive months. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq: that he was asked about the verse in Surat al-Nisa’: But whoever cannot find [the means] - then a fast of two consecutive months: Is fasting the two months for the slave alone, or for the blood money and the slave? He said: Whoever cannot find the means, then it is for the blood money and the slave. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Masruq, something similar. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard is that fasting for a slave is not for blood money, because the blood money for an accident is on the killer’s family, and the expiation is on the killer, according to the consensus of the authorities on this, transmitted from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the fast of a fasting person does not make up for what is due from someone else’s money. And to continue fasting for two months, and not to break it by breaking the fast on some of its days for no reason preventing him from fasting. Then He, the Most High, said: “A repentance from God. And God is Knowing and Wise.” Meaning: God has overlooked you and made it easy for you, by easing for you what He eased for you of the obligation of freeing a believing slave if you were unable to do so, by making it obligatory for you to fast for two consecutive months. And God is Knowing and Wise. He says: And God has always been Knowing of what is good for His servants in what He charges them with of His obligations and other things, Wise of what He decrees for them and wants.
4:93: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, killing him, intending to destroy his life, his recompense is Hell, meaning: his reward for killing him, Hell, meaning: the torment of Hell, abiding therein, meaning: remaining there, and the ha’ and the alif in His statement: therein are from the mention of Hell, “and the wrath of God upon him,” meaning: and the wrath of God upon him for killing him intentionally, and cursed him, meaning: and distanced him from His mercy and disgraced him, and prepared for him a great punishment, and that is something whose extent is not known to anyone but Him, may He be glorified. The people of interpretation differed about the description of the killing that deserves to be called deliberate, after all of them agreed that if a man strikes a man with an iron edge that wounds, cuts, or slits, and he does not stop striking him with it until he destroys himself, and he is striking him with it intending to strike him: then he intentionally killed him. Then they differed about what is beyond that. Some of them said: There is no intention except what was like that in the manner we described. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Ata’ said: The deliberate is the weapon - or he said: the iron - he said: And Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It is the weapon. Abu Kuraib and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, they said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Deliberate killing is that which is done with an iron weapon, and that which is done without an iron weapon is semi-deliberate killing, and there is no retaliation for it. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Deliberate is what is done with an iron object, and quasi-deliberate is what is done with wood. Quasi-deliberate can only be done to the soul. Ahmad bin Hammad al-Dulabi told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Tawus, he said: Whoever kills in a clannish manner, by throwing stones at them, or flogging with whips, or hitting with sticks, then it is an accident, and his blood money is the blood money of an accident. And whoever kills intentionally, then his hand is to be retaliated for. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir and Mughirah told us, on the authority of Al-Harith and his companions, regarding a man who beats another man and he becomes sick until he dies. He said: Ask the witnesses that he beat him, and he remained sick from his beating until he died. If it was with a weapon, then it is retaliation, and if it was with something else, then it is quasi-intentional. Others said: Everything that the striker intended to cause harm to the person being struck is intentional, if what he struck with was most likely to kill. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Habban bin Abi Jabalah, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, that he said: What intention is more intentional than hitting a man with a stick, and then not stopping until he dies? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: If he strangles him with a rope until he dies, or strikes him with a stick until he dies, then it is retaliation. The reason for those who say: Everything other than iron is wrong is: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Azib, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, he said, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Everything is a mistake except the sword, and for every mistake there is a compensation. The reason for the one who said: The ruling on everything that kills the one who is struck with it is the ruling on the sword, in that whoever kills with it is a deliberate victim!, is: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu al-Walid told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: A Jew impregnated a slave girl on her back between two rocks, so he was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he killed him between two rocks. They said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took retaliation for the one who killed with a stone, and that is not iron. They said: And the same is the ruling for anyone who kills a man with something, the most likely of which is that he is killed like the one killed with it, similar to the ruling for the Jew who kills a slave girl between two stones. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement regarding this matter, according to us, is the statement of those who said: Whoever strikes a person with something that is most likely to kill him, and does not stop until he kills himself with it, is a premeditated murderer, regardless of what he was struck with, based on what we mentioned from the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for his saying: His recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said that it means: His punishment is Hell if He punishes him. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, regarding the statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, he said: It is his recompense, and if He wills, He may forgive him. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Al-Nu’man Al-Hakam bin Abdullah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Yasar, on the authority of Abu Salih: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell. He said: His recompense is Hell if He punishes him. Others said: This refers to a specific man who had converted to Islam but then abandoned his Islam and killed a believing man. They said: Whoever kills a believer intentionally, considering his killing permissible, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah: That a man from the Ansar killed the brother of Muqays ibn Subaba, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him the blood money and he accepted it, then he attacked his brother’s killer and killed him. Ibn Jurayj said: And someone else said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, imposed his blood money on Banu al-Najjar, then he sent Muqays, and sent with him a man from Banu Fihr on an errand for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He carried Muqays al-Fihri - who was strong - and threw him to the ground, and crushed his head between two stones, then he was found singing: I took revenge on him, and the nobles of Banu al-Najjar, the masters of Fare’, carried his mind. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I think he has done something! By God, if he has done something, I will not trust him in any place outside the sanctuary, in peace, or in war! So he was killed on the day of the conquest. Ibn Jurayj said: This verse was revealed about him: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, the verse. Others said: The meaning of this is: except for those who repent. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said: Saeed bin Jubair told me - or: Al-Hakam told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair - he said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, he said: If a man knows Islam and the laws of Islam, then kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, and there is no repentance for him, so I mentioned that to Mujahid and he said: Except for the one who regrets it. Others said: This is an imposition from God of a threat to the one who intentionally kills a believer, whoever the killer may be, as He has not described him in His Book, and He has not made it possible for him to repent from his action. They said: So every intentional killer of a believer will have what God has threatened him with of torment and eternal life in Hell, and there is no repentance for him. They said: This verse was revealed after the one in Surat Al-Furqan. Who said that? Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Yahya al-Jaber on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d who said: We were with Ibn Abbas after he had lost his sight, when a man came to him and called out: O Abdullah ibn Abbas, what do you think of a man who killed a believer intentionally? He said: His recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and the wrath and curse of God are upon him, and a great punishment is prepared for him. He said: What if he repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, then finds guidance? Ibn Abbas said: May his mother lose him! How can he repent and find guidance? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I heard your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: May his mother lose him! A man who killed a man intentionally will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his right or left hand, his veins gushing with blood, before the Throne of the Most Merciful, holding his killer with his other hand saying: Ask this man why he killed me? By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Abdullah, this verse was revealed, and no verse abrogated it until your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, and no proof was revealed after it. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Abu Khalid narrated, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, on the authority of Yahya ibn al-Harin al-Taimi, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and God has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment. It was said to him: What if he repents, believes, and does righteous deeds? He said: How can he repent?! Abu Kuraib narrated, Musa bin Dawud narrated, Hammam narrated, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Rabir, on the authority of Salim, who said: I was sitting with Ibn Abbas when a man asked him, What do you think of a man who intentionally kills a believer? Where will he end up? He said, Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and God has become angry and cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment. He said, What if he repents, believes, and does righteous deeds, then finds guidance? He said, How can he be guided? May his mother be bereaved of him! By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I heard him say - meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - “He will come on the Day of Resurrection with his head hanging from one of his hands, either his right or his left, holding his companion by the other hand, his veins sticking out towards the Throne of the Most Merciful, saying, ‘O Lord, ask this servant of yours why he killed me?’ So no prophet came after your Prophet, and no book was revealed after your book.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, he said, Ammar bin Raziq told us, on the authority of Ammar al-Dahni, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: something similar, except that he said in his hadith: By God, it was revealed to your Prophet, then something abrogated it, and I heard him say: Woe to the killer of the believer, he will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his head in his hand, then he mentioned the hadith similar to it. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Abdurrahman bin Abza told me: Ibn Abbas was asked about the statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, he said: Nothing abrogated it. And he said about this verse: “And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty” (al-Furqan 25:68). He said: It was revealed about the polytheists. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Abdurrahman bin Abza ordered me to ask Ibn Abbas about these two verses, and he mentioned something similar. Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Talq bin Ghannam narrated to us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, he said: Saeed bin Jubair narrated to me - or: I was told on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair - that Abd al-Rahman bin Abza ordered him to ask Ibn Abbas about these two verses in al-Nisa 4:And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell to the end of the verse, and the verse in al-Furqan 25:And whoever should do that will meet a sin to and will abide therein in disgrace (al-Furqan 25:68-69). Ibn Abbas said: If a man enters Islam and learns its laws and its commands, then he kills a believer intentionally, there is no repentance for him. As for the verse in Al-Furqan, when it was revealed, the polytheists of Mecca said: We have equated God with us, and we have killed the soul that God has forbidden unjustly, and we have committed indecencies, so Islam will not benefit us! He said: Then the verse was revealed: Except for those who repent (al-Furqan 25:70). Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Mughira ibn al-Nu’man, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, he said: Nothing abrogated it. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdur-Rahman told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It is among the last to be revealed, and nothing abrogated it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, he said: The people of Kufa differed about killing a believer, so I went to Ibn Abbas and asked him, and he said: It was revealed among the last to be revealed of the Qur’an, and nothing abrogated it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Abu Iyas Mu’awiyah bin Qurra told us, he said, Shahr bin Hawshab told me, he said, I heard Ibn Abbas say: This verse was revealed: And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell after His saying: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteousness (Al-Furqan 25:70), one year later. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Salim bin Qutaybah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: And whoever kills a believer intentionally - his recompense is Hell, he said: It was revealed after except for those who repent (al-Furqan 25:75), by a year. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Samad Ibn Abd Al-Warith told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: Abu Iyas told us, he told me who heard Ibn Abbas say about the killer of the believer: It was revealed a year after that. So I said to Abu Iyas: Who told you? He said: Shahr Ibn Hawshab. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, he said: There is no repentance for the killer, unless he seeks forgiveness from God. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally the verse, Atiyah said: Ibn Abbas was asked about it, and he claimed that it was revealed eight years after the verse in Surat Al-Furqan, which is His statement: And those who do not invoke with God another deity to His statement: Forgiving, Merciful (al-Furqan 25:68-70). Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu al-Safar, on the authority of Najbah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They are the two ambiguous ones: polytheism and murder. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The greatest of the major sins is associating partners with God and killing a soul that God has forbidden, because God Almighty says: His recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and God has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of some of his Kufi sheikhs, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding his statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, he said: It is a decisive matter, and it only increases in severity. Abu Kuraib narrated, Uthman ibn Saeed narrated, Hayaj ibn Bastam narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Kharijah ibn Zayd, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: Surat al-Nisa was revealed six months after Surat al-Furqan. Ibn al-Barqi narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Maryam, who said: Nafi’ ibn Yazid narrated, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah al-Bajali, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The one who was killed will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his head in his right hand, his jugular vein gushing with blood, saying: O Lord, my blood is with so-and-so! So they will be taken and supported by the Throne, and I do not know what will be decided between them. Then he recited this verse: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally (al-Furqan 4:10). Ibn Abbas said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, God, the Almighty, has not abrogated it since He revealed it to your Prophet, peace be upon him. Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, he said, I heard a man telling Kharijah bin Zayd bin Thabit, on the authority of Zayd bin Thabit, he said, I heard your father say: The severe verse was revealed six months after the easy verse, His statement: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, to the end of the verse, after His statement: And those who do not invoke with God another deity, to the end of the verse, (al-Furqan 25:68). Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, he said: I heard a man telling Kharijah bin Zayd, he said: I heard your father in this place in Mina say: The severe was revealed after the easy one - he said: I think it was: six months - meaning: And whoever kills a believer intentionally after: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him (An-Nisa’: 48, 116). Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: Nothing has abrogated it since it was revealed, and there is no repentance for it. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense, if He punishes him, is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally. But He pardons and bestows favor upon the people of faith in Him and His Messenger, so He does not punish them with eternal abode in it. Rather, He, the Mighty and Sublime, will either pardon him out of His grace and not admit him to Hell, or He will admit him to it and then bring him out of it out of the grace of His mercy, based on what He previously promised His believing servants in His saying: “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins.” (al-Zumar 39:53) If someone thinks that if the murderer must be included in this verse, then the polytheist must be included in it, because polytheism is one of the sins. God Almighty has informed us that He will not forgive polytheism for anyone, saying: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills (An-Nisa’: 48, 116), and murder is less than polytheism.
4:94: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: O you who have believed, O you who have believed in God and believed in His Messenger in what he brought to them from their Lord, when you go forth in the cause of God, meaning: when you set out on a journey for God in jihad against your enemies, then verify, meaning: take your time in killing someone whose matter is unclear to you, so you do not know the truth of his Islam or his disbelief, and do not rush to kill someone whose matter is unclear to you, and do not rush to kill someone whose killing is not preceded by killing someone you know for certain, in war against you, God, and His Messenger, “and do not say to one who offers you peace,” meaning: and do not say to one who surrenders to you but does not fight you, showing you that he is from your religion and your call, you are not a believer, so that you kill him seeking, the display of worldly life, meaning: seeking the enjoyment of worldly life, for, with God are many spoils, from His provisions and the excess of His blessings, so it is report to you if you obey God in what He commanded you to do it and forbade you from it, so He rewarded you for it for your obedience to Him, so seek that from Him. Thus were you before, meaning: just as this one who offered you peace and you said to him: You are not a believer, so you killed him, so were you before, meaning: before God glorified His religion with his followers and supporters, you were belittling your religion, just as this one whom you killed and whose wealth you took hid his religion from his people so that he would not reveal it to them, fearing for himself from them. He said that the meaning of His statement: Thus were you before is that you were disbelievers like them, then God bestowed His favor upon you, meaning: so God favored you by glorifying His religion with its supporters and the large number of its followers. It has been said: God has bestowed upon you repentance for killing this one whom you killed and took his money after he offered you peace. Then verify, meaning: Do not rush to kill the one you wanted to kill, whose Islam you were confused about, for perhaps God has bestowed upon him a similar Islam as He bestowed upon you, and guided him to the same faith to which He guided you. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Aware, meaning: God was aware of your killing of those you kill, and your restraint from those you restrain from killing from the enemies of God and your enemies, and other matters of yours and the matters of others. Aware, meaning: He has experience and knowledge of it, and He preserves it for you and them, until He rewards all of you for it on the Day of Resurrection, the doer of good for his good, and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed regarding a man killed by a company of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after he said: I am a Muslim, or after he bore witness to the truth - or after he greeted them - for spoils that he had with him, or other matters of his property, so they took him from him. He mentioned the narration and the traces in that: Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Muhallim ibn Juthamah as an expedition. Amir ibn al-Adbat met them and greeted them with the greeting of Islam. There was a quarrel between them in the pre-Islamic period, so Muhallim shot him with an arrow and killed him. The report reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ‘Uyaynah and al-Aqra’ spoke about it. Al-Aqra’ said: O Messenger of God, today is a different age than tomorrow! ‘Uyaynah said: No, by God, not until his wives taste the same grief as my wives! Muhallim came wearing two cloaks and sat in front of the Messenger of God to seek forgiveness for him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: May God not forgive you! He stood up while wiping his tears with his two cloaks. Not even seven days had passed before he died. They buried him and the earth rejected him. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He said: The earth accepts those who are worse than your companion! But God, the Almighty, the Majestic, wanted to admonish you. Then they threw him between the two sides of a mountain, and threw stones at him, and the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate, the verse. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Abu al-Qa’qa’ ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami, on the authority of his father Abdullah ibn Abi Hadrad, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent us to Idam. I went out with a group of Muslims, among them Abu Qatada al-Harith ibn Rib’i and Muhallim ibn Juthama ibn Qays al-Laythi. We went out until we were in the valley of Idam, and Amir ibn al-Adbat al-Ashja’i passed by us on his camel, with his provisions and a bowl of milk. When he passed by us, he greeted us with the greeting of Islam, but we refrained from him. Muhallim ibn Juthama al-Laythi attacked him because of something that had happened between them, and he killed him and took his camel and provisions. When we returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the story, the Qur’an was revealed concerning us: “O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate and do not say to one who gives you peace, ‘You are not a believer.’” (al-An’am 4:10) Harun bin Idris al-Asamm told me, he said, al-Maharibi Abd al-Rahman bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Qusayt, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami, on the authority of his father, something similar. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Some Muslims caught up with a man in his spoils, and he said: Peace be upon you! So they killed him and took the spoils, and this verse was revealed: “And do not say to one who gives you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’ seeking the goods of worldly life,” that was the spoils. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Muslims caught up with a man, then he mentioned something similar. Abu Kuraib narrated that Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated on the authority of Isra’il on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: A man from Banu Salim passed by some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was with his sheep, and he greeted them. They said: He only greeted you to seek refuge from you! So they went after him, killed him, and took his sheep and brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate to the end of the verse. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, he said: A man would speak about Islam, believe in God and the Messenger, and be among his people. When the expedition of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, he would inform his tribe - meaning his people - and they would flee. The man would remain, not fearing the believers because he was of their religion, until he met them and greeted them with peace. The believers would say, You are not a believer, and he had greeted them, so they would kill him. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate, to seek the goods of worldly life, meaning: kill him in order to make lawful for you his wealth that you found with him - and that is the goods of worldly life - for I have many spoils, so seek from the bounty of God. He was a man named Mirdas, and his people fled from a cavalry that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent, led by a man from Banu Laith named Qulayb. He did not flee with them, and when Mirdas met them and greeted them, they killed him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his family to pay blood money, and returned his money to them, and forbade the believers from doing such a thing. Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate, the verse. He said: This hadith is about Mirdas, a man from Ghatafan. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent an army led by Ghalib al-Laythi to the people of Fadak, and there were people from Ghatafan in it, and Mirdas was one of them. His companions fled, and Mirdas said: I am a believer, and I will not follow you. So the cavalry attacked him in the morning, and when they met him, Mirdas greeted them. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shot him and killed him, and took whatever goods he had with him. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed about him: “And do not say to one who gives you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’” because the greeting of the Muslims is peace, with which they recognize each other, and with which they greet each other. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi: “O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate and do not say to one who offers you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’ seeking the goods of worldly life. But with God are many spoils. Thus were you before, but God has bestowed His favor upon you, so investigate.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a detachment led by Usamah ibn Zayd to Banu Damrah. They met a man from them called Mirdas ibn Nahik, who had his spoils and a red camel. When he saw them, he took refuge in a cave in the mountain, and Usamah followed him. When Mirdas reached the cave, he placed his sheep in it, then he turned to them and said, “Peace be upon you. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.” Usamah attacked him and killed him, for the sake of his camel and his spoils. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Usamah, he liked to be praised and his companions would ask about him. When they returned, he did not ask them about him. The people began to talk to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and say: O Messenger of God, if you had seen Usamah and a man met him, and the man said: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, then he attacked him and killed him! He turned away from them. When they kept at him, he raised his head to Usamah and said: How are you with there is no god but God?
