He said: O Messenger of God, he only said it seeking refuge, seek refuge with it! The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Why did you not split open his heart and look at it? He said: O Messenger of God, his heart is a part of his body! Then God revealed the report of this and informed him that he had killed him for the sake of his camel and sheep. That is when God says: Seeking the goods of the worldly life. When he reached: Then God has conferred favor upon you, he said: Then God has accepted your repentance. Usamah swore that he would not fight a man who says there is no god but God after that man and what he had encountered from the Messenger of God because of him. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement of God: {And do not say to one who offers you peace, You are not a believer,}, he said: It has reached me that a Muslim man attacked a polytheist and attacked him. The polytheist said to him: I am a Muslim, I bear witness that there is no god but God. The Muslim killed him after he said it. When that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said to the one who killed him: Did you kill him after he said there is no god but God? He said, apologetically: O Prophet of God, he only said it to seek refuge, but that is not the case! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Why didn't you split open his heart? Then the man's killer died and was buried, but the earth threw him out. This was mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he ordered them to bury him, but the earth threw him out, and they did that to him three times. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The earth refused to accept him, so they threw him into one of the caves. Muammar said: Some of them said: The earth accepts those who are worse than him, but God made him a lesson for you. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq: That a group of Muslims met a polytheist while he was in his spoils, and he said: Peace be upon you, I am a believer. They thought that he was seeking refuge in that, so they killed him and took his spoils. He said: Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed: “And do not say to one who offers you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’ seeking the goods of worldly life,” that was the spoils. Thus were you before, but God has bestowed His favor upon you, so verify. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said, my father narrated, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Amra, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate, he said: Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad went out on a military expedition, sent by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: They passed by a man with his spoils, and he said: I am a Muslim, so Al-Miqdad killed him. When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: “And do not say to one who offers you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’ seeking the goods of worldly life,” he said: spoils. Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: That was revealed about a man killed by Abu al-Darda’. He mentioned from the story of Abu al-Darda’, something similar to the story that was mentioned about Usamah ibn Zayd, and it was mentioned in the interpretation of his statement: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, then he said in al-Naba 78:And the Criterion was revealed: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, so he read until he reached: You are not a believer, seeking the goods of the worldly life, his booty that was, the goods of the worldly life, but with God are many spoils, better than those spoils, until his statement: Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: “And do not say to one who offers you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’” he said: A shepherd of sheep was met by a group of believers who killed him and took what he had with him, and they did not accept from him: “Peace be upon you, for I am a believer.” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And do not say to one who gives you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’” he said: God has forbidden the believers to say to one who bears witness that there is no god but God, You are not a believer, just as He has forbidden them to eat dead meat. He is safe with regard to his wealth and blood, so do not reject his statement. Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his statement: So verify. The majority of the Meccan and Medinan reciters, and some of the Kufians and Basrans, read it as fatabayyinu with a ya and a noon, from tabayyun meaning to take one’s time, look, and uncover something until it becomes clear. The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as fatabayyinu, meaning to verify, which is the opposite of haste. Abu Jaafar said: Our opinion on this matter is that they are two well-known readings that are widely used in the reading of Muslims with one meaning, even if the wording differs between them. Because what is verified is clarified, and what is clarified is verified, so whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct in his reading in that regard. There is a difference in the reading of His statement: And do not say to one who offers you peace. The majority of the Meccans, Medinans, and Kufians read it as as-Salam without an alif, meaning surrender. Some Kufians and Basrans read: “peace” with an alif, meaning greeting. Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading of this in our view is: for those who offer them peace, meaning: those who surrender to you, submitting to God’s monotheism, and acknowledging your religion. We chose this because of the difference in the narrations about it: Some narrators narrate that he surrendered by bearing witness to the truth and saying: I am a Muslim. Some narrate that he said: Peace be upon you, so he greeted them with the greeting of Islam. Some narrate that he was a Muslim with a previous Islam before they killed him. All of these meanings are included in peace, because the Muslim is one who surrenders, and the one who greets with the greeting of Islam is one who surrenders, and the one who bears witness to the truth is one who surrenders to the people of Islam. So the meaning of peace includes all the meanings that were narrated about the murdered person about whom this verse was revealed. But that is not the case with peace, because peace has no meaning in this situation except greeting. Therefore, we described peace as correct. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: Thus were you before. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Just as this man whom you killed after he offered you peace, was hiding his religion from his people, fearing for his life from them, you were hiding your religion from your people, fearing for your lives from them, so God was gracious to you. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Abdullah bin Kathir told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, regarding his statement: Thus were you before, you belittled your faith, just as this shepherd belittled his faith. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: That is how you were before, concealing your faith from the polytheists. Others said: The meaning of this is: Just as this one whom you killed, after he offered you peace, was a disbeliever, you were disbelievers, so He guided him as He guided you. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said Ibn Wahb told us, he said Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Thus were you before, but God bestowed His favor upon you, disbelievers like him, so verify. Abu Ja`far said: The first of these two interpretations of the verse is the first, which is the opinion of those who said: Thus you were concealing your faith from your people of the polytheists while you were residing among them, just as this one whom you killed was residing among his people of the polytheists, concealing his religion from them. Rather, we said: This interpretation is more correct, because God Almighty only rebuked those who killed him from the people of faith after he had offered them peace and did not lead his killers to it, due to the confusion that had entered into his affair with his killers due to his position among his people from the polytheists, and their assumption that he had offered peace to the believers seeking refuge from them, and he did not rebuke them for killing him as a polytheist, so it would be said: Just as he was a disbeliever, you were disbelievers. Rather, there is no reason for that, because God Almighty did not rebuke anyone from His creation for killing a polytheist who was at war with God and His Messenger, after He had given him permission to kill him. The people of interpretation also differed in the interpretation of his saying: So God has been gracious to you. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: God has bestowed His favor upon you by making His religion manifest and honoring its people, until they made Islam manifest after they had concealed it from the people of polytheism. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: So God bestowed His favor upon you, so he declared Islam. Others said: The meaning of this is: God has bestowed His favor upon you, O murderers, who offered you peace, seeking the offer of worldly life, by repenting for killing him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: So God has been gracious to you, meaning: God has accepted your repentance. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the one I mentioned on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, because of what we have mentioned of the evidence that the meaning of His statement, Thus were you before, is what we have described before. So what should follow that is: Then God bestowed His favor upon you, so He removed the fear you were in from your enemies by manifesting His religion and honoring His people, until you were able to manifest what you used to hide of His Oneness and worship of Him, out of fear of the polytheists.
4:95: Abu Ja'far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Are not those believers who sit at home other than those who are disabled and those who strive in jihad equal? Those who are left behind from jihad in the cause of God from among the people of faith in God and His Messenger, who prefer ease, humility, and sitting in their homes over enduring the hardships of travel and travelling on earth, and the difficulty of meeting the enemies of God by striving for the sake of God, and fighting them in obedience to God, are not equal, except for those among them who have an excuse such as the loss of their sight, and other reasons for which there is no way for their people - due to the harm they are suffering - to fight and strive in the cause of God, and those who strive in the cause of God, and the path of His religion, so that the word of God may be supreme, who exhaust their energy in fighting the enemies of God and the enemies of their religion, with their wealth, spending it on what weakens the plot of the enemies of the people of faith in God - and with themselves, directly fighting them, so that the word of God may be exalted, and the word of those who disbelieve may be base. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: except for those who are harmed. This was read by the majority of the people of Medina, Mecca, and the Levant, except those who are harmed by it, in the accusative case, meaning: except those who are harmed. The majority of the people of Kufa and Basra read this as: Ghair Uli al-Harrar with ghair raised, according to the description of those who sit. Abu Ja`far said: The correct reading of this in our view is: other than those who are harmed, with other than in the accusative case, because the reports agree that His statement: other than those who are harmed was revealed after His statement: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives, as an exception to His statement: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive. Some of the report reported about this: Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa': The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bring me the shoulder blade and the tablet. So he wrote: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive hard, and Amr bin Umm Maktum was behind him. So he said: Do I have a dispensation, O Messenger of God? Then the following was revealed: Except those who are disabled. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Bakr Ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: When the verse, Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum, who was blind, came and said: O Messenger of God, how can I be blind when I am blind? He did not stop until the verse, Except those who are disabled, was revealed. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, regarding His statement: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, except those who are disabled, he said: When it was revealed, Amr bin Umm Maktum came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was blind, and he said: O Messenger of God, what do you command me, for I am blind? So God revealed this verse, and he said: Bring me the shoulder blade and the inkwell, or: the tablet and the inkwell. Ismail bin Israel Al-Dallal Al-Ramli told me, he said, Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Al-Mughirah told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’: When the verse: Not equal are those believers who sit at home, was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum spoke to him, so the verse: Except those who are disabled was revealed. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, that he heard Al-Baraa’ say about this verse: Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive and fight in the cause of God. He said: So the Messenger of God ordered Ibn Zaid to bring a shoulder and write it. He said: So Ibn Umm Maktum complained to him about his disability, so the verse: Not equal are those believers who sit at home was revealed, except those who are disabled. Shu`bah said: Sa`d ibn Ibrahim informed me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Zayd, regarding this verse: Those who sit are not equal, like the hadith of Al-Baraa. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan al-Shaibani, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zayd bin Arqam, he said: When the verse: Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive and fight in the cause of God, was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum came and said: O Messenger of God, do I have an exemption? He said: No! Ibn Umm Maktum said: O God, I am blind, so grant me an exemption! So God revealed: except those who are disabled, and He commanded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to write it, meaning: the scribe. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay` and Ya`qub ibn Ibrahim told me: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, who said: I saw Marwan ibn al-Hakam sitting, so I came and sat next to him, and he told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit: That the verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home and those who strive and fight in the cause of God. Ibn Umm Maktum came while he was dictating it to me and said: O Messenger of God, if I could fight, I would fight! So the verse was revealed to him while his thigh was on my thigh, and I felt heavy, and I thought that my thigh would be broken, then it was relieved, and he said: Except those who are disabled. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb, on the authority of Zayd bin Thabit, he said: “I was writing for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Write: ‘Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive in the cause of God.’ Then Abdullah bin Umm Maktum came and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I love striving in the cause of God, but I have a condition that you see, and my sight has gone!’ Zayd said: The thigh of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became so heavy on my thigh that I feared that he would crush it. Then he said: Write: ‘Not equal are those believers who sit at home except those who have a disability and those who strive in the cause of God.’” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Abd al-Karim told me: Muqsim, the freed slave of Abdullah bin al-Harith, told him: Ibn Abbas told him, he said: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal, about Badr, and those who go out to Badr. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, Abdul Karim informed me that he heard Muqsim narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he heard him say: Not equal are those believers who sit at home, about Badr, and those who went out to Badr, when the Battle of Badr was revealed. Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum and Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh ibn Qays Al-Asadi said: O Messenger of God, we are blind, so do we have a dispensation? So the verse was revealed: “Not equal are those believers who sit at home, except those who have a disability, and those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives. God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree.” Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Those believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives. Then Abdullah bin Umm Maktum, the blind man, heard about that, “So he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, God has revealed about jihad what you know, and I am a blind man who is unable to fight. Do I have a dispensation from God if I sit? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I have not been commanded to do anything about you, and I do not know if there is a dispensation for you and your companions! Ibn Umm Maktum said: O God, I ask You for my sight! Then God revealed after that to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Those believers who sit at home except those who are disabled are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God,” until His saying: A degree above those who sit. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, he said: The verse was revealed: Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive and fight in the cause of God. A blind man said: O Prophet of God, I love jihad but I am not able to fight! So the verse was revealed: Except those who are disabled. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Hisin told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, who said: When this verse was revealed about jihad: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, Abdullah bin Umm Maktum said: O Messenger of God, I am blind as you can see! Then the verse was revealed: Except those who are disabled. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, except for those who have a disability, God excused those who had an excuse from among the people, saying: except for those who have a disability, among them was Ibn Umm Maktum, and those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: Not equal are those believers who sit at home, except those who are disabled, and those who strive and fight in the cause of God, up to His saying: And to each God has promised good, when he mentioned the virtue of jihad, Ibn Umm Maktum said: O Messenger of God, I am blind and I am not able to fight! So God revealed concerning him: except those who are disabled. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Nufaili told us, he said, Zuhair ibn Muawiyah told us, he said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Bara’, he said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Call Zaid for me, and tell him to bring - or: bring - the shoulder blade and the inkwell - or: the tablet and the inkwell - the doubt is from Zuhair - and write: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God. Ibn Umm Maktum said: O Messenger of God, my eyes are hurt! So before he left, the verse was revealed: ‘except those who are disabled.’” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Raja’ al-Basri told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara’, similarly, except that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Call Zaid for me, and let him bring me with him a shoulder blade and an inkwell - or: a tablet and an inkwell. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ubayd God bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Ziyad bin Fayyad, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, he said: When the verse, Those who sit at home are not equal, was revealed, Amr bin Umm Maktum said: O Lord, You have tested me, so what should I do? He said: Then the verse, Except those who are disabled, was revealed. Ibn Abbas used to say something similar to what we said about the meaning of not those who are harmed. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: except those who are harmed, he said: those who are harmed. Abu Ja`far said: What he meant by his saying, may his praise be exalted: God has favoured those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree, is that God has favoured those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home who are disabled by one degree - meaning: one virtue - and that is by virtue of his striving with himself. As for other than that, they are equal, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us: He heard Ibn Jurayj say in: God has given preference to those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit back by a degree, he said: over those who are harmed. Abu Ja`far said: He, may His praise be glorified, means: And to all of them God has promised the best, God has promised all of those who strive with their wealth and their lives, and those who sit back from among the people of harm, the best, and He, may His praise be glorified, means: by the best, Paradise, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And to each of them God has promised the best, which is Paradise, and God gives every person of virtue His virtue. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: Al-Hasna means Paradise. As for his saying: And God has favored those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit with no harm, with a great reward, it means: And God has favored those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit with no harm, with a great reward, as: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And God has preferred those who strive over those who sit at home with a great reward * Degrees from Him and forgiveness, he said: Over those who sit at home from among the believers who are not disabled.
4:96: Abu Jaafar said: He, may His praise be glorified, means: degrees from Him, virtues from Him and stations of honor. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the degrees of which God Almighty said: Degrees from Him. Some of them said: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Degrees from Him, forgiveness, and mercy. It was said: Islam is a degree, and migration in Islam is a degree, and jihad in migration is a degree, and killing in jihad is a degree. Others said: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, I asked Ibn Zayd about the statement of God, the Most High: “And God has preferred those who strive hard over those who sit at home, with a great reward. Degrees from Him.” The degrees are the seven that He mentioned in Surat Bara’ah: “It was not for the people of Madinah and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind the Messenger of God or to prefer themselves over himself. That is because they are afflicted neither by thirst nor by fatigue.” So he recited until he reached: The best of what they used to do. (al-Tawbah 9:120-121) He said: These are the seven degrees. He said: And the first thing was, the degree of jihad was general, so the one who strives with his money has a name in this, but when these degrees came in detail, he was excluded from it, so he had nothing from it except the expenses, so he recited: They are afflicted neither by thirst nor by fatigue. (al-Tawbah 9:120), and he said: This is not for the one who spends. Then he recited: And they do not spend anything. (al-Tawbah 9:120), he said: This is the expenses of the one who sits. Others said: He meant by that the degrees of Paradise. Who said that? Ali bin Al-Hassan Al-Azdi told us, he said, Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Jabalah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Ibn Muhairiz, regarding his statement: God has favored those who strive over those who sit, to his statement: degrees, he said: The degrees are seventy degrees, and between the two degrees a well-trained horse is seventy years old. Abu Ja`far said: The most appropriate interpretation of his statement, degrees thereof, is that it means the degrees of Paradise, as Ibn Muhayriz said. Because the statement of God Almighty, degrees thereof, is a translation and explanation of his statement, a great reward, and it is known that the reward is the recompense and recompense. Since this is the case, and the degrees, forgiveness, and mercy are a translation of it, it is known that there is no basis for the statement of those who attributed the meaning of his statement, degrees from it, to deeds and their increase over the deeds of those who sit back from jihad, as Qatada and Ibn Zayd said. Since this is the case, and the correct interpretation of this is what we have mentioned, then it is clear that the meaning of the statement is: God has favored those who strive in the cause of God over those who sit at home other than those who are disabled, with a great reward and abundant recompense, which are degrees that He has given them in the Hereafter from the degrees of Paradise, raising them by it over those who sit at home because of what they have done for the sake of God. And forgiveness, he says: And He pardoned them for their sins, so He favored them by leaving their punishment for them, and mercy, he says: And compassion for them, and God is Forgiving and Merciful, he says: And God has always been forgiving of the sins of His believing servants, pardoning them for their punishment, Merciful towards them, favoring them with His blessings, despite their disobedience to His commands and prohibitions, and their committing His sins.
4:97: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty means by His statement: Those whom the angels take in death, that those whose souls the angels take, are wrongdoers to themselves, meaning: those who earn God’s wrath and anger for themselves. We have explained the meaning of injustice previously. They said, ‘In what were you?’ He says: The angels said to them: In what were you? In what part of your religion were you? They said, ‘We were oppressed on the earth.’ That is, those whom the angels took while they were wronging themselves said: We were oppressed on the earth. The polytheists oppress us in our land and country with their great numbers and strength, and they prevent us from believing in God and following His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a weak excuse and a flimsy argument. They said, ‘Was not the earth of God spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?’ He says: So you would leave your land and your homes, and separate from those who prevent you from believing in God and following His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the land whose people prevent you from the authority of the polytheists, so you would unify God therein and worship Him, and follow His Prophet? God Almighty says: Their abode is Hell, meaning: These are those whose description I have described to you, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, their abode is Hell, meaning: Their destiny in the Hereafter is Hell, which is their abode, and evil it is as a destination, meaning: Hell is evil for its people who have gone to it, as a destination, as a dwelling, and as a shelter.
4:98: Then He, the Most High, excepted the weak ones whom the polytheists oppressed - of men, women, and children, and they are those who are unable to emigrate, due to difficulty, lack of resources, poor eyesight, and poor knowledge of the road, from their land, the land of polytheism, to the land of Islam, from the people whom He, the Most High, informed us that their abode is Hell - from Hell being their abode, due to the excuse they are in, as He, the Most High, explained. The accusative case of the oppressed is an exception to the ha’ and the mim in His statement: Then their abode is Hell.
4:99: God, the Most High, says: Then it is those whom God may pardon, meaning: these are the weak ones. He says: Perhaps God will pardon them, due to the excuse they have while they are believers, so He will favor them by forgiving them for not emigrating, since they did not leave it by choice or preference for the land of disbelief over the land of Islam, but rather due to their inability to move from it. And God is Pardoning and Forgiving, He says: And God has always been Pardoning, meaning: He pardons, by His grace, the sins of His servants, by leaving the punishment for them, Forgiving, covering their sins by forgiving them for them. He mentioned that these two verses and the ones after them were revealed about some people from Mecca who had converted to Islam and believed in God and His Messenger, but they had not emigrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he emigrated. Some of them were exposed to temptation and were tempted, and they witnessed the war with the polytheists against the Muslims. God refused to accept the excuse they had made, which He explained in His statement, reporting on them: They said, ‘We were oppressed in the land.’ Mentioning the report that came with the authenticity of what we mentioned, about the revelation of the verse regarding those we mentioned that it was revealed regarding: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Ikrimah: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, he said: There were people from the people of Mecca who converted to Islam, and whoever died there was destroyed. God said: For those, their refuge is Hell, and evil it is as a destination, except for the oppressed among men, women and children until His saying: Pardoning, Forgiving. Ibn Abbas said: So I am one of them, and my mother is one of them. Ikrimah said: And Al-Abbas was one of them. Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi narrated, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri narrated, Muhammad bin Sharik narrated, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were people from Mecca who had converted to Islam, but they were hiding their Islam. The polytheists expelled them with them on the day of Badr, and some of them were killed. The Muslims said: These people of ours were Muslims, and they were forced! So they asked forgiveness for them, and this verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves - they will be asked, ‘In what condition were you?’ [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] He said: So he wrote to those Muslims who remained in Mecca with this verse: They have no excuse. He said: So they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them and caused them trial, so it was revealed about: And of the people is he who says, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the cause of God (al-Ankabut 29:10), to the end of the verse. So the Muslims wrote to them about that, and they were saddened and despaired of all good. Then it was revealed about them: Indeed, your Lord is to those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful (Al-Nahl: 110). So they wrote to them about that: Indeed, God has made a way out for you, so they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them, and they fought them until those who escaped escaped and those who were killed were killed. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Haywah or Ibn Lahi’ah told us, the doubt is from Yunus - on the authority of Abu al-Aswad: that he heard a freed slave of Ibn Abbas say on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Some Muslim people were with the polytheists and they would increase the number of polytheists against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so an arrow would come and be shot, and it would hit one of them and kill him, or it would strike and kill him, so God revealed about them: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves until he reached and they emigrated therein. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told me, he said: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri’ told us, he said: Haywah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal al-Asadi told us: A mission was sent to Yemen by the people of Medina, so I registered for it. I met Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, and he forbade me from that in the strongest terms. Then he said: Ibn Abbas told me that some Muslims were with the polytheists. Then he mentioned something like the hadith of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, they are people who came after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did not go out with him. So whoever among them died before joining the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the angels struck his face and back. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves - they will say, ‘In what [condition] were you?’ until His statement: And evil is the destination, he said: It was revealed about Qays ibn Al-Fakih ibn Al-Mughira, Al-Harith ibn Zama’ah ibn Al-Aswad, Qays ibn Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Abu Al-‘As ibn Munabbih ibn Al-Hajjaj, and Ali ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf. He said: When the polytheists from Quraysh and their followers went out to prevent Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and the Quraysh caravan from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and his companions, and to seek what they had taken from them on the Day of Nakhl, some young men went out with them reluctantly, who had converted to Islam and gathered at Badr without an appointment, so they killed infidels at Badr and turned away from Islam, and they are those whom we have named. Ibn Jurayj said, and Mujahid said: This verse was revealed about those who were killed on the Day of Badr from the weak infidels from Quraysh. Ibn Jurayj said, and Ikrimah said: When the Qur’an was revealed about these people up to the words, And evil is the destination, “Except for the weak among men, women, and children,” he said: It means the old man, the old woman, the young slave girls, and the boys. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves until His saying: And evil is the destination, he said: When al-Abbas and Nawfal were taken prisoner, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to al-Abbas: Redeem yourself and your nephew. He said: O Messenger of God, did we not pray towards your qiblah and bear witness to your testimony? He said: O Abbas, you argued and you disputed! Then he recited this verse: Was not God’s earth spacious enough for you to emigrate therein? For those, their refuge is Hell, and evil it is as a destination, so on the day this verse was revealed, whoever embraced Islam but did not emigrate, he is a disbeliever until he emigrates, except for the weak who cannot find a way nor are they guided to a way, a way with money, and the way is the road. Ibn Abbas said: I was one of them, from the children. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he said: I heard Ikrimah say: There were people in Mecca who had testified that there is no god but God, and when the polytheists went out to Badr, they took them out with them, and they were killed, so the following verse was revealed about them: Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves until the words: Those - perhaps God will pardon them, and God is Pardoning and Forgiving. The Muslims in Medina conveyed this to the Muslims in Mecca. He said: We sent out some Muslims, and when they were on a part of the road, the polytheists sought them out, and they caught up with them, and some of them gave rise to temptation? So God revealed about them: And of mankind is he who says, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the cause of God, he considers the persecution of the people to be like the punishment of God. (al-Ankabut 29:10) The Muslims in Medina wrote to the Muslims in Mecca, and God revealed about those who were subjected to the trial: Then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then fought. (al-Nahl
4:100: Abu Ja'far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God, and whoever leaves the land of polytheism and its people, fleeing for his religion from it and from them, to the land of Islam and its believing people, for the cause of God, meaning: in the method of God's religion and His way that He has prescribed for His creation, and that is the upright religion, will find on the earth many [alternative] locations, meaning: This emigrant will find many [alternative] locations, and he is the one who is disturbed in the country and the religion. It is said from this: So-and-so is opposing his people, opposing and opposing, a verbal noun, and from this is the saying of Nabigha Bani Ja'dah: Like a mountain, the dear one who is reluctant and the one who escapes seeks refuge in its corners His saying: and spaciousness, it may be interpreted as spaciousness in the matter of their religion in Mecca, and that was preventing them - them - from showing their religion and worshipping their Lord openly. Then, the Most High, the Praised, informed us about the one who emigrated from the land of polytheism, fleeing with his religion to God and His Messenger, if his death overtook him before reaching the land of Islam and the abode of migration. He said: Whoever is like that, his reward has become due to God, and that is the reward for his work and the recompense for his emigration and leaving his homeland and his tribe for the abode of Islam and the people of his religion. The Most High, the Praised, says: And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger, then the reward for his emigration is due to his Lord - if he does not reach the abode of his emigration because death overtook him before he reached it - and God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: God, the Most High, has always been Forgiving, meaning: He covers the sins of His believing servants by pardoning them from punishment for them, Merciful, kind to them. He mentioned that this verse was revealed because of some of those who were residing in Mecca and were Muslims, so he left when he heard that God had revealed the two verses before it, which are His saying: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, to His saying: And God is Forgiving and Forgiving, so he died on his way before reaching Medina. Mentioning the report reported about this: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding His statement: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God and His Messenger, he said: There was a man from Khuza`ah called Damrah in Al-Muhais - or: Al-`Ays ibn Damrah ibn Zinba` - he said: When they were ordered to emigrate, he was ill, so he ordered his family to spread out a bed for him and carry him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: So they did, and death came to him while he was in At-Tan`im, so this verse was revealed. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, that he said: This verse was revealed: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has become incumbent upon God, concerning Damrah ibn al-Muhays ibn al-Zinba` - or so-and-so ibn Damrah ibn al-`Ays ibn al-Zinba` - when he reached al-Tan`im and died, so it was revealed concerning him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam Al-Taimi, similar to the hadith of Yaqub, on the authority of Hisham, he said: He was a man from Khuza’ah. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance, the verse. He said: When God revealed these verses, a man from among the believers called Damrah was in Mecca and said: By God, I have enough wealth to take me to Medina and beyond, and I am indeed guided! Take me out, and he was sick at that time. When he crossed the Sacred Sanctuary, God took him and he died. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God, the verse. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: When the verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, some men from among the Muslims said that day while he was sick: By God, I have no excuse. I am a guide on the road, and I am well-off, so carry me. So they carried him, and death overtook him on the road, and the verse was revealed about him: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God and His Messenger. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: When God revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, and the two verses, a man from Banu Damrah, who was ill, said: Bring me out to the spirit, so they brought him out, until he died in al-Hashahs, and then the verse was revealed about him: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God and His Messenger, and the verse. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Mundhir bin Tha’laba, on the authority of Alba’ bin Ahmar Al-Yashkari, his saying: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has become incumbent upon God, he said: It was revealed about a man from Khuza’ah. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Aamer told us, Qurra told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding the statement of God, the Almighty and Majestic: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon God, he said: When a man from the people of Mecca heard that the angels had struck the faces and backs of Banu Kinanah, he said to his family: Take me out, for he is close to death. He said: So he was carried until he reached a pass that he had named, and he died, and God revealed: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger, the verse. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: When Damrah ibn Jundub al-Damri heard this - meaning: His statement: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves to His statement: And God is Pardoning and Forgiving - Damrah ibn Jundub al-Damri said to his family, and he was in pain: Move my mount, for the two mountains have covered me - meaning: the two mountains of Mecca - so that I may go out and a spirit may strike me! So he sat on his mount, then he headed towards Madinah, and he died on the way, so God revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has become incumbent upon God. And when he headed towards Madinah, he said: O God, I am emigrating to You and to Your Messenger. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed, meaning His statement: Indeed, those whom the angels take in death, Jundub bin Damrah Al-Junda’i said: O God, I have conveyed my apology and argument, but I have no apology or argument! He said: Then he went out while he was an old man, and he died on the way, so the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He died before he emigrated, so we do not know whether he had the highest position of authority or not! So this verse was revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home as an emigrant to God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has become incumbent upon God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say: When God revealed about those who were killed with the polytheists of Quraysh at Badr: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves 2:100, a man from Banu Laith who was following the religion of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and residing in Mecca heard what God had revealed about them. He was an old man and a young man. He said to his family: I will not spend the night in Mecca! So he went out with him, and when he reached At-Tan’im on the road to Medina, death overtook him, and the following was revealed about him: And whoever emigrates for the sake of God 2:100. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance, he said: A man from Banu Kinanah emigrated seeking the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he died on the way, so his people mocked him and ridiculed him and said: He neither achieved what he wanted, nor did he stay with his family so that they could take care of him and bury him! He said: Then the Qur’an was revealed: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has become incumbent upon God. Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, and there was a man in Mecca called Damrah, from Banu Bakr, who was ill. He said to his family: Get me out of Mecca, for I am feeling very hot. They said: Where should we take you? He pointed with his hand toward Medina, and this verse was revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God and His Messenger, to the end of the verse. Al-Harith bin Abi Usamah told me, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Aban told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: When this verse was revealed: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home except those who are disabled, he said: Some of the Muslims in Mecca who were disabled made concessions regarding it, until the virtue of the mujahideen over the mujahideen was revealed, so they said: God has made clear the virtue of the mujahideen over the mujahideen, and has made concessions for the disabled! Until the verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves until His saying: And evil is the destination, they said: This is binding! Until the verse was revealed: Except for the weak among men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan nor are they shown a way, so Damrah bin Al-Ays Al-Zarqi, one of the Banu Laith, who was blind, said: I am capable of planning, I have wealth, and I have slaves, so carry me. He went out while he was sick, and death overtook him at At-Tan’eem. He was buried at At-Tan’eem Mosque, and this verse was revealed about him: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him Al-Tan’eem 1:17. The interpreters differed in the interpretation of al-Maraghim. Some of them said: It is the transition from one land to another. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: Much reluctantly, he said: Refusing is moving from one land to another. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: often resorting to evil, that is: shifting. Al-Muthanna told me, who said: Ishaq told us, who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi`, regarding His statement: He will find on the earth many places of refuge, that is: shifting. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan or Qatada: Much reluctantly, he said: Changing. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: He will find on earth many places of refuge, he said: An escape from what he dislikes. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Much reluctantly, he said: Refusing to do what he dislikes. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Muhad: Much reluctantly, he said: Refusing to do what he dislikes. Others said: seeking a livelihood. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hasan told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: He finds many places of refuge on earth, meaning: seeking a livelihood. Others said: The one who is reluctant, the immigrant. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: in denial, the denial is the emigrant. Abu Jaafar said: We have already explained the most correct of the sayings on this matter in what has passed before. They also differed about the meaning of the reputation that God mentioned in this place. He said: vast. Some of them said: It is: the abundance of provision. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Much and abundant, he said: Abundance in provision. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement: Much and abundant, he said: Abundance in provision. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: ample, meaning: abundance in provision. And others said regarding that what: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He will find on earth many places of refuge and abundance, yes, by God, from misguidance to guidance, and from poverty to wealth. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God has informed us that whoever migrates for His sake will find on earth both turmoil and spaciousness. Spaciousness may include spaciousness in provision and wealth from poverty, and spaciousness from the narrowness of worry and distress that the people of faith in God from the polytheists in Mecca were in, and other meanings of spaciousness, which means the spirit and relief from the dislike that God disliked for the believers due to their standing among the polytheists and under their authority. God did not provide evidence that He meant by His saying: spaciousness some of the meanings of spaciousness that we have described. So all meanings of spaciousness that mean the spirit and relief from what they were in of narrow living conditions, and the grief of being in the neighborhood of the polytheists, and the tightness of the chest due to the difficulty of showing faith in God and sincerely believing in His Oneness and separating from rivals and gods, are included in that. Some scholars have interpreted this verse - I mean His statement: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon God - as being like a fighter who goes out for a raid, and death overtakes him after he has left his home and dies, that he has his share of the spoils, even if he did not witness the battle, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yusuf bin Adi told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib: The people of Medina say: Whoever goes out to separate, his share is obligatory, and they interpreted the words of God Almighty: And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger.
4:101: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: And when you travel through the land, and when you travel, O believers, through the land, there is no blame upon you, meaning: there is no blame nor sin upon you, that you shorten the prayer, meaning: that you shorten its number, so you pray whatever number you had of it when you were at home and you were staying, four, two, according to some of them. And it was said: its meaning is: there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer to its minimum number while you are traveling through the land, he pointed to one, according to others. Others said: The meaning of this is: There is no blame upon you if you shorten the limits of prayer. If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, meaning: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you in your prayer. And their temptation of them in it means that they attack them while they are prostrating in it until they kill them or take them prisoner, preventing them from establishing and performing it, and standing between them and the worship of God and sincere monotheism for Him. Then He, the Most High, informed them about what the disbelievers were doing to them, saying: Indeed, the disbelievers have been to you a clear enemy, meaning: those who denied the Oneness of God. They have been to you a clear enemy, meaning: an enemy who has made their hostility clear to you by waging war against you because of your belief in God and His Messenger, and your abandoning the worship of what they worship of idols and statues, and your opposition to what they are upon of misguidance. The interpreters differed about the meaning of: the palace in which God placed the wing, regarding its doer. Some of them said: When travelling, the prayer that was obligatory to be completed when at home was four rak’ahs, and permission was given to shorten it when travelling to two. Who said that? Ubayd ibn Ismail al-Hibari told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ammar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Babih, on the authority of Ya`la ibn Munyah, he said: I said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer if you fear, while the people are safe! He said: I was amazed by what amazed me, until I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he said: It is charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ammar, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Babih, on the authority of Ya`la Ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi narrated, he said: Muhammad bin Abi Uday narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: I heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abi Ammar narrating, on the authority of Abdullah bin Babih narrating, on the authority of Ya’la bin Umayya, he said: I said to Umar bin Al-Khattab: I am amazed at people shortening the prayer even though they are safe, and God the Most High said: That you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you! Umar said: I am amazed at what you are amazed at, so I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: It is a charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity. Ibn Bashar narrated, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated, Abu Awana narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, who said: I travelled to Mecca, and I was praying two rak’ahs, and some reciters from this area met me and said: How do you pray? I said: Two rak’ahs. They said: Sunnah or Qur’an? I said: Eat, Sunnah and Qur’an, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed two rak’ahs. They said: He was at war! I said: God said: “God has fulfilled the vision of His Messenger in truth. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if God wills, in security, with your heads shaved or your hair cut short, having no fear” (al-Fath 48:27), and He said: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, and he recited until he reached: And when you are secure. Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, Saif told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali, who said: A group of merchants asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we travel throughout the land, so how do we pray? So God revealed: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, then the revelation was cut off. A year later, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on a military expedition and prayed the noon prayer. The polytheists said: Muhammad and his companions have given you control over their backs, why did you not attack them more severely? One of them said: They will have another like it after it! So God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed between the two prayers: “If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you - indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy. * And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a party of them stand with you” until His saying: Indeed, God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment, so the prayer of fear was revealed. Abu Ja`far said: This is a good interpretation of the verse, if the words if were not in the speech, and if indicates the disconnection of what comes after it from the meaning of what comes before it. If the words if were not in the speech, the meaning of the speech - according to this interpretation that Sayf narrated on the authority of Abu Rawq - would be: If you fear, O believers, that those who disbelieve will tempt you in your prayer, and you are among them, O Muhammad, and you lead them in prayer, then let a group of them stand with you verse. And then, this is what was mentioned in the reading of Abi bin Kaab: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you. Al-Harith told me that, he said: Abdul Aziz told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Wasil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abza, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, that he used to recite: That you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, and he did not recite: If you fear. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bakr bin Shurud told us, on the authority of Al-Thawri, on the authority of Wasil Al-Ahdab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b that he read: That you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you. Bakr said: And it is in the Imam’s copy of the Mushaf of Uthman, may God have mercy on him: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you. This reading indicates that His statement, If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, is a continuation of His statement, There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, and that the meaning of the statement is: And when you travel throughout the land, if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, and that His statement, And when you are among them, is an introductory story different from the story of this verse. This is because the interpretation of this reading of Abu that we mentioned from him: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, lest those who disbelieve tempt you. So la was omitted because the speech indicates it, as God Almighty said: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray (An-Nisa’: 76), meaning: lest you go astray. In what we have described as evidence of the corruption of the interpretation narrated by Saif, on the authority of Abu Rawq. Others said: Rather, it is shortening the prayer while traveling, but God Almighty only permitted it for the traveler in a state of fear of an enemy who he fears will tempt him during his prayer. Who said that? Abu Asim Imran bin Muhammad Al-Ansari told me, he said: Abdul Kabir bin Abdul Majeed told us, he said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Bakr Al-Siddiq told me, he said: I heard my father say: I heard Aisha say while traveling: Complete your prayer. They said: Does the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pray two rak’ahs while traveling? She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was at war and was afraid. Are you afraid? Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me, he said, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, he said, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Umayyah ibn Abdullah ibn Khalid ibn Asid: that he said to Abdullah ibn Umar: We find in the Book of God the shortening of the prayer of fear, but we do not find the shortening of the prayer of the traveler? Abdullah said: We found our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, doing a deed that we did. Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father: That Aisha used to pray two rak’ahs while traveling. Saeed bin Yahya told us, my father told us, Ibn Jurayj told us: I said to Ata’: Which of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to complete the prayer while traveling? He said: Aisha and Saad bin Abi Waqqas. Others said: Rather, this verse means shortening the prayer of fear, except in the case of combat. They said: And it was revealed about it. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, he said: One day the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were at Usfan, and the polytheists were at Dajnan, and they stopped, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions prayed the noon prayer with two rak’ahs - or: four, Abu Asim was uncertain - their bowing, prostration, and standing all together, then the polytheists intended to attack their luggage and their burdens, so God revealed to him: So let a party of them stand with you, so he prayed the afternoon prayer, so he lined up his companions in two rows, then he said the takbir with them all, then the first prostrated once, and the others stood, then the others prostrated when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood, then he said the takbir with them and they all bowed, so the last row advanced and the first stayed behind, so they took turns prostrating as they did the first time, and the afternoon prayer was shortened to two rak’ahs. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, On the authority of Mujahid: There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were in Usfan and the polytheists were in Dajnan, so they stopped, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon prayer with his companions in two rak’ahs, bowing, prostrating, and standing all together. The polytheists wanted to attack their luggage and burdens, so God Almighty revealed: Then let a party of them stand with you. So he prayed the afternoon prayer with them, and his companions lined up in two rows, then he said the takbir with them all, then the first prostrated for his prostration, and the last stood and did not prostrate, until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood, then he said the takbir with them, and they all bowed, so the other row advanced and the front row retreated, so they took turns prostrating as they had entered the first time, and the afternoon prayer was shortened to two rak’ahs. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi, he said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Usfan, and Khalid ibn al-Walid was in charge of the polytheists. He said: So we prayed the noon prayer, and the polytheists said, They were in a state, if we had wanted to, we would have taken them by surprise, we would have been caught by surprise. The verse of shortening the prayers between noon and afternoon prayers was revealed. “Then the people took up their weapons and lined up behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, facing the qiblah, and the polytheists faced them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Allahu Akbar,’ and they all said, ‘Allahu Akbar.’ Then he bowed, and they all bowed. Then he raised his head, and they all raised their heads. Then he prostrated, and the row next to him prostrated, and the others stood guarding them. When these finished their prostration, these prostrated, then the row next to him retreated and the others advanced, and they stood in their places. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bowed, and they all bowed. When these finished their prostration, these others prostrated, then they stood with him, and they all sat down. Then he greeted them all, and he prayed it in ‘Usfan, and he prayed it on the day of Banu Sulaym.” Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Shaiban al-Nahwi, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi, and on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Ayyash, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Usfan, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sulayman al-Yashkari: that he asked Jabir bin Abdullah about shortening the prayer: On what day was it revealed? Or: On what day is it? Jabir said: We set out to meet the caravan of Quraysh coming from Ash-Sham, until we reached Nakhl, “A man from the people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad! He said: Yes. He said: Do you fear me? He said: No. He said: Who will protect you from me? He said: God will protect me from you! He said: Draw your sword, then he threatened him and warned him, then he called for departure and took up arms, then the call for prayer was made, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with a group of the people and another group guarding them, so he prayed two rak’ahs with those closest to him, then those closest to him retreated on their heels and stood in line with their companions, then the others came and he prayed two rak’ahs with them while the others guarded them, then he said the salutation. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed four rak’ahs, and the people prayed two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs, and on that day God revealed about shortening the prayer and commanding the believers to take up arms.” Others said: Rather, it means shortening the prayer of fear in a situation other than extreme fear, except that it means shortening the prayer of travel, not the prayer of residence. They said: This is because the prayer of travel in a situation other than fear is two rak'ahs, complete and not shortened, just as the prayer of residence is four rak'ahs in a situation of residence. They said: So it was shortened in travel in a situation of security other than fear from the prayer of the resident, so it was made half, and it is complete in travel. Then it was shortened in a situation of fear while traveling from the prayer of security in it, so it was made half, one rak'ah. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening your prayers, until His saying: A clear enemy, that if you pray two rak’ahs of prayer while traveling, then it is complete. Shortening is not permissible, unless you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you away from the prayer. Shortening is one rak’ah: the imam stands and his soldiers stand in two groups, one group behind him and one group parallel to the enemy, so he prays one rak’ah with those with him, and they walk towards them on their backs until they stand in the place of their companions, and that is the backward walk. Then the other group comes and prays another rak’ah with the imam, then the imam sits and says the salutation, so they stand and pray one rak’ah for themselves, then they return to their row, and the others stand and add one rak’ah to their rak’ah. The people say: No, rather it is one rak’ah, none of them prays anything to his rak’ah, the imam’s rak’ah is sufficient for him. The imam will pray two rak’ahs, and they will pray one rak’ah. This is what God says: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer until His saying: And take your precautions. Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak al-Hanafi, he said: I asked Ibn `Umar about the prayer of travel, and he said: Two rak`ahs are complete and not shortened. Rather, shortening is the prayer of fear. I said: What is the prayer of fear? He said: The imam prays one rak`ah with a group, then these come in the place of those, and those come in the place of those, and he prays one rak`ah with them, so the imam prays two rak`ahs, and each group has one rak`ah. Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: How can it be shortened when they pray two rak’ahs? It is only one rak’ah. Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Baqiyah told us, he said, Al-Masoudi told us, he said, Yazid Al-Faqir told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: The prayer of fear is one rak’ah. Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, he said, my uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, he said, Bakr ibn Sawada told me: Ziyad ibn Nafi told him, on the authority of Ka’b - who was one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whose hand was cut off on the day of Yamamah - that the prayer of fear for each group is one rak’ah and two prostrations. Those who said this statement based their argument on the following narrations: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya ibn Sa’id told us, he said, Sufyan told us, he said, Ash’ath ibn Abi al-Sha’tha’ told me, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Hilal, on the authority of Tha’labah ibn Zahdam al-Yarbu’i, he said: We were with Sa’id ibn al-’As in Tabaristan, and he said: Who among you remembers the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in fear? Hudhayfah said: I will. So we stood behind him in a row, one row parallel to the enemy, and he prayed one rak’ah with those closest to him, then these went to the ranks of those, and those came and he prayed one rak’ah with them. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Rakeen ibn al-Rabi’, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Hassan, he said, I asked Zayd ibn Thabit about him and he told me something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Ash’ath, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Hilal, on the authority of Tha’laba ibn Zahdam al-Yarbu’i, on the authority of Hudhayfah, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm told me, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed at Dhi Qard, and the people lined up behind him in two rows, one row behind him and one row parallel to the enemy. He prayed one rak’ah with those behind him, then these went to the place of those, and those came, and he prayed one rak’ah with them and they did not make it up. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Sakhir, on the authority of Ubaid God bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Bishr bin Muadh told us - he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God imposed prayer on the tongue of your Prophet, peace be upon him, four rak’ahs when at home, two rak’ahs when traveling, and one rak’ah when in fear. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Bakir ibn al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Azdi told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Aaidh Al-Ta’i, on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Yaqub bin Mahan told us: Al-Qasim bin Malik told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Aaidh Al-Ta’i, on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, he said: Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Yazid al-Faqir, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them in the prayer of fear. A row stood in front of him and a row stood behind him, so he led those behind him in prayer, one rak`ah and two prostrations.
