Then these came forward until they stood in the place of their companions, and those came until they had taken the place of those, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them in prayer, one rak`ah and two prostrations, then he gave the salutation, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had two rak`ahs and they had one rak`ah.” Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman bin Wahb told us, he said, my uncle Abdullah bin Wahb told me, he said, Amr bin Al-Harith told me: Bakr bin Sawada told him, on the authority of Ziyad bin Nafi’ who told him, on the authority of Abu Musa: Jabir bin Abdullah told them: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with them the prayer of fear, and Muharib and Tha’laba were thrown, each group having one rak’ah and two prostrations.” Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Tusi told me, he said, Abd al-Samad told us, he said, Saeed bin Ubaid al-Hana’i told us, he said, Abdullah bin Shaqiq told us, he said, Abu Hurairah told us: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped between Dajnan and Usfan, and the polytheists said: These people have a prayer that is dearer to them than their children and their virgins, and it is the afternoon prayer, so make up your mind and attack them with one attack. Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ordered him to divide his companions into two groups, so that he would pray with some of them, and another group would stand behind them and take precautions and weapons, then he would order the other group to pray with him, and these would take precautions and weapons, so that they would have one rak’ah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have two rak’ahs.” Others said: It means shortening the prayer while traveling, except that it means shortening it during intense war and during sword fighting. So when the war is in full swing, it is permissible for the worshipper to bow one rak'ah, nodding his head wherever he faces. They said: This is the meaning of His statement: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when you travel throughout the land, the verse, shorten the prayer, if you encounter the enemy and the time for prayer has come: that you glorify God, and lower your head in a gesture, whether you are riding or walking. Abu Ja`far said: The first of these statements that we have mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the statement of those who said: What is meant by shortening it is its limits. That is leaving out the completion of its bowing and prostration, and permitting its performance in any way possible, facing the qiblah or turning one’s back to it, riding or walking, and that is in the case of a weapon, fencing, the clash of wars, and the advancing ranks, which is the case in which God Almighty said: But if you fear, then on foot or riding (al-Baqarah 2:239), and He permitted the obligatory prayer in it while riding, indicating the bowing and prostration, in the manner that was narrated from Ibn `Abbas regarding his interpretation of that. We said that this is the most appropriate interpretation of His statement: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, because the statement of God Almighty: And when you are secure, establish prayer, indicates that this is the case. Because establishing it means completing its limits of bowing, prostration, and all its obligations, without increasing its number, which was not obligatory in a state of fear. If someone thinks that this is a command from God to complete the number of rak’ahs that are obligatory upon him in a state of security after the fear has disappeared, then it may be necessary for the traveler, in his case of shortening his prayer from that of the resident, not to be performing his prayer, because the number of his prayers is less than the four obligatory rak’ahs that he would have performed when he was resident, to two rak’ahs. This is a statement, if someone says it, that contradicts what the ummah is unanimously agreed upon: that the traveler does not deserve to be told - if he performs his prayer with all the limits imposed upon him in it, and shortens its number from four to two - that he is not performing his prayer. If this is the case, and God Almighty has commanded the one who was permitted to shorten his prayer out of fear that his enemy would tempt him, to perform his prayer when he is reassured and the fear is gone, it is known that what was imposed on him to perform it in a state of reassurance is the same as what was dropped from him in a state of fear. And since what was imposed on him in a state of reassurance was to perform his prayer, then what was dropped from him in a state other than reassurance was to abandon performing it. And we have shown that abandoning performing it is abandoning its limits, as we have explained.
4:102: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And if you are among your companions, O Muhammad, who are fearful that their enemy will tempt them, and you establish prayer for them, meaning: So you establish prayer for them with its limits, bowing, and prostration, and you do not shorten it with the shortening that you permitted them to shorten it in the event that they meet their enemy and some of them are advancing on others, from neglecting to establish its limits, bowing, prostration, and the rest of its obligations, then let a group of them stand with you, meaning: Let a group of your companions, among whom you are with you, stand with you in your prayer, and let the rest of them face the enemy. He left out mentioning what the other groups that do not pray with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, should do, because the aforementioned words indicate what is meant by them, and what was mentioned is sufficient for what was left out. And let them take their weapons. The interpreters differed regarding the group commanded to take up arms. Some of them said: It is the group that used to pray with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: The meaning of the words: And let them take, is: And let the group praying with you take from their groups, their weapons, and the weapons that they were ordered to take with them in their prayers, such as the sword that one of them wears, and the knife, and the dagger that he fastens to his armor and the clothes that he is wearing, and the like of his weapons. Others said: Rather, the group ordered to take up arms from them is the group that was facing the enemy, not the group praying with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the statement of Ibn Abbas. Al-Muthanna told me that, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then when they prostrate, he says: So when the group that stood with you in your prayer prostrates, praying with your prayer, and they finish their prostration, then let them be behind you, he says: So let them, after they finish their prostration, stand behind you in the enemy’s ranks in the place where the rest of the groups that did not pray with you and did not join you in your prayer are. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: So when they prostrate, let them be behind you. Some of them said: Its interpretation is: So when they pray and finish their prayer, let them be behind you. Then the people of this article differed. Some of them said: If this group prays one rak'ah with the imam, they should say the salutation and leave their prayer until they reach the place where their companions stand facing the enemy, and they do not have to make it up. They said: They are the ones whom God meant by His saying: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, that you should make it - if you fear that the disbelievers will tempt you - one rak'ah. They narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he prayed with one group the fear prayer, one rak'ah, and they did not make it up, and with another group one rak'ah, and they did not make it up. We have mentioned some of this previously, and what we have mentioned is sufficient to cover all of what is in it. Others among them said: Rather, it was obligatory upon this group, which God commanded to stand with their Prophet if he wanted to establish prayer with them in a state of fear of the enemy, and if they finished their rak’ah in which God commanded them to pray with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He commanded them in His Book, to stand in the place where they prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pray for themselves the rest of their prayer and say the salutation, and go to the ranks of their companions. And it was upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to remain standing in his place until the group that prayed with him the first rak’ah finished the rest of their prayer, if their prayer that they prayed with him was one whose number may be shortened from the obligation that is upon those who reside in security, and they go to the ranks of their companions, and the other group that was in the ranks of their enemy comes, and he prays with them another rak’ah of their prayer. Then they differ in the ruling of this second group. A group of people who follow this opinion said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished his two rak’ahs and raised his head from prostration in his second rak’ah, he should sit for the tashahhud. The group that prayed the second rak’ah with him but did not catch up with him in the first rak’ah because they were busy with their enemy should stand up and perform their missed rak’ah with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) should wait for them while sitting for his tashahhud until this group finished their missed rak’ah and recited the tashahhud, then he should greet them. Another group of them said: Rather, it was obligatory for the group that did not catch up with him in the first rak’ah, if the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sat for the tashahhud, to sit with him for the tashahhud and recite his tashahhud. Then when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished his tashahhud, he said the salutation. Then the group that prayed the second rak’ah with him stood up and made up their missed rak’ah. And every one of those whose statement we mentioned narrated reports from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he did as he said. It was mentioned that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, waited for the two groups until each group had completed its prayer, and he did not exit his prayer until after the two groups had finished their prayer. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, on the authority of Salih ibn Khawat, on the authority of those who prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the fear prayer on the day of Dhat ar-Riqa’: That a group lined up with him, and a group faced the enemy. So he prayed one rak’ah with those with him, then he remained standing and they completed it for themselves. Then the other group came and he prayed with them, then he remained sitting and they completed it for themselves, then he gave them the salutation. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ubaydullah ibn Muadh told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salih ibn Khawat, on the authority of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with his companions in fear, and he made them two rows behind him. He prayed with those who were next to him one rak’ah, then he stood up. He remained standing until those behind him had prayed one rak’ah, then they moved forward and those who were in front of them stayed behind. He prayed one rak’ah with them, then he sat down until those who stayed behind had prayed one rak’ah, then he said the salutation.” Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: Ruh narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salih ibn Khawat, on the authority of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said regarding the fear prayer: A group stands in front of the imam and a group behind him, so he prays with those behind him one rak’ah and two prostrations, then he sits in his place until they complete one rak’ah and two prostrations, then they move to the place of their companions. Then those move to the place of these, so he prays with them one rak’ah and two prostrations, then he sits in his place until they pray one rak’ah and two prostrations, then he says the salutation.” It was mentioned that he said: “The second group would sit with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his prayer, then they would make up what remained of it.” Ibn Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, I heard Yahya bin Saeed, I heard Al-Qasim, Salih bin Khawat bin Jubair told me, that Sahl bin Abi Hathmah told him, that the prayer of fear is that the imam stands facing the qiblah and prays, and with him is a group of his companions, and another group facing the enemy, so he prays. The imam bows with those with him and prostrates, then he stands. When he stands up straight, those behind him bow for themselves, one rak’ah and two prostrations, then they say the salutation and leave, and the imam is standing. They stand facing the enemy, and the others come and say Allahu Akbar in place of the imam, so the imam bows with them and prostrates, then he says the salutation. They stand and bow for themselves, one rak’ah and two prostrations, then they say the salutation. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad: that Salih bin Khawat told him, on the authority of Sahl bin Abi Hathmah, regarding the prayer of fear, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us and he asked him, he said, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Salih, on the authority of Sahl bin Abi Hathmah, regarding the prayer of fear, he said: The imam stands facing the qiblah, and a group of them stand with him, and a group from the side of the enemy, their faces towards the enemy, so he bows with them in one rak’ah, then they bow for themselves and prostrate twice in their place, and they go to the place of those, and those come and he bows with them in one rak’ah and prostrates twice, so it is two rak’ahs for him and one for them. Then they bow in one rak’ah and prostrate twice. Bandar said: I asked Yahya bin Saeed about this hadith, so he told me on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salih bin Khawat, on the authority of Sahl bin Abi Hathmah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar to the hadith of Yahya bin Saeed, and he said to me: Write it next to it, for I do not memorize it, but it is similar to the hadith of Yahya bin Saeed. Nasr bin Ali told us, Abdul A’la told us, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad bin Abi Bakr, on the authority of Salih bin Khawat: That the imam stands and forms two rows, one group facing the enemy, and the other group behind the imam. The imam prays one rak’ah with those behind him, then they stand and pray one rak’ah for themselves, then they say the salutation, then they go and form a row. The others come and he prays one rak’ah with them, then he says the salutation, then they stand and pray one rak’ah for themselves. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la narrated to us, saying: Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Ubaydullah, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Salih ibn Khawat, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The prayer of fear is that a group stands behind the imam and a group faces the enemy. The imam prays one rak’ah with those behind him and stands, and the people pray another rak’ah with it, then they say the salutation and go to their companions. Their companions come while the imam is standing, and he prays one rak’ah with them, then he says the salutation. Then they stand and pray another rak’ah with it, then they leave. Ubaydullah said: I have not heard anything in what we mention about the prayer of fear that is better to me than this. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a party of them stand with you, this is when praying in fear. The imam stands and a party of them stands with him, and a party takes their weapons and stands facing the enemy. The imam prays one rak’ah with those with him, then he sits as he was, and the people stand and pray the second rak’ah for themselves while the imam is sitting. They do not leave until they come to their companions, so they stand in their place. Then the others come and the imam prays the second rak’ah with them, then he says the salutation, and the people stand and pray the second rak’ah for themselves. This is how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed on the day of Batn Nakhal. Others said: Rather, the interpretation of his statement: So when they prostrate, let them be behind you, is that if the group that stood with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he entered into his prayer prostrated and entered with him into his prayer, the second prostration of its first rak’ah, let them be behind you, meaning: behind you, O Muhammad, and behind your companions who did not pray facing the enemy. They said: This group did not finish its rak’ah when it finished the two prostrations of its rak’ah that it prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but rather it would go to the place where its companions stood facing the enemy, and the rest of its prayer was due. They said: The other group that was facing the enemy would come until it entered with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the rest of his prayer, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would pray with them the rak’ah that was left for him. They said: This is the meaning of the statement of God, the Exalted: And let another group come who have not prayed, and let them pray with you, and let them take their precautions and their weapons. Then the people of this article differed regarding the method of making up what remained for each group of these two groups of their prayers, after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his prayer and greeted him with his prayer, according to the sayings of the speakers of this article and the interpreters of this interpretation. Some of them said: The second group that prayed the second rak’ah of their prayer with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished his prayer, stood up and completed what they had missed of their prayer with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their place, after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished his prayer. The group that prayed the first rak’ah with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, facing the enemy had not yet completed it. So when they had finished the rest of the prayer that they had missed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they went to the ranks of their companions facing the enemy, and the first group that prayed the first rak’ah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the place where they had prayed behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and completed the rest of their prayer. The novel mentioned that: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Khasif narrated to us, Abu Ubaidah ibn Abd God narrated to us, “Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the fear prayer. A group of us stood behind him, and a group faced the enemy. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, led those behind him in one rak’ah, then they turned back and went to the place where their companions were standing. The others came and stood behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them in one rak’ah. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the salutation. Then these people stood up and prayed one rak’ah for themselves, then they went and stood in the place where their companions faced the enemy, and the others returned to their places and prayed one rak’ah for themselves.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, he said, Khasif told us, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the prayer of fear, and he mentioned something similar. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Others said: Rather, the second group that prayed the second rak’ah with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) did not complete the rest of their prayer after the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) had finished his prayer, but rather they would continue before completing the rest of their prayer, so they would stand in the place where their companions who had prayed the first rak’ah with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) had prayed, and the first group would come to the place where they had prayed their first rak’ah with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), and complete the rak’ah that was left of their prayer. Some of them said: They would complete that rak’ah without reciting. Others said: Rather, they would complete it with recitation. So when they had completed their remaining rak’ah there and given the salutation, they would go to the ranks of their companions facing the enemy, and the group that had prayed the second rak’ah with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) would return to the place where they had prayed the second rak’ah of the Messenger of God's (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) prayer with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), and complete the second rak’ah of their prayer with recitation. When they had finished and given the salutation, they would return to their companions. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding the prayer of fear, he said: He would form a row behind him, and a row facing the enemy in a place other than his prayer place, and he would pray one rak’ah with the row behind him, then they would go to the ranks of those, and those facing the enemy would come, so he would pray one rak’ah with them, then he would greet them, and he had prayed two rak’ahs, and each row would pray one rak’ah. Then those whom he had greeted would go to the ranks of those facing the enemy, and they would take their place, and they would come and complete the rak’ah, then they would go and stand in the place of those facing the enemy, and those would come and pray one rak’ah. Sufyan said: So it would be two rak’ahs for each person, two rak’ahs. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us and Ali told me, he said, Zaid told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: Ibrahim used to say in the fear prayer, and he mentioned something similar to it. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God have mercy on him, the same. Others said: Rather, each group of the two groups should complete its prayer as much as it can, without wasting any of it. Who said that? Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari led his companions in the fear prayer in Isfahan when he invaded it. He said: He led a group of the people in a rak'ah, and a group stood guard. Then those who had led them in a rak'ah turned back, and the others followed them and took their place. Then he led them in a rak'ah, then he said the salutation, and each group stood up and prayed a rak'ah. Imran bin Musa Al-Qazzaz told us, he said, Abdul-Warith told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Musa, something similar. Muhammad bin Bashar narrated, he said: Muadh bin Hisham narrated, he said: My father narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah and Yunus bin Jubair, they said: Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari led his companions in prayer in the dayr of Isfahan, and they were not afraid that day, but he wanted to teach them their prayer. So he lined them up in two rows: one row behind him, and one row facing the enemy, facing their enemy. So he prayed one rak'ah with those who were next to him, then they went to the rows of their companions. Then those people came, so he lined them up behind him, and he prayed one rak'ah with them, then he gave the salutation. So these people completed one rak'ah, and those people completed one rak'ah, then some of them gave the salutation to one another. So the imam would have two rak'ahs in a group, and they would have one rak'ah. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Abu Musa, similarly. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: He said regarding the fear prayer: He prays with a group of people one rak’ah, and a group stands guard. Then those with whom he prayed one rak’ah go and stand in the place of their companions, then those come and he prays one rak’ah with them, then he says the salutation. Then each group stands and prays one rak’ah. Nasr bin Ali told us, he said, Abdul A’la told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me, he said, Yahya bin Saleh told us, he said, Ibn Ayyash told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: that he prayed the prayer of fear, and he mentioned something similar. Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that he used to narrate that he prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Nafi’, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the fear prayer: The emir and a group of people stand and prostrate once, and a group of them stand between them and the enemy, then he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Harun al-Harbi told us, he said, Abu al-Mughirah al-Himsi told us, he said, al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Musa, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the fear prayer with one of the two groups, one rak’ah, then he mentioned something similar. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer until his statement: Let them pray with you, for a group of them would take up arms and face the enemy, and the other group would pray one rak`ah with the imam, then they would take up their arms and face the enemy, and their companions would go back and pray one rak`ah with the imam, so the imam would have two rak`ahs, and the rest of the people would have one rak`ah, then they would complete another rak`ah. And this is the completion of the prayer. Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed regarding the prayer of fear, and the enemy that day was at the back of the qiblah, between the Muslims and the qiblah. So the prayer that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with them that day was the prayer of fear, as the enemy was between the imam and the qiblah. Mentioning the report transmitted about that: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying, Yunus bin Bakir narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Nadr Abu Omar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out on a raid and met the polytheists at Usfan. When he prayed the noon prayer, they saw him bowing and prostrating with his companions. Some of them said to each other that day: ‘It was an opportunity for you. If you had attacked them, they would not have known about you until you attacked them!’ One of them said: ‘They have another prayer that is dearer to them than their families and their wealth, so prepare yourself until you attack them in it.’ Then God, the Almighty, revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘And when you are among them and lead them in prayer’ to the end of the verse, and informed him of what the polytheists had plotted. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the afternoon prayer and they were facing him in the qiblah, the Muslims formed two rows behind him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said Allahu Akbar and they all said Allahu Akbar. Then he bowed and they all bowed with him. When he prostrated, the row next to him prostrated with him, and the row behind them stood facing The enemy, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his prostration and stood up, the second row prostrated and then stood up, and those who were next to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed back and the others came forward, so they were next to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when he bowed, they all bowed with him, then he rose and they rose with him, then he prostrated and those next to him prostrated with him, and the second row stood facing the enemy, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his prostration and those next to him sat down, the last row prostrated, then they sat down and they all testified with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the greeting of peace, he greeted them all. When the polytheists looked at them, some of them prostrating and some of them standing looking at them, they said: They have been informed of what we wanted! Ibn Humayd narrated, Al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated, Umar ibn Dhir narrated, Mujahid narrated: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was at Usfan and the polytheists were at Dajnan at the water point next to Mecca. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon prayer, they saw him prostrating and the people prostrating. They said: If he prays another prayer after this, we will attack him! So God warned him of that. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray and said the takbir and the people said the takbir with him. Something similar was mentioned. Imran bin Bakkar told me, Yahya bin Salih told us, Ibn Ayyash told us, Ubaydullah bin Amr told me, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we met the polytheists at Nakhl, and they were between us and the qiblah. When the noon prayer came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in prayer, and we were all together. When we finished, the polytheists began to quarrel and said: If only we had attacked them while they were praying! Some of them said: They have a prayer that they are waiting for and it will come now, and it is dearer to them than their children, so when they pray, then turn towards them. He said: So Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the report, and taught him how to pray. When the afternoon prayer came, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood facing the enemy, and we stood behind him in two rows, and the Prophet of God said the takbir and we all said the takbir with him, then he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Muammar told me, he said, Hammad bin Mas`adah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Abi Abdullah, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Muammil bin Hisham narrated, Ismail bin Ibrahim narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar. Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, “On the authority of Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi, he said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Usfan, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the noon prayer, and Khalid ibn al-Walid was in charge of the polytheists. The polytheists said: We have caught them by surprise, and we have caught them unawares!! So God revealed the fear prayer between noon and afternoon prayers, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the afternoon prayer, and he divided us into two groups - one group praying with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the other group praying behind them, guarding them. Then he said Allahu Akbar, and they all said Allahu Akbar, and they all bowed together, then those who were next to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, then he stood up and the others came forward and prostrated, then he stood up and bowed with them all, then he prostrated with those next to him, until these fell behind and stood in the ranks of their companions, then the others came forward and prostrated, then he greeted them. So each of them had two rak’ahs with their imam. And he prayed again in The land of Bani Salim. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the verse, according to the opinion of those who said this statement and narrated this narration, is: And if you, O Muhammad, are among them - meaning: among your companions, fearing - “and you lead them in prayer, then let a group of them stand with you,” meaning: of those who joined you in your prayer, and when they prostrate, meaning: if this group prostrates with your prostration, and raises their heads from their prostration, then let them be behind you, meaning: let those behind you be behind the group that guarded you and them when you prostrate with them and they prostrate with you, and let another group come who have not prayed, meaning: the guarding group that prayed with him, but did not prostrate with his prostration. So the meaning of his saying: they have not prayed - according to the opinion of these people - is: they did not prostrate with your prostration, then let them pray with you, meaning: let them prostrate with your prostration when you prostrate, and let those who prostrated with your prostration in the first rak`ah guard you and them, and let them take their precautions and their weapons, meaning the guarding group. Abu Ja`far said: The first of the statements we have mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is: So when the group that stood with you in prayer prostrates, let them be behind you, meaning: behind you and behind whoever enters your prayer from those who did not pray the first rak`ah with you facing the enemy, and after they have finished the rest of their prayer, let another group come, which is the group that was facing the enemy, who did not pray, meaning: they did not pray the first rak`ah with you, let them pray with you, meaning: let them pray the rak`ah that remains for you, and let them take their precautions and their weapons, to fight their enemy, after they have finished their prayer. This is similar to the report narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he did it on the day of Dhat ar-Riqa’, and the report narrated by Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah. Rather, we said: This is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because God Almighty said: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, and we have shown that establishing it means completing it with bowing and prostration. And we have shown with that that His statement: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, is only permission to shorten its bowing and prostration in a state of intense fear. If this is correct, then it is clear that there is no basis for an interpretation of this: that if the first group prostrates with the imam, then their prayer is complete, because of His saying: So when they prostrate, let them be behind you, because this could have the meanings I mentioned before, and because there is no indication in the verse that the shortening mentioned in the verse before it meant shortening the number of rak’ahs. Since there is no basis for this, then the statement of those who said: What is meant by this is advancing and delaying in prayer, in the manner of the Prophet’s prayer, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Usfan, is further from the truth. This is because God Almighty says: And let another group come who have not prayed and pray with you, and both groups had prayed the first rak’ah with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his prayer in Usfan. It is impossible that the one who prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the one who did not pray with him. If someone thinks that what is meant by his saying, They did not pray, is that they did not prostrate, then that is not the apparent meaning understood from the meanings of prayer. Rather, the meanings of the words of God, may He be glorified, are directed to the most apparent and well-known of its aspects, unless something prevents that which must be accepted. Since this was the case, and the verse did not contain a command from God Almighty to the first group to delay making up what remained of their prayer until the imam had finished the rest of his prayer, nor was there any harm to the Muslims facing the enemy in being busy making up that, then there was no meaning to the command to delay that and to leave their place before making up the rest of their prayer. However, even if this is the case, we see that if an imam prays it and his prayer matches some of the aspects that we mentioned about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying it, then his prayer is complete and complete for him, due to the authenticity of the reports on all of that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that it is one of the matters that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught his nation, then he permitted them to do whatever they wanted. Abu Ja`far said: As for his statement: Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage, it means that those who disbelieve in God wished that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage, meaning that you would be busy with your prayers and not with the weapons with which you fight them, and with your baggage with which you are able to travel, so that you would be heedless of them, so that they would attack you with a single attack, meaning that they would attack you while you are busy with your prayers and not with your weapons and baggage, and they would take you by surprise, kill you and take your army by force. God Almighty says: Do not do that after this, so that you all become busy with your prayers when your prayer time comes and you are facing the enemy, so that you give your enemy power over yourselves, your weapons, and your belongings. Rather, establish prayer as I have explained to you, and take precautions against your enemy and your weapons. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement, And there is no blame upon you, and no burden or sin upon you, if you are harmed by rain, meaning: if you are harmed by rain that rains down while you are standing against your enemy, or you are ill, meaning: or you are wounded or on high ground, that you lay down your weapons, if you are too weak to carry them. But if you lay down your weapons because of harm from rain or illness, then take from your enemy, your warning, meaning: beware of them lest they attack you while you are heedless and unaware of them, Indeed, God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment, meaning by that: He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment in which they will remain forever, never to emerge from it. And that is the punishment of Hell. It was mentioned that his saying: Or you were ill was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who was wounded. Who said that? Abbas bin Muhammad told us, Hajjaj told us, Ibn Jurayj said, Ya`la bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If you are harmed by rain or are ill, Abd al-Rahman bin Awf, was wounded.
4:103: Abu Ja'far said: By that, the Most High means: So when you, O believers, have finished your prayer and you are facing your enemy - which we have explained to you - then remember God in all your states - standing, sitting, and lying on your sides, by glorifying Him, and praying for yourselves to be victorious over your enemy, so that God may grant you victory and aid you against them. This is similar to His saying: O you who have believed, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much that you may be successful (al-Anfal 8:45), and as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And remember God often, meaning: God does not impose an obligation on His servants except that He has set a known limit for it, then He excuses those who do it in a state of excuse, other than remembrance, for God has not set a limit for it to reach, and He has not excused anyone for abandoning it except one who is overcome by his mind, so He said: So remember God standing, sitting, and [lying] on your sides, by night and by day, on land and by sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and poverty, sickness and health, in secret and in public, and in every state. As for his saying: So when you are secure, establish prayer, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of his saying: Then when you are reassured, is when you have settled in your homelands and resided in your cities, then establish prayer, meaning: complete the prayer that you have been permitted to shorten in the event of your fear during your travels and your striking out on the earth. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Then when you are reassured, he said: leaving the place of travel to the place of residence. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “Then when you are at peace,” he said: When you are at peace in your cities, then complete the prayer. Others said: The meaning of this is: When you have settled down, establish the prayer, meaning: complete its limits with bowing and prostration. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then when you are reassured, he said: Then when you are reassured after fear. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: “So when you are at peace, then establish prayer,” he said: So when you are at peace, then perform the prayer, do not perform it riding, nor walking, nor sitting. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: So when you are secure, establish prayer, he said: Complete it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Abu Ja`far said: The most appropriate of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it: So when your fear of your enemy has passed and you have become secure, O believers, and your souls are reassured by security, establish prayer, so complete its limits imposed upon you, without falling short of any of its limits. We said that this is the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse, because God Almighty mentioned that He informed His believing servants of the obligation of their prayers with these two verses in two situations: One of them: In a state of intense fear, they were permitted to shorten the prayer, as I have explained, limiting its limits to completion. The other: A state other than extreme fear, in which He commanded them to establish its limits and complete them, as He, the Most High, described to them, of punishing each other in praying behind their imams, and guarding each other from their enemy. This is a state in which there is no shortcoming, because He, the Most High, says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this state: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer. So it is known from this that His statement: And when you are secure, establish prayer, means: When you are secure from the state in which you were not establishing your prayer, then establish it. And this is a state of extreme fear, because He commanded them to establish it in a state other than extreme fear by His statement: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer 1:10. Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: It means: Prayer was an obligatory duty for the believers. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi, regarding his statement: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, he said: It is obligatory. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, he said: Obligatory, specified, obligatory. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said: As for a fixed book, it is obligatory. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: A prescribed book, he said: It is obligatory. Others said: The meaning of this is that prayer was an obligatory duty for the believers. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, he said: An obligatory decree. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: a book of specified times, he said: obligatory. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Muammar bin Sam, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, regarding his statement: a book of specified times, he said: obligatory. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, and specified means obligatory. Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Muammar bin Yahya told us, he said, I heard Abu Ja`far say: Prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specific times, he said: its obligation. Others said: The meaning of this is: Prayer was prescribed for the believers at specific times, and they performed it according to its stars. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, he said: Ibn Masoud said: Prayer has a time like the time of Hajj. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding his statement: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, he said: In parts, whenever one star passes another star comes. He says: whenever a time passes another time comes. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Ja`far Al-Razi, on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, similarly. Abu Jaafar said: These statements are close in meaning to each other. Because what was imposed is obligatory, and what must be performed at a certain time is a mystery. However, the first meaning of the interpretation of the word is the saying of the one who said: Prayer was obligatory upon the believers at specified times, because timed is the action of the speaker: God has set an obligation upon you, so He will delay it. So His obligation upon you is timed, if you delay it, He has set a time for it that you must perform. Likewise, the meaning of His saying: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times, is: It was an obligation upon the believers at a specific time for them, a time for its obligation, so He made that clear to them.
4:104: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty means by His saying: And do not weaken, and do not become weak. From their saying: So-and-so is weak in this matter, he is weak and feeble. And His saying: In seeking out the people, means: in seeking out the people and seeking them, and the people are the enemies of God and the enemies of the believers from the people of polytheism with God, If you are suffering, he says: If you, O believers, are grieving from the wounds that befall you from them in this world, then they are suffering as you are suffering, he says: The polytheists are grieving from the wounds and harm that befall them from you just as you are grieving from their wounds and harm in it, and you hope, you, O believers, from God of reward for what befalls you from them, what they do not hope for what befalls them from you. He says: So, since you are certain of God’s reward for you for what they befall you, for what they deny, it is more appropriate and fitting that you be patient in their war and fighting them than they are in your war and fighting you, and that you strive in seeking and seeking them, to fight them for what they find easy and do not find, so how about what they strive for and do not find easy? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering.” He says: Do not weaken in pursuing the enemy, for if you are hungry, then they are hungry as you are, and you hope from God for reward and recompense that they do not hope for. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And do not weaken in pursuing the enemy, for if you are suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering. He said: He says: Do not weaken in pursuing the enemy, for if you are suffering from wounds, then they are suffering as you are suffering. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy, do not become weak. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement: And do not weaken, he said: Do not become weak. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy, he said, he says: Do not weaken in pursuing them, If you are suffering in fighting, then they are suffering as you are suffering. This is before they are wounded - if you hate fighting and you are suffering from it - “then they are suffering as you are suffering. And you hope from God that which they do not hope for,” he says: Do not weaken in pursuing them in the place of fighting. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: If you are in pain, you are in pain. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, If you are in pain, he said: You are in pain because of what they inflict on you, for they are in pain as you are, and you hope for a reward for what they inflict on you that they do not hope for. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Umar told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “When the Battle of Uhud took place, and the Muslims suffered what they suffered, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended the mountain, and Abu Sufyan came and said: O Muhammad, will you not go out? Will you not go out? War is a contest, one day for us and one day for you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Answer him. They said: No, no, no, our dead are in Paradise and your dead are in Hell. Abu Sufyan said: He consoled us and you have no consoler. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Tell him: God is our protector and you have no protector. Abu Sufyan said: Hubal is superior, Hubal is superior! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Tell him: God is higher and more exalted! Abu Sufyan said: Our meeting place and your meeting place is Badr Al-Sughra. And the Muslims slept with wounds on them.” And Ikrimah said: “In it was revealed: ‘If a wound should touch you, there has already touched the [other] people a wound similar to it. And such days We alternate among the people’” (Al Imran 3:140), and in it was revealed: ‘If you are suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering. And you hope from God that which they do not hope for. And ever is God Knowing and Wise’” (Al Imran 3:140). Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: If you are suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering, he said: They are hungry as you are hungry. It was mentioned about some of them that he interpreted his statement: And you hope from God what they do not hope for, and you fear from God what they do not fear, from God’s statement: Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God (al-Jathiyah 45:14), meaning: they do not fear the days of God. It is not known that the meaning of hope is used to mean fear in the speech of the Arabs, except with a previous denial of it, as God Almighty said: What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? (Nuh 71:13), meaning: you do not fear God’s greatness, and as the poet said: Do not expect when you meet the seven defenders whether they meet together or one As Abu Dhuayb al-Hudhali said: If a bee stings him, he does not want to be stung by it, and he opposes it in the house of Nubb factors It is, as far as we have been informed, a language used by the people of Hijaz, and they say it, meaning: I don’t care, I don’t care. By this, He, the Most High, means: God has always been Knowing of the interests of His creation, Wise in His management and judgment. And from His knowledge, O believers, of your interests, He has made you know - when your prayers are due and when God has imposed on you, and you are confronting your enemy - what will enable you to perform God’s obligation upon you and be safe from your enemy. And from His wisdom He has made you see what will support you and weaken the plot of your enemy.
4:105: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by that which God has shown you, “Indeed, We have sent down to you,” O Muhammad, the Book, meaning: the Qur’an, so that you may judge between the people, so that you may decide between the people and decide between them, by that which God has shown you, meaning: by that which God has sent down to you from His Book, and be not an advocate for the treacherous, meaning: and do not be an advocate for the one who betrays a Muslim or a covenanted person in his person or his wealth, “arguing on his behalf, and defending on his behalf whoever demands his right in which he betrayed him,
4:106: And seek forgiveness from God, O Muhammad, and ask Him to pardon you for the punishment of your sin in your dispute over the traitor who betrayed someone else's money, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: God has always pardoned the sins of His believing servants, by leaving them unpunished for them if they seek His forgiveness for them, Merciful to them. So do that, O Muhammad, and God will forgive you for your previous dispute over this traitor. It was said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not argue on behalf of the traitor, but he intended to do so, so God commanded him to seek forgiveness for what he intended to do. He mentioned that the traitors whom God Almighty rebuked His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his hostility towards them were Banu Ubayraq. The people of interpretation differed regarding his betrayal, which God described him with. Some of them said: It was a theft. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by that which God has shown you, until His statement: And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of God, in between that, regarding Ibn Ubayraq, and his armor of iron, from the Jews, which he had stolen: And his companions from the believers said to the Prophet: Excuse him before the people with your tongue, and they threw the armor at an innocent man from the Jews. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Hasan bin Ahmad bin Abi Shuaib Abu Muslim Al-Harrani narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Salamah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Asim bin Umar bin Qatada, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Qatada bin Al-Nu’man, he said: There was a family among us called Banu Ubayraq: Bishr, Bashir, and Mubashir. Bashir was a hypocrite, and he used to write poetry satirizing the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he would attribute it to some Arab, then he would say: So-and-so said such-and-such, and so-and-so said such-and-such. When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard that poetry, they would say: By God, only a wicked person would write this poetry! So he said: Or whenever men say a poem, they join in and say: Ibn Al-Abiraq said it! He said: They were a family of poverty and need in the pre-Islamic era and Islam. The food of the people in Medina was dates and barley. If a man was wealthy, a load of dirhams would arrive from Syria, and he would buy some of it and keep it for himself. As for the family, their food was dates and barley. A load of dirhams arrived from Syria, and my uncle Rifa’ah ibn Zayd bought a load of dirhams and put it in his drinking place. In the drinking place were his weapons: two coats of mail, their swords, and whatever was suitable for them. Then someone attacked him in the middle of the night, so the drinking place was dug up, and the food and weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa’ah came to me and said: O son of my brother, you know that we were attacked last night, so our drinking place was dug up, and our weapons and food were taken! He said: We searched the house and asked, and we were told: We saw the Banu Ubayraq lighting a fire this night, and we did not see from what we saw except some of your food. He said: Banu Ubairiq said while we were asking in the house: By God, we do not think your master is anyone other than Labid bin Sahl! A man from among us who is righteous and a Muslim. When Labid heard that, he drew his sword and came to Banu Ubairiq and said: By God, this sword will mix with you, or this theft will be exposed. They said: Go away from us, O man, by God, you are not its owner! So we asked in the house until we had no doubt that they were its owners, and my uncle said: O son of my brother, why don’t you go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tell him about that! Qatada said: So I came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and mentioned that to him and said: O Messenger of God, a family of ours are rude people. They went to my uncle Rifa’ah and dug into his drinking place and took his weapons and food. Let them return our weapons to us, as we have no need for the food. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: Look into that. When Banu Ubayraq heard that, they went to a man of theirs called Aseer ibn Urwah and spoke to him about that. Some of the people of the house gathered around him and came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and said: O Messenger of God, Qatada ibn al-Nu’man and his uncle went to a family of ours who are Muslims and righteous people and accused them of theft without any evidence or proof. Qatada said: So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him. He said: You went to a family among whom there is mention of Islam and righteousness, and you accuse them of theft without any evidence or proof!! He said: So I went back and wished that I had given away some of my money and not spoken to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it. So I went to my uncle Rifa’ah, and he said: O son of my brother, what did you do? So I told him what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to me. He said: God is the one sought for help! And it was not long before the Qur’an was revealed: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. And be not an advocate for the treacherous,” meaning: Banu Abiriq, and seek forgiveness from God, meaning: from what you said to Qatada, “Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves,” meaning: Banu Abiriq, “Indeed, God does not like anyone who is a traitor and a sinner. They hide themselves from the people,” until His saying: Then he seeks forgiveness from God, he will find God Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: if they seek forgiveness from God, He will forgive them, “And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And God is Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns a fault or a sin and then attributes it to an innocent person has indeed taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin,” their saying to al-Bayd, And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have resolved to mislead you, meaning: the captive and his companions, “And they mislead none but themselves, and they do not harm you at all. And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom,” until His saying: We will give him a great reward. When the Qur’an was revealed, the weapon was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he returned it to Rifa’ah. Qatada said: When I brought the weapon to my uncle, he was an old man who had lived in the pre-Islamic era, and I thought his Islam was questionable. When I brought him the weapon, he said: O son of my brother, he is in the way of God. He said: Then I knew that his Islam was correct. When the Qur’an was revealed, Bashir joined the polytheists, and it was revealed to Sulafa, the daughter of Sa’d ibn Shahid, and God revealed about him: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers until His saying: And whoever associates others with God has certainly strayed far astray (An-Nisa’: 115-116). When it was revealed to Sulafa, Hassan ibn Thabit threw some verses of poetry at her, so she took his saddlebag and put it on her head, then went out and threw it in the valley, then said: You gave me Hassan’s poetry! You never used to bring me anything good!” Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you, meaning: by that which God has sent down to you and made clear to you, and be not an advocate for the deceitful, then he recited until His saying: Indeed, God does not like anyone who is a treacherous sinner. He mentioned to us that these verses were revealed concerning Tu’mah bin Ubayraq, and when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was about to excuse him, and God explained the matter of Tu’mah bin Ubayraq, and admonished His Prophet and warned him not to be an advocate for the deceitful. Ta'mah ibn Ubayraq was a man from the Ansar, then one of the Banu Thafar. He stole a shield that belonged to his uncle, which was a deposit with him, then threw it at a Jew who used to visit them, whose name was Zayd ibn al-Sameen. The Jew came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, complaining. When his people, Banu Thafar, saw that, they came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to excuse their companion. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was about to excuse him, until God revealed what He revealed concerning him, saying: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves until His saying: Here you are! You argued on their behalf in worldly life, but who will argue on their behalf with God on the Day of Resurrection? He meant his people by that, And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin. Ta'mah had accused an innocent person of it. When God explained the matter of Ta'mah, he became a hypocrite and joined the polytheists in Mecca, so God revealed concerning him. “And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.” (An-Nisa’: 115) Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.” That is because a group of the Ansar went out on a campaign with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the armor of one of them was stolen. I thought it was a man from the Ansar, so the owner of the armor came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Tu’mah bin Ubayraq has stolen my armor. So it was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the thief saw that, he went to it and threw it in the house of an innocent man, and he said to a group of his tribe: I have hidden the armor and thrown it in the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him. They went to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at night and said: O Prophet of God, our companion is innocent, and the thief of the shield is so-and-so, and we have knowledge of that, so excuse our companion in front of the people and argue on his behalf, for unless God protects him through you, he will perish! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and acquitted him and excused him in front of the people, and God revealed: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between the people by that which God has shown you. And be not an advocate for the deceitful.” He said: Judge between them by what God has revealed to you in the Book, “And ask forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves.” Then He said to those who came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, at night: They hide from the people and do not hide from God until His saying: Or who is their guardian? meaning: those who came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, hiding, arguing on behalf of the traitor. Then He said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. meaning: those who came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, hiding with lies. Then He said: And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin. meaning: the thief and those who argue on behalf of the thief. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you the verse, he said: There was a man who stole an iron shield during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and threw it to a Jew. The Jew said: By God, I did not steal it, O Abu al-Qasim, but it was thrown to me! The man who had stolen had neighbors who would exonerate him and throw it to the Jew and say: O Messenger of God, this wicked Jew disbelieves in God and what you have brought! He said: Until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to him with some words, and God, the Almighty, rebuked him for that and said: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And ask forgiveness of God,” for what he said to this Jew - Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Then he turned to his neighbors and said: Here you are, you argued on their behalf in the life of this world. So he recited until he reached Or who can be a guardian over them? He said: Then he presented repentance and said: “And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And whoever earns sin only earns it against himself.” So what brought you, O people, into this sin that you are speaking about without Him? “And God is Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then throws it at an innocent person,” even if he is a polytheist, has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin. So he recited until he reached: There is no good in much of their private conversation. So he recited until he reached: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him (An-Nisa’: 115). He said: He refused to accept the repentance that God presented to him, and he went out to the polytheists in Mecca, and dug into a house to steal, so God destroyed it on him and killed him. This is what God Almighty said: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him (An-Nisa’: 115), and he read until he reached And evil it is as a destination (An-Nisa’: 116). It is said that he is Ta’mah ibn Ubayraq, and he was staying with Banu Thafar. Others said: Rather, the betrayal that God described with the one who described Him in His saying: And do not be an advocate for the traitors, is his denial of a trust that he had entrusted. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. And be not an advocate for the deceitful.” He said: As for that which God has shown you, it is what God has revealed to you. He said: It was revealed about Tu’mah ibn Ubayraq. A Jewish man entrusted him with a shield, so he went with it to his house. The Jew dug a hole for it and then buried it. Tu’mah went back to it, dug it up and took it. When the Jew came asking for his shield, he denied it. So he went to some Jews from his tribe and said: Come with me, for I know where the shield is. When Tu’mah knew about them, he took the shield and threw it in the house of Abu Malil al-Ansari. When the Jews came asking for the shield but could not find it, Tu’mah and some of his people caught up with him and cursed him. He said: Are you betraying me? So they went looking for it in his house, and they looked at the house of Abu Malil, and there they found the shield. Ta'mah said: Abu Malil took it! And I argued with the Ansar on behalf of Ta'mah, and he said to them: Go with me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tell him to refute my argument and to disbelieve the Jew, for if I lie, the Jew will lie to the people of Medina! So some of the Ansar came to him and said: O Messenger of God, argue on behalf of Ta'mah and disbelieve the Jew. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, understood what he should do, so God revealed to him: “And do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And ask forgiveness of God” for what I meant, “Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, God does not like anyone who is a treacherous sinner.” Then he mentioned the Ansar and their argument with him, saying: They hide from the people, but they do not hide from God, and He is with them when they spend the night saying that which does not please Him. He said: They say that which does not please Him. “Here you are, you argued on their behalf in the life of this world. Who will argue on their behalf with God on the Day of Resurrection?” Then he called for repentance, saying: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. Then he mentioned his statement when he said that Abu Mulayl took it, saying: And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself, “And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person has indeed taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin.” Then he mentioned the Ansar and their coming to him, to denounce their companion and argue on his behalf. He said: “A party of them have inspired you to mislead you, but they mislead only themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom,” meaning: prophethood. Then he mentioned their private conversations about what they wanted to lie about Ta’mah, and he said: There is no good in much of their private conversations, except for those who enjoin charity or righteousness or conciliation between people. So when God exposed Ta’mah in Medina with the Quran, he fled until he came to Mecca, and disbelieved after his conversion to Islam, and stayed with Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Alat Al-Sulami, so he dug into Al-Hajjaj’s house, and wanted to rob him, but Al-Hajjaj heard a rustling in his house and the rattling of hides that were with him, so he looked and saw Ta’mah and said: My guest and my cousin, and you wanted to rob me!! So he took him out, and he died in Bahrah Bani Salim as a disbeliever, and God revealed about him: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken to And evil is the destination (An-Nisa’: 115-116).
