Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: A man from the Ansar entrusted a drinking place to Tuma ibn Ubayraq, in which was a shield, and he went out and disappeared. When the Ansari returned, he opened his drinking place, but did not find the shield, so he asked Tuma ibn Ubayraq about it, and he threw it at a Jewish man called Zayd ibn al-Sameen. The owner of the shield clung to Tuma in his shield. When his people saw that, they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him to ward off the evil. They intended to do that, but God Almighty revealed: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. And be not an advocate for the deceitful. And ask forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves.” That is, Tu’mah ibn Ubayraq and his people. “Here you are, you argued on their behalf in the worldly life. But who will argue with God on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?” That is, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of Tu’mah. And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. That is, Muhammad, Tu’mah, and his people. He said: And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. That is, Tu’mah. And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person. That is, Zayd ibn al-Sameen. He has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin. That is, Tu’mah ibn Ubayraq. And had it not been for the favor of God upon you. And His mercy, O Muhammad, A party of them were inspired to mislead you, but they mislead none but themselves, and they do not harm you at all, the people of Ta’mah ibn Ubayraq, “And God has sent down upon you the Book and wisdom and taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of God upon you been great,” O Muhammad, There is no good in much of their private conversation, except for him who enjoins charity or righteousness, until the verse is completed for the people in general, And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, the verse (An-Nisa’: 115). He said: When the Qur’an was revealed about Ta’mah ibn Ubayraq, he joined the Quraysh and returned to his religion, then he passed by a drinking place belonging to Al-Hajjaj ibn ‘Alat Al-Bahzi then Al-Sulami, an ally of Banu ‘Abd Al-Dar, so he dug a hole in it, and a stone fell on him, so he migrated. When morning came, they expelled him from Mecca. He went out and met a group of people from Bahra’ from Quda’ah, and he confronted them and said: A wayfarer is stranded there! So they carried him, until night fell upon him, he attacked them and robbed them, then he left. So they went back in search of him and caught up with him, and they stoned him until he died. Ibn Jurayj said: All of these verses were revealed about him up to the words: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. They were revealed about Tu’mah ibn Ubayraq, and they say that he threw the shield into the house of Abu Malil ibn Abdullah al-Khazraji, and when the Qur’an was revealed, he went to Quraysh, and what happened to him happened. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, That you may judge between people by what God has shown you, meaning: by what He has revealed to you and shown you in His Book. This verse was revealed about a man from the Ansar who was entrusted with a shield and its owner denied it, so some of the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, betrayed him. His people became angry on his behalf and came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, “They have betrayed our companion, and he is a trustworthy Muslim. So excuse him, O Prophet of God, and forbid him!” Then the Prophet of God stood up and excused him and lied about him, seeing that he was innocent and that he had been lied to. So God revealed the explanation of that and said: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by that which God has shown you until His saying: Or who will be a guardian over them? So God revealed his treachery, so he joined the polytheists of Mecca and apostatized from Islam, so the following was revealed about him: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him until His saying: And evil it is as a destination (An-Nisa’: 115-116). Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the two interpretations of this, based on what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the verse, is the statement of those who say: His betrayal, with which God described him in this verse, was his denial of what he entrusted, because that is the well-known meaning of betrayal in the speech of the Arabs. And directing the interpretation of the Qur’an to the most famous meanings of the speech of the Arabs, to which a path was found, is more correct than anything else.
4:107: Abu Ja'far said: By that, God the Most High means: And do not argue O Muhammad, so argue, on behalf of those who betray themselves, meaning: they betray themselves, they make themselves traitors by betraying the money of those who betrayed their money, and they are the Banu Ubayraq. He says: Do not argue on their behalf with those who demand their rights and the money they betrayed them in, Indeed, God does not like anyone who is a treacherous sinner, meaning: God does not like anyone whose characteristic is betraying people in their money, and committing sin in that and other things that God has forbidden for him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: The narration from them has been mentioned previously. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves, he said: A man deceived his uncle with his armor, and threw it at a Jew who used to visit them. The man’s uncle argued with his people, and it was as if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, excused him. Then he went to the land of polytheism, and the verse was revealed about him: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him (An-Nisa’: 115).
4:108: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: They hide from the people, is that these people who betray themselves, what they have done of betrayal, and what they have committed of shame and disobedience, from the people, who are not able to do anything except mention them with the ugly thing they have done of their actions, and the heinous thing they have committed of their crime when they find out about it, out of shame from them and fear of the ugly story, and they do not hide from God, who is aware of them, nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, and in His hand is punishment, chastisement, and hastening the torment, and He is more deserving of being ashamed of than anyone else, and more deserving of being glorified by not seeing them where they would hate for any of His creation to see them, and He is with them, meaning: and God is watching them, when they plan by night what is not pleasing of speech, meaning: when they do by night what is not pleasing of speech, changing it from its intended meaning, and lying in it. We have explained the meaning of staying overnight in other places, and that it is any speech or matter that is best done at night. It was narrated from some of the Ta’i people that in their language, tabayt means exchange. And he recited the following verse by Al-Aswad bin Aamer bin Juwain Al-Ta’i in his reproach to a man: And my saying, Abdul Malik, may God kill you, you ungrateful slave!! Meaning: I changed my words. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Razin that he used to say, in the meaning of his saying: they spend the night, that they compose. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Razin: When they plot unacceptable words, he said: They compose unacceptable words. Ahmad bin Sinan Al-Wasiti told us, he said, Abu Yahya Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Razin, something similar. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Razin, the same. Abu Jaafar said: This statement is similar in meaning to what we have said. That is because composition is equalization and change from what it is, and transforming it from its meaning to something else. It has been said: What he meant by his saying: They hide from the people but do not hide from God is the group who went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the matter of defending and arguing on behalf of Ibn Ubayraq, as we mentioned before in what has passed from Ibn Abbas and others. And God is encompassing of what they do. He, may His praise be glorified, means: And God is encompassing of what these people who are belittling them do, in what they have committed of their crime, out of shame from them, from their concealing what is not pleasing of speech and other actions of theirs, encompassing, counting and nothing of it is hidden from Him, preserving that for them, until He rewards them for it with their reward.
4:109: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Here you are, you argued for them in the life of this world, is that here you are the ones who argued, O group who argued for Banu Abiriq, in the life of this world. The ha’ and the mim in His statement: for them are from the mention of the traitors. So who will argue with God on their behalf? He says: Who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection? That is, the day when people will rise from their graves for their gathering, and He will defend on their behalf what God will do to them and punish them with. What He means by that is that you, the defenders of these traitors themselves, even if you defend them in this worldly life, they will in the Hereafter be with someone before whom no one will defend them in the painful torment and humiliating punishment that will befall them. As for his saying: Or who will be a guardian over them?, he means: Who is the one who will be a guardian over these traitors on the Day of Resurrection? That is: Who will be their guardian in their dispute with their Lord on the Day of Resurrection? We have previously explained the meaning of agency, which is carrying out the task of the one to whom it is entrusted.
4:110: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And whoever commits a sin, which is evil, or wrongs himself, by causing himself to deserve God’s punishment, then seeks God’s forgiveness, meaning: then repents to God by turning back to Him for what he has done of evil and wronging himself, and reviewing what God loves of righteous deeds that erase his sin and remove his crime, will find God Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: he will find his Lord covering his sin by pardoning him for the punishment of his crime, merciful to him. The interpreters differed about who was meant by this verse. Some of them said: It refers to those whom God described as traitors when He said: And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Others said: Rather, he meant by it those who were arguing on behalf of the traitors, to whom God said: Here you are, you argued on their behalf in worldly life. We have mentioned those who said both statements previously. Abu Jaafar said: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is that it refers to everyone who has done evil or wronged himself, even though it was revealed regarding the traitors and those who disputed on their behalf, whose matter God mentioned in the verses before it. A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said, Abdullah said: When one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would wake up with the expiation for that sin written on his door. When urine got on some of it, he would cut it off with scissors. A man said: God has given the Children of Israel good! Abdullah said: What God has given you is better than what He has given them. God has made water a means of purification for you. He said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins (Al Imran 3:135), and He said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: A woman came to Abdullah ibn Mughaffal and asked him about a woman who committed adultery and became pregnant, and when she gave birth she killed her child. Ibn Mughaffal said: What is wrong with her? Hellfire is hers! So she left crying, and he called her and said: I do not see your case as being one of two things: Whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. He said: So she wiped her eye and went away. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful, he said: God informed His servants of His forbearance, pardon, and generosity, and the breadth of His mercy and forgiveness. So whoever commits a sin, whether small or great, and then seeks forgiveness from God, will find God Forgiving and Merciful, even if his sins were greater than the heavens, the earth, and the mountains.
4:111: Abu Ja'far said: By that, the Most High means: And whoever commits a sin intentionally and knowingly, then he only brings the consequences of that sin, its harm, its shame and its disgrace upon himself, and not upon anyone else among the rest of God's creation. He says: So do not argue, O you who argue, on behalf of these traitors, for even if you are their clan, relatives and neighbors, you are innocent of the sin they have committed and of the responsibility for which they will be followed, because whenever you defend them or argue because of them, you will be like them, so do not defend them and do not argue. As for his saying: And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, it means: And God is All-Knowing of what you do, O you who argue on behalf of those who betray yourselves, in your argument on behalf of them and other actions of yours and the actions of others, and He counts them against you and against them, until He rewards all of you for them. Wise, he says: And He is All-Wise in your politics and your management and the management of all of His creation. It was said: This verse was revealed about Banu Abiriq. We have mentioned those who said that before.
4:112: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And whoever commits a sin, which is a crime, or a crime, and that is what is not permissible of disobedience. The difference between sin and guilt is that sin can be intentional or unintentional, while guilt can only be intentional. Therefore, God Almighty distinguished between them by saying: And whoever commits a sin unintentionally or a crime intentionally. “Then he throws it away innocently,” meaning: then he attributes to him what he has of his mistake or sin that he deliberately committed, innocent of what he attributed to him and attributed to him, then he has borne a slander and a manifest sin, meaning: by doing that he has borne a slander, a lie, and a great sin, meaning, and a great crime, knowingly and deliberately for what he did of his disobedience and sin. The people of interpretation differed about who God meant by His saying: innocent, after they all agreed that the one who accused the innocent of the sin that he had committed was Ibn Ubayraq, whose situation we described before. Some of them said: God Almighty meant by the innocent a man from the Muslims called Labid bin Sahl. Others said: Rather, he meant a Jewish man called Zaid bin Al-Sameen, and we mentioned the narration that he said that previously. Among those who said: He was Jewish, is Ibn Sirin. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: Then he throws it at an innocent person, he said: a Jew. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Badal bin Al-Muhabir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, the same. It was said: He throws it at an innocent person, meaning: Then he throws the sin that this traitor committed at someone who is innocent of what he threw at him. So the ha in his saying: at it refers back to the sin. If it was made a metaphorical phrase from mentioning the sin and the error, it would be permissible, because the actions, even if the expressions about them differ, return to one meaning, which is that they are an action. As for his saying: He has borne a slander and a manifest sin, its meaning is: This one who accused what he committed of disobedience and committed a sin, who is innocent of what he accused him of, has borne a slander, which is a lie and a lie, and a manifest sin, meaning: a manifest sin, meaning: he reveals the matter of his burden and his audacity towards his Lord, and his going ahead in contradicting Him in what He forbade him from doing to those who know his matter.
4:113: Abu Ja`far said: What He means by His saying, may He be glorified: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, and had it not been that God had been kind to you, O Muhammad, and had protected you with His guidance and clarification of the matter of this traitor, so that you would have refrained from arguing about him and defending the people of truth from their right before him, a party of them would have been determined, meaning: a group of them would have been determined, meaning: of those who betray themselves, to mislead you, meaning: to make you stray from the path of truth, and that is because they confuse the matter of the traitor with him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and testify for the traitor before him that he is innocent of what was claimed against him, and ask him to excuse him and stand up for his excuse in his companions, so God, may He be blessed and exalted, said: And none misleads those who intended to mislead you from the duty of judgment in the matter of this traitor, the shield of his neighbor, except themselves. If someone says: What was the reason for their misleading themselves? It was said: The reason for their misleading themselves is that they took them in ways other than what God had permitted them to take them in from His paths. This is because God, the Most High, had previously preceded them in His Book through the tongue of His Messenger to His creation, with the prohibition of cooperating in sin and aggression, and the command to cooperate in the truth. So it was obligatory for God, with regard to those who sought to deal with the traitors, whose matter God described in His saying: And do not be an advocate for the traitors, to assist those whom they wronged, rather than those who argued with them before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in seeking their right from them. So their seeking to assist them, rather than assisting those whom they wronged, was taking from them in ways other than God’s path. And this is their misleading themselves, which God described when He said: And they mislead none but themselves. “And they will not harm you at all,” and those who intended to lead you astray from the truth in the matter of this traitor from his people and clan, will not harm you at all, because God is making you steadfast and directing you in your affairs, and making clear to you the matter of those who sought to mislead you from the truth in his matter and their matter, so expose them and them. And His saying: And God has sent down upon you the Book and wisdom, meaning: And from the favor of God upon you, O Muhammad, along with all the other favors He has bestowed upon you, is that He sent down upon you the Book, which is the Qur’an in which is an explanation of everything and guidance and admonition, and wisdom, meaning: And He sent down upon you along with the Book wisdom, which is what was mentioned in the Book in general terms, from His lawful and unlawful, His commands and prohibitions, His rulings, His promises and His threats, and taught you what you did not know, from the report of the first and the last, and what was and what will be. All of that is from the favor of God upon you, O Muhammad, since He created you, so thank Him for what He has bestowed upon you of His kindness to you, by adhering to His obedience, hastening to His pleasure and love, and adhering to what He has sent down to you in His Book and wisdom, and opposing whoever tries to misguide you from His path and the method of His religion, for God is the One Who takes care of you with His favor, and He will suffice you against the misfortune of whoever wants to harm you and tries to turn you away from His path, just as He sufficed you with the matter of the group that… She wanted to lead you astray from His path through the affair of this traitor. And no one but Him can save you from the evil he intended for you, if you disobeyed Him in any of His commands and prohibitions, and followed the whims of the one who tried to turn you away from His path. This verse is a warning from God to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to correct his mistake, and a reminder from Him of what is required of him regarding his right.
4:114: Abu Ja`far said: What God Almighty means by His saying: There is no good in much of their private conversation, is that there is no good in much of the private conversation of all people, except for those who enjoin charity or righteousness, and righteousness is everything that God has commanded or encouraged of righteous and good deeds, or reconciliation between people, which is reconciliation between those who differ or dispute, by what God has permitted reconciliation between them, so that they may return to what brings harmony and unity of word, according to what God has permitted and commanded. Then He, the Most High, informed us of what He promised to whoever does that, saying: And whoever does that, seeking the pleasure of God - We will surely give him a great reward. He says: And whoever enjoins charity or a good deed, or makes peace between people, seeking the pleasure of God, meaning: seeking the pleasure of God by doing that, We will surely give him a great reward. He says: We will give him a great reward for what he did of that, and there is no limit to the amount of what God called great that anyone but He knows. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of his saying: There is no good in much of their private conversation, except for those who enjoin charity. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of this is: There is no good in much of their secret conversation, except in the secret conversation of someone who orders charity, as if he had connected min to the ha’ and mim in their secret conversation. This is a mistake according to the Arabs, because illa is not connected to the ha’ and the mim in such a situation, because it was not denied. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Min may be in the accusative or genitive cases. As for the genitive case, it is based on your saying: There is no good in much of their private conversations except for one who is commanded to give charity. So the private conversation, according to this interpretation, is the men who are talking privately, as God, the Most High, said: There is not a private conversation between three but that He is the fourth of them (Al-Mujadilah: 7), and as He said: And when they are talking privately (al-Isra’ 17:47). As for the accusative, it is based on making the whispering a verb, so it is accusative, because then it is a discontinuous exception, because it is contrary to the whispering, so that is similar to the poet’s saying. I stood there in the evening asking her questions, but she couldn’t give me an answer, and there was no one in the room Except that I hide it for no reason, and distance is like a pool that covers the skin of the oppressed. It may be possible that this interpretation is a nominative, as the poet said: A town with no companions except the camels and the wild donkeys Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings is to put min in the accusative case, in response to al-Najwa, and al-Najwa would mean gathering those whispering, as in the case of drunks, wounded people, and patients. This is because its meanings are clearer. The interpretation of the statement is: There is no good in many of the people who whisper to each other, O Muhammad, except for those who command charity, goodness, or reconciliation between people, for there is good in those.
4:115: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: And whoever contradicts the Messenger, and whoever opposes the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, being hostile to him, and departs from him out of hostility to him, after guidance has become clear to him, meaning: after it has become clear to him that he is the Messenger of God, and that what he brought from God guides to the truth and to a straight path, and follows a path other than the way of the believers, meaning: and follows a path other than the path of the people of belief, and takes a path other than their path, and that is disbelief in God, because disbelief in God and His Messenger is not the path of the believers and not their path, We will give him what he has taken, meaning: We will make as his supporter what he sought for help and assistance from of idols and statues, and they will not benefit him or ward off from him anything from the punishment of God, nor will they benefit him, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: We will give him what he has taken, he said: of the gods of falsehood. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And We will burn him in Hell, meaning: We will burn him in it. We have explained the meaning of the word sali previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. And what an evil destination, he says, and what an evil destination is Hell, “a place to which whoever goes to it will go.” This verse was revealed about the traitors whom God mentioned in His saying: And do not be an advocate for the traitors, when one of them, namely Tu’mah ibn al-Ubayraq, refused to repent and joined the polytheists who worshipped idols in Mecca, apostatizing and abandoning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his religion.
4:116: Abu Ja'far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means that God does not forgive Ta'mah if he associated partners with God and died as such, nor does He forgive any of His creation for their association and disbelief in Him. But He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. He says: And He forgives what is less than associating partners with God of sins for whomever He wills. By that, may His praise be exalted, He means that if Ta'mah had not associated partners with God and died as such, he would have been in God's will for his previous betrayal and disobedience, and his affair with God would be in his punishment and forgiveness of him. And likewise, the ruling for everyone who commits a crime, his affair is with God, unless his crime is associating partners with God and disbelief, then he is one of those who are destined to be among the people of Hell if he dies as such. But if he dies as such, God has forbidden him Paradise and his abode is Hell. Al-Saddī said about this: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills, meaning: whoever among the Muslims avoids major sins. As for his statement: And whoever associates others with God has certainly strayed far astray, it means: And whoever makes a partner for God in his worship has strayed far from the path of truth and has deviated from the straight path, a far departure and a severe deviation. That is because by associating others with God in his worship, he has obeyed Satan and followed his path, and abandoned the obedience of God and the path of His religion. That is the far straying and the clear loss.
4:117: Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: They call upon none besides Him except Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat. So God called them females, just as the polytheists called them females. Who said that? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding his statement: They invoke not besides Him except female deities, he said: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, all of them feminine. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik, something similar, except that he said: All of them are feminine. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: They invoke besides Him only female deities, meaning: They call them female deities: Lat, Manat, and Uzza. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, They invoke none but female deities besides Him, he said: Their deities, Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, Yasaf, and Na’ilah, are females, they invoke them besides God. They invoke none but a rebellious devil. Others said: The meaning of this is: They call upon nothing besides Him except death, in which there is no life. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They invoke besides Him only female deities, meaning: dead. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They invoke besides Him only female deities, meaning: except a dead person with no soul in him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: They invoke besides Him only female deities, he said: And female deities are everything dead that has no soul: dry wood or dry stone. God Almighty said: And they invoke only a rebellious devil, until His saying: Then let them cut off the ears of the cattle. Others said: He meant by that that the polytheists used to say: The angels are daughters of God. Who said that? Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: They invoke not besides Him except female deities, he said: The angels, they claim that they are the daughters of God. Others said: The meaning of this is that the idolaters used to call their idols females, so God revealed this in the same way. Who said that? Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Noah bin Qais, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Every tribe of the Arabs had an idol, which they called: the female of the Banu So-and-so, so God revealed: They do not invoke besides Him except female deities. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Noah bin Qais told us, he said, Muhammad bin Saif Abu Raja Al-Hadani told us, he said, I heard Al-Hasan say: Every tribe of the Arabs had, and he mentioned something similar. Others said: The females in this place are idols. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: females, he said: idols. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said: In Aisha’s copy of the Qur’an was: They invoke not besides Him except female deities. Abu Ja`far said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: They invoke besides Him only idols, meaning the plural of idols, as if he had pluralized idols, then he changed the waw to a damma hamza, as it was said: How beautiful are these faces, meaning faces, and as it was said: And when the messengers are appointed (al-Mursalat 77:11), meaning: they are appointed. It was mentioned that some of them used to recite this: They invoke besides Him only females, as if he wanted to gather the females, so he gathered them into female, just as fruits are gathered into fruit. Abu Ja`far said: The reading that we do not permit reading other than it is the reading of those who read: They invoke besides Him only females, meaning the plural of female, because it is like that in the copies of the Muslims’ Qur’ans, and because of the consensus of the evidence on reading it like that. Abu Ja`far said: The most appropriate interpretation that was mentioned is the interpretation of that, since the correct reading for us is what I described, the interpretation of the one who said: What was meant by that were the deities that the polytheists of the Arabs worshipped instead of God and called them by female names, such as al-Lat, al-`Uzza, Na`ilah, Manat, and the like. We said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because the most apparent meaning of females in the speech of the Arabs is what is known as feminine and not otherwise. So since this is the case, it is necessary to direct its interpretation to the most common of its meanings. Since this is the case, the interpretation of the verse: “And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.” They invoke not besides Him except female deities, meaning: Those who contradict the Messenger and follow other than the way of the believers invoke not anything, besides God, after God and other than Him, except female deities, meaning: except what they call by female names such as Al-Lat and Al-Uzza and the like. God, the Most High, says: It is sufficient for those who associate partners with God and worship what they worship other than Him of idols and rivals, as proof against them of their misguidance, disbelief, and deviation from the right path, that they worship female deities and call them gods and lords. And females are the most vile of all things, so they acknowledge the worship of the most vile of things, knowing their vileness, and they refrain from sincerely worshipping the One to Whom belongs the dominion of all things, and in Whose hand is creation and command. Abu Ja`far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: And they call upon none but a rebellious devil. And these people who call upon these female idols besides God, by calling upon them, call upon none but a rebellious devil, meaning: one who rebels against God in contradicting what He has commanded him to do and what He has forbidden him to do, such as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they invoke none but a rebellious devil, he said: He rebelled against the sins of God.
4:118: Abu Jaafar said: By His saying, May God curse him, He meant to disgrace him, banish him, and distance him. The meaning of the words: They invoke none but a rebellious devil, whom God has cursed and kept far from all good. And he said, ‘I will surely take,’ meaning that the rebellious devil said to his Lord when he cursed him: I will surely take from among Your servants a prescribed portion. It means that it is supposed to be known, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: A prescribed share, he said: known. If someone says: How can Satan take a specific portion of God’s servants? It was said: He takes that portion from them, by tempting them away from the straight path, calling them to obey Him, and beautifying for them misguidance and disbelief until He removes them from the path of the way. So whoever answers His call and follows what He beautifies for him, then he is from His known portion and His allotted share. Rather, God Almighty informed us in this verse of what He informed us about Satan, when He said: I will surely take from among Your servants a prescribed portion, so that those who opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them would know that they are from the prescribed portion of Satan, whom God has cursed, and that they are among those about whom his suspicions were true. We have already explained the meaning of the curse, so we did not want to repeat it.
4:119: Abu Ja`far said: By His statement, may His praise be exalted, informing about what the rebellious Satan said, whose description was described in this verse: And I will surely mislead them, and I will divert the prescribed portion that I have taken from Your servants from the path of guidance to misguidance, and from Islam to disbelief, and I will arouse in them false hopes, meaning: I will deviate them - by what I put in their souls of false hopes - from Your obedience and monotheism to My obedience and associating partners with You, and I will command them to slit the ears of cattle, meaning: I will command the prescribed portion of Your servants to worship other than You from idols and rivals until they worship for Him, and forbid and permit for Him, and legislate other than what You legislated for them, so they follow Me and oppose You. And the word batak means to cut, and in this case it means cutting off the ear of the lake to show that it is a lake. What the wicked one meant by that was that he would invite them to the lake, and they would respond to him and work there in obedience to him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Then let them cut the ears of the cattle, he said: The cutting refers to the bahīrah and the sā’ibah. They used to cut their ears for their tyrants. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: He said: And I will command them to slit the ears of cattle. They will not slit the ears of cattle, they will slit them and make them into a lake. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza told me, on the authority of Ikrimah: So let the ears of the cattle be cut off, he said: A religion that Satan legislated for them, like the form of the lakes and the sib. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying: So let them change the creation of God. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: I will command them to change God’s creation of animals by castrating them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ammar bin Abi Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he disliked castration and said: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God was revealed about it. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdullah bin Dawud told us, he said, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Anas: that he disliked castration and said: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God was revealed about it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: It is castration, meaning the statement of God: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, he said: A man told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Castrating animals is mutilation! Then he recited: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Abu Ja`far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` bin Anas, he said: Among the ways of changing God’s creation is castration. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ja`far bin Sulayman told us, he said, Shabil told me: that he heard Shahr bin Hawshab recite this verse: So let them change the creation of God. He said: Castration. He said: So I ordered Abu al-Tiyah to ask al-Hasan about castrating sheep, and he said: There is nothing wrong with it. Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, my uncle Wahb ibn Nafi’ told us, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, he said: Mujahid ordered me to ask Ikrimah about his statement: So they will change the creation of God, so I asked him, and he said: It is castration. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, my father narrated, on the authority of Abdul-Jabbar bin Ward, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, who said: Mujahid said to me: Ask Ikrimah about it: And I will command them to change the creation of God. So I asked him and he said: Castration. Mujahid said: What is wrong with him, may God curse him! By God, he knew that he changed castration. Then he said: Ask him. So I asked him and Ikrimah said: Haven’t you heard the saying of God, the Most High: “The nature of God in which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God” [ar-Rum 30]? He said: The religion of God. So I told it to Mujahid and he said: What is wrong with him, may God disgrace him! Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Laith, he said, Ikrimah said: So let them change the creation of God, he said: castration. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Harun al-Nahwi told us, he said, Matar al-Warraq told us, he said, Ikrimah was asked about his statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: It is castration. Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh, who said: Castration. Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, he said: I heard Anas bin Malik say regarding His statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: Among them is castration. Amr told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah: that he disliked castration. He said: And in it was revealed: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God. Others said: The meaning of this is: I will command them to change the religion of God. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman and Abu Ahmad told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn al-Salam, on the authority of Ibrahim: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, Qais bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Naim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, my uncle told us, on the authority of al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, he said, I told Mujahid about the words of Ikrimah regarding his statement: So let them change the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Harun al-Nahwi told us, he said, Matar al-Warraq told us, he said, I mentioned to Mujahid what Ikrimah said about His statement: So they will change the creation of God, so he said: The servant has lied! And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: The religion of God. Ibn Wakee’ and Amr ibn Ali told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, who said: The religion of God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi and Hafs told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The religion of God. Then he recited: That is the right religion (al-Rum 30:30). Muhammad bin Amr and Amr bin Ali told us, they said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So let them change the creation of God, he said: The fitrah, the religion of God. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So let them change the creation of God, he said: the nature, the religion. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Abdullah bin Katheer told me: He heard Mujahid say: And I will command them to change the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, meaning: the religion of God, according to Al-Hasan and Qatada. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: So let them change the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, regarding his statement: So let them change the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And I will command them to change the creation of God. He said: As for the creation of God, it is the religion of God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: So let them change the creation of God, he said: The religion of God, which is the statement of God: “The nature of God in which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God” (al-Rum 30:30), he said: The religion of God. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, I heard Ibn Zayd say about His statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: The religion of God. And he recited: There is no changing the creation of God, he said: The religion of God. Amr bin Ali told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, Qais bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Ibrahim: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: God’s religion. Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Muadh bin Muadh told us, he said, Imran bin Hadhir told us, on the authority of Isa bin Hilal, he said: Kathir, the freed slave of Ibn Samurah, wrote to Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim asking him about his statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, so he wrote: It is the religion of God. Others said: The meaning of this is: And I will command them to change God’s creation by tattooing. Who said that? Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God, he said: tattooing. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Nuh bin Qais, on the authority of Khalid bin Qais, on the authority of Al-Hasan: So let them change the creation of God, he said: tattoos. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Yunus bin Ubaid or someone else told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: So let them change the creation of God, he said: tattoos. Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Abu Hilal al-Rasibi told us: A man asked al-Hasan: What do you say about a woman who peels her face? He said: What is wrong with her? May God curse her! She has changed God’s creation. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Abdullah said: God cursed those who file their teeth, pluck their eyebrows, and get tattoos, changing God’s creation. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: God cursed the women who pluck eyebrows, those who get tattooed, those who have their eyebrows plucked, and those who file their teeth for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: God cursed those who shorten their hair and file their teeth. Shu`bah said: I think he said: The dusty ones are God’s creation. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God. He said: The religion of God. This is because the other verse indicates that this is its meaning, which is His statement: “The nature of God in which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God. That is the right religion.” (al-Rum 30:30) If that is what it means, then it includes doing everything that God has forbidden: castrating what is not permissible to castrate, branding what He has forbidden to brand and tattoo, and other sins. It also includes abandoning everything that God has commanded. Because there is no doubt that Satan calls to all sins against God and forbids all obedience to Him. So that is the meaning of his command to his obligatory portion of God’s servants, to change what God has created of His religion. Abu Ja`far said: There is no point in interpreting the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): And I will command them to change the creation of God, to the effect that he promised the one who commanded to change some of what God forbade but not others, or some of what he commanded but not others. If the one who interpreted the meaning of that to castration and tattooing but not others, did so because he meant changing bodies, then in His statement, may He be glorified, there is information about what Satan said: And I will command them to slit the ears of cattle, which indicates that the meaning of that is not what he intended. Because slitting the ears of cattle is changing the creation of God, which is bodies. The report about him that he promised the one who commanded to change the creation of God of bodies has already been explained, so there is no reason to repeat the report about him in a general way, since the eloquent way in the speech of the Arabs is to translate the general from the general to the specific, without interpreting the general from the specific to the specific. Directing the Book of God to the most eloquent speech is more appropriate than directing it to something else, as long as the path to it is found. Abu Ja`far said: This is report from God, the Most High, about the fate of the devil, who opposed God and His Messenger after guidance had become clear to them. God says: And whoever follows Satan, obeying him in disobeying God and opposing His command, and befriends him and takes him as a protector and helper for himself instead of God, has certainly suffered a clear loss. He says: He has perished utterly, and has cheated himself out of it, clearly. It explains his failure and destruction, because Satan does not possess any support from God if He punishes him for his disobedience to Him in opposing His command. Rather, He abandons him when he needs it. His condition with him is only as long as he is alive, and he is given respite for the punishment.
4:120: As God, the Most High, described him by saying: He promises them and arouses false hopes in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion. By that, the Most High, means: Satan, the wicked, promises his allies who are his appointed portion: that he will be a supporter for them against those who wish them harm and a backer for them against him, preventing them from him and defending them, and arousing in them the hope of victory over those who attempt to harm them and their success. Then he said: And Satan promises them nothing but delusion, meaning: And Satan promises his allies who have taken him as a guardian instead of God, nothing but delusion, meaning: nothing but falsehood. And He, the Most High, made His promise to them deception, because they thought that in taking him as a friend, they were actually counting on his false promises and false hopes. Then, when the truth became clear and they needed him, the enemy of God said to them: “Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot be your savior, nor can you be my savior. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before.” (Ibrahim 14:22) And as He said to the polytheists at Badr, and He had made their deeds seem good to them: No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am your protector. But when the two armies came into sight of one another, and the truth became clear, and he witnessed the seriousness of the matter and the descent of God’s punishment upon his party, “He turned on his heels and said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear God, and God is severe in penalty.’” (al-Anfal 8:48), so his enemies, God’s enemies to them when they needed Him, became deceitful: “Like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty man thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it is nothing. But he finds God with him, and He will pay him his due.” (al-Nur 24:39)
4:121: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Those, is those who took Satan as a friend instead of God. Their refuge is Hell, meaning: their destination is Hell, and they will not find any escape from it, meaning: they will not find any alternative to Hell - if God sends them to it on the Day of Resurrection. It is said: So-and-so turned away from this matter, if he turned away from it. And from it is the hadith of Ibn Omar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a raiding party, and I was among them. We encountered the polytheists and we fought a fierce battle. Some of them said: They fought a fierce battle, and the fighting and the fighting are close in meaning.
4:122: Abu Ja`far said: He, the Most High, meant by His statement: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds, and those who believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged His Oneness, and the Prophethood of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and did righteous deeds, meaning: and performed the obligations God imposed upon them, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, meaning: We will admit them on the Day of Resurrection when they have come to God, as a reward for what they did in this world of righteous deeds, gardens, meaning: orchards, under which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, meaning: remaining in these gardens that He described, forever, always. And they said: The promise of God is true, meaning: a promise from God to them in this world, truly, meaning: a true certainty, not like the false promise of Satan which is a deception to those he promises to his followers, but it is a promise from one who does not lie, lies are not from him, and he does not break his promise. Rather, the Most High described His promise as truthful and right in this, because of what preceded from His report, the Most High, about the statement of Satan, which He related in His statement: “And he said, ‘I will surely take from among Your servants a specified portion. And I will surely mislead them and arouse in them false desires and I will command them to slit the ears of cattle.’” Then the Most High said, “He promises them and arouses false desires in them. But Satan promises them nothing but delusion.” But God promises those who believe and do righteous deeds that He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, a promise from Him that is true, not like the promise of Satan whose description He described. So He, the Most High, described the two promises and the ones who made the promises, and informed us of the ruling on the people of each promise, as a reminder from Him, the Most High, to His creation of what is in their best interest and their salvation from destruction and ruin, so that they may be deterred from disobeying Him and work in obedience to Him, and so that they may win what He has prepared for them in His gardens of reward. Then He, the Most High, said to them: And who is more truthful than God in statement? He says: Who, O people, is more truthful than God in statement? That is, no one is more truthful than Him in statement! So how can you abandon working with what your Lord has promised you for working with it, gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide forever, and disbelieve in Him and disobey His command, while you know that no one is more truthful than Him in statement, and you do what Satan commands you to do in the hope of achieving what he promises you of false promises and vain desires, while you know that his promises are delusions that have no truth or reality, and you take him as a friend instead of God, and you abandon obeying God in what He commands you to do and forbids you from, so that you become His friends? The meaning of qayl and qawl is the same.
4:123: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed about those meant by his saying: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book. Some of them said: What he meant by his saying, It is not according to your desires, are the people of Islam. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, he said: The Christians and the Muslims boasted, and some said: We are better than you! And those said: We are better than you! He said: Then God revealed: It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, he said: When the verse, It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture, was revealed, the People of the Scripture said: We and you are the same! Then this verse was revealed: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer. Abu Al-Sa'ib and Ibn Wakee' told me: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, regarding His statement: It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture, he said: The Muslims and the People of the Scripture argued, and the Muslims said: We are better guided than you! And the People of the Scripture said: We are better guided than you! So God revealed: It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture, he said: So the Muslims defeated them with this verse: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer, to the end of the two verses. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Book were boasting, and the People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet, and our Book came before your Book, and we are closer to God than you! The Muslims said: We are closer to God than you, our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes the books that came before it! So God revealed: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” until His saying: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? So God made the Muslims’ argument successful against those of the people of other religions who opposed them. Muhammad bin Al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad bin Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” He said: Some Jews and Christians met, and the Jews said to the Muslims: We are better than you, our religion came before your religion, our book came before your book, and our prophet came before your prophet, and we are on the religion of Abraham, and no one will enter Paradise except those who are Jews! The Christians said the same, and the Muslims said: Our book comes after your book, and a prophet comes after your prophet, and you have been commanded to follow us and abandon your affairs, so we are better than you, we are on the religion of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, and no one will enter Paradise except those who are on our religion! God responded to their statement and said: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” Then God preferred the believers, the All-Knowing, and said: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God, while being a doer of good, and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj who said, I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” the people of religions disputed. The people of the Torah said, Our book is the first book and the best of them, and our Prophet is the best of the Prophets! The people of the Gospel said something similar to that, and the people of Islam said, “There is no religion but the religion of Islam, and our book abrogates every book, and our Prophet is the seal of the Prophets, and we have been commanded to act according to our book and believe in your book.” So God judged between them and said, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” then He chose between the people of religions and favored the people of virtue and said, And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God while being a doer of good? until His statement, And God took Abraham as a friend. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: It is not according to your desires, nor the desires of the People of the Scripture, to: nor a helper, the people of religions were brought to trial. The people of the Torah said: Our book is the best of books, it was revealed before your book, and our Prophet is the best of prophets. The people of the Gospel said the same, and the people of Islam said: There is no religion but Islam, our book abrogated every book, and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets. You were commanded and we were commanded to believe in your book and act according to our book! So God judged between them and said: “It is not according to your desires, nor the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” and He chose between the people of religions and said: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And God took Abraham as a friend. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ya`la bin Ubayd and Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, he said: A group of people from the people of the Torah, the people of the Gospel, and the people of faith sat down. Some of them said: We are better! And some of them said: We are better! Then God revealed: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” Then God singled out the people of faith, saying: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, he said: The people of the Torah, the people of the Gospel, and the people of the Psalms sat and boasted. Some of them said: We are better! And those of them said: We are better! And those of them said: We are better! So God revealed: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, as much as the speck on a date seed. Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Yazid told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding His statement: It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture, he said: The people of religions boasted, so the Jews said: Our book is the best of books and the most honored of them to God, and our Prophet is the most honored of the prophets to God. God spoke to Moses before, and He spoke to him privately, and our religion is the best of religions! The Christians said: Jesus, son of Mary, is the seal of the messengers, and God gave him the Torah and the Gospel, and if Moses had lived to see him, he would have followed him, and our religion is the best of religions! The Magians and the infidel Arabs said: Our religion is the oldest and best of religions! The Muslims said: Our Prophet Muhammad is the seal of the prophets and the master of the prophets, and the Furqan is the last of the books revealed from God, and He is the trustee of every book, and Islam is the best of religions! So God chose between them and said: It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Others said: Rather, God meant by His saying: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book, the people who associate partners with Him from among the idol worshippers. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Scripture, he said: Quraysh, they said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: It is not according to your desires, he said: Quraysh said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished, so God revealed: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” he said: The Arabs said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished, and the Jews and Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian (Al-Baqarah 2:111), or they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days (Al-Baqarah 2:85), Abu Bishr was not sure. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book, Quraysh and Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: I heard Ibn Zayd say about His statement: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture, to the end of the verse, he said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab came to the polytheists and they said to him: O Huyayy, you are People of the Book, so are we better or Muhammad and his companions? He said: We and you are better than him! That is what His statement: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture, to His statement: And he whom God curses, you will never find for him a helper. (An-Nisa’: 51-52). Then he said to the polytheists: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Scripture, and he recited until he reached: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, they will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even as much as a speck on a date stone, he said: And God promised the believers that He would remove from them their misdeeds, but He did not promise those, and he recited: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do. (An-Ankabut: 7). Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” he said: Quraysh said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished! Others said: It refers to the People of the Book in particular. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book the verse, he said: It was revealed about the People of the Book when they disobeyed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the two interpretations in this regard is what Mujahid said: that he meant by his saying: not according to your desires, the polytheists of Quraysh. We said that this is more correct, because the Muslims’ desires were not mentioned in the previous verses before His saying: It is not according to your desires. Rather, the desires of the devil’s share were mentioned, and that is in His saying: And I will arouse their desires and command them to slit the ears of cattle, and His saying: He promises them and arouses their desires. So attaching the meaning of His saying, may He be glorified: It is not according to your desires to what was mentioned before, is more right and more appropriate than claiming an interpretation of it, for which there is no evidence from the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor a trace from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor a consensus from the people of interpretation. And since that is the case, then the interpretation of the verse is: The matter is not according to your desires, O group of the allies of Satan and his party, which your friend, the enemy of God, is hoping for, of saving you from whoever wants to harm you, and of supporting you against him and making you triumph over him, nor are the desires of the People of the Book who said, deceived by God and His forbearance towards them: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days (al-Baqarah 2:80), and None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian (al-Baqarah 2:111), for God will reward every worker among you according to his work, whoever among you does evil, and whoever is not among you, will be rewarded for it, and he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper, and whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise. What indicates the correctness of what we have said in the interpretation of that, and that He meant by His statement, not by your desires, the polytheists of the Arabs, as Mujahid said: that God described the promise of Satan as He promised his allies and informed of the state of his promise, then He followed that with the description of His true promise by saying, “And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. The promise of God is true.” And God, the Most High, mentioned, along with His description of the promise of Satan to His allies, His wishing them wishes by His statement, He promises them and arouses in them hopes, just as He mentioned His promise to them. So what is more likely is that He follows His wishing them from the description with the same as He made His promise to them from the description. Since this is the case, it is correct that His statement, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it” verse, is only a statement from God about the desires of the allies of Satan. And what their desires will lead to, with their evil deeds of evil recompense, and what the deeds of God’s allies will lead to of good recompense. And the Most High included the People of the Scripture with the polytheists in His statement, It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture, because the desires of both groups are from Satan’s desires for them, which He promised them that He would give them desires with His statement, And I will surely mislead them, and arouse in them desires, and I will command them to do so. Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: By evil he meant every sin of his tongue. They said: The meaning of the verse is: Whoever commits a small or large sin of God, whether a believer or a disbeliever, God will punish him for it. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: that Al-Rabi’ bin Ziyad asked Ibn Ka’b about this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, so he said: I did not see you except as more knowledgeable than I see! The calamity, the return, and the scratch. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Hisham Al-Dastawai, he said, Qatada told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Ziyad, he said: I said to Ubayy bin Ka’b: The statement of God, the Blessed and Exalted: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, by God, if we were recompensed for everything we did, we would be destroyed! He said: By God, I think you are more knowledgeable than I see! A man is not afflicted with a scratch or a stumble except for a sin, and what God pardons is more, even a sting or a sneeze. Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Marouf told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Hajjaj al-Sawaaf, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu al-Muhallab, who said: I entered upon Aisha to ask her about this verse: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” She said: That is what will befall you in this world. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Khalid told me: that he heard Mujahid say about His statement, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: He will be recompensed for it in this world. He said: I said: What are the calamities? He said: What you dislike. Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever among the disbelievers does evil will be punished for it. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: the disbeliever. Then he recited: And do We recompense anyone except the disbelievers? (Saba’: 17), he said: of the disbelievers. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Hammam Al-Ahwazi told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he used to say: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and Do We recompense anyone except the ungrateful?
