(Saba’: 17), meaning by that the ungrateful, not the people of prayer. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: By God, God does not recompense a servant with good or evil except that He punishes him. He said: That He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done and recompense those who do good with goodness (al-Najm 53:31). He said: By God, they had sins, but He forgave them and did not recompense them for them. God does not recompense His believing servant for a sin, so his sins will destroy him. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His statement, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: God promised the believers that He would expiate their evil deeds, but He did not promise those, meaning the polytheists. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: That is only for whomever God wills, but as for whomever He wills to honor, he is among the people of Paradise: The promise of truth which they were promised. (al-Ahqaf 46:16) Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, meaning by that: the Jews, Christians, Magians, and Arab infidels, and they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper. Others said: The meaning of evil in this context is polytheism. They said: The interpretation of His statement, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, is that whoever associates partners with God will be recompensed for his polytheism, and he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, meaning: whoever associates partners with God will be recompensed for it - and it is evil - and he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper, unless he repents before his death, then God will accept his repentance. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal Ibn Amr, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Jubayr: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: polytheism. Abu Jaafar said: The most appropriate interpretation that we mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the interpretation that we mentioned on the authority of Abi bin Kaab and Aisha: which is that everyone who does a bad deed, whether small or large, whether a believer or a disbeliever, will be punished for it. We said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse: because the verse is general in its application to every evil doer, without specifying or excluding anyone from them. So it is general, since there is no indication in the verse of its specificity, nor is there any evidence for that from a report from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. If someone were to say: Where is that in relation to the statement of God: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins (An-Nisa’: 31)? And how is it permissible for Him to punish for what He has promised to remove? It was said: By His saying: We will remove from you your misdeeds (An-Nisa’: 30), He did not promise to leave retribution for them, but rather He promised retribution by leaving disgrace from Him to their people in their afterlife, just as He disgraced the people of polytheism and hypocrisy. But if He recompenses them for them in this world with calamities in order to remove them from them, so that they may meet Him without any sin for which they deserve retribution, then He has fulfilled for them what He promised them by His saying: We will remove from you your misdeeds (An-Nisa’: 30), and He has fulfilled for them what He guaranteed for them by His saying: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow (An-Nisa’: 122). In the same way as we said, the report about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reported. Mentioning the report reported about this: Abu Kurayb, Sufyan ibn Wakee’, Nasr ibn Ali and Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani told us, they said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Muhaisin, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah, “on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ‘Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,’ it was difficult for the Muslims, and it reached what God willed it to reach. So they complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Be moderate and go straight, for for everything that befalls a Muslim there is expiation, even a calamity that befalls him or a thorn that pricks him.’” Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad and Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told me, they said: Zaid bin Habbab told us, he said: Abdul Malik bin Al-Hasan Al-Harithi told us, he said: Muhammad bin Zaid bin Qunfudh told us, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Abu Bakr, he said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for everything we do? He said: O Abu Bakr, has such and such not befallen you? That is its expiation. Ibrahim bin Saad Al-Jawhari told me, he said, Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Ziyad Al-Jassas, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, he said, Abdullah bin Omar told me: He heard Abu Bakr say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world. Ibn Humayd narrated, Hakam narrated, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhair, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, that he said: O Prophet of God, how can there be righteousness after this verse? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which verse? He said: God says: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” So whatever we do, we will be recompensed for it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God forgive you, O Abu Bakr! Are you not sick? Are you not sad? Are you not afflicted with pain? He said: This is what you will be recompensed for! Yunus told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, who said: I think it was on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: When this verse was revealed: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, Abu Bakr said: How is righteousness? Then he mentioned something similar, except that he added: Are you not sinning? Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair: that Abu Bakr said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: How is righteousness? And he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me, he said, Abu Malik Al-Janbi told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair Al-Thaqafi, he said, “Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: So for every evil we have done, we will be rewarded for it? And he also said: Do you not get sick? Do you not suffer? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer from distress? He said: Yes. He said: It is what you will be rewarded for!” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, “On the authority of Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Zuhair Al-Thaqafi, he said: When this verse was revealed: ‘It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,’ he said: Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, will we be recompensed for everything we do? He said: O Abu Bakr, are you not afflicted? Are you not sad? Are you not afflicted with distress? This is one of the things for which you will be recompensed.” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, he said, Ibn Abi Khalid told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair Al-Thaqafi told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, and he mentioned something similar. Abu Al-Sa’ib and Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, they said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, he said: “Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, how severe is this verse: ‘Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it’? He said: O Abu Bakr, the calamity in this world is a recompense.” Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Ruh ibn Ubadah narrated, he said: Abu Aamer Al-Khazzaz narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, “On the authority of Aisha, she said: I said: I know which verse in the Book of God is the most severe! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Which verse? I said: ‘Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it!’ He said: The believer will be recompensed for his worst deeds in this world. Then he mentioned things, including sickness and fatigue. The last thing he mentioned was the calamity, and he said: Everyone will be recompensed for his deeds, O Aisha. No one will be held accountable on the Day of Resurrection except that he will be punished. I said: Doesn’t God say: ‘Then he will be held accountable with an easy reckoning’ (al-Inshiqaq 84:8)? He said: That will be at the presentation, whoever is called to account will be punished. And he pointed with his hand on his finger, as if he was poking it.” Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Maruf narrated to me, he said: Sulayman bin Harb narrated to us, he said: Sulayman bin Harb narrated to us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Umayyah, she said: I asked Aisha about this verse: And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it (al-Baqarah 2:284), and “It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” She said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: O Aisha, that is God’s reward for the servant for what befalls him of fever and old age, and the merchandise that He puts in his sleeve and loses it, and is alarmed by it, then finds it in his sleeve, until the believer emerges from his sins as red gold emerges from the bellows. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Amir Al-Khazzaz told us, he said, Ibn Abi Malikah told us, “On the authority of Aisha, she said: I said, O Messenger of God, I know the most severe verse in the Qur’an! He said: What is it, O Aisha? I said: It is this verse, O Messenger of God: ‘Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.’ He said: It is whatever befalls a believing slave, even a calamity befalls him.” Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ bin Subaih, on the authority of Ata’, he said: When the verse was revealed: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, how severe is this verse? He said: O Abu Bakr, you get sick, you get sad, and some harm befalls you, so this is for that. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ata’ bin Abi Rabah told me: When it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: The back-breaker has come! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are only the calamities in this world. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And he who does evil, such as disobeying God and going against what He has commanded him, will not find, besides God, meaning: after God and other than Him, a protector who will oversee his affairs and protect him from what befalls him of God’s punishment, nor a helper, meaning: nor a supporter who will aid him from what befalls him of God’s punishment and painful chastisement.
4:124: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: those to whom He said: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book. God says to them: Only those of you who do righteous deeds, males and females, and the males and females of My servants, who believe in Me and My Messenger Muhammad, who believe in My Oneness and in the Prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought from Me, will enter Paradise and enjoy it in the Hereafter. Not you, O polytheists who disbelieve in Me and in My Messenger, so do not hope to take the place of those who believe in Me, while you are disbelievers, and to enter their place on the Day of Resurrection, while you are disbelievers in My Messenger, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer, he said: He refused to accept faith except through righteous deeds, and he refused to accept Islam except through goodness. As for His statement: And they will not be wronged, even as much as a speck on a date stone, it means: And God will not wrong those who do righteous deeds, in the reward of their work, the size of a speck on the back of a date pit, so how about something greater than that and more? Rather, He, may He be glorified and praised, informs His servants of this that He will not diminish their reward for their work, little or much, but He will give them it in full as He promised them. And with what we said about the meaning of the peephole, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid. And they will not be wronged as much as a speck, he said: The speck is what is in the back of the date pit. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Amer told us, he said, Qura told us, on the authority of Atiyah, he said: The hollow is what is in the middle of the seed. If someone were to say to us: What is the reason for including whoever in His statement: and whoever does righteous deeds, and not saying: and whoever does righteous deeds? It was said: There are two aspects to its entry: One of them: That God knew that His believing servants would not be able to do all the good deeds, so He made His promise obligatory for whoever did what he could of them, and He did not deprive him of His grace because of what his strength was unable to do of them. The other of them: That the Almighty, the Most High, made His promise obligatory for those who avoid major sins and perform the obligatory duties, because He fell short in some of what was obligatory for Him, as a favor from Him to His believing servants, since favor is more deserving of Him, and forgiveness of the people of faith is more deserving of Him. Some Arab scholars may say that it was inserted in this place in the sense of deletion, and they interpret it as: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer. This is not permissible in my opinion, because it has a meaning, so it is not permissible for its meaning to be deletion.
4:125: Abu Ja`far said: This is a decree from God, the Most High, for Islam and its people to be superior to all other religions and their people. God says: And who is better in religion O people, and more correct in path and more guided in way, than one who submits his face to God, meaning: one who submits his face to God and submits to Him in obedience, believing in his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he brought from his Lord, and is a doer of good, meaning: one who does what his Lord has commanded him to do, forbidding what He has forbidden and permitting what He has permitted, and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, meaning: and follows the religion that Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, was upon, and he commanded his children after him to follow it and advised them to follow it, inclining toward truth, meaning: upright in his method and path. We have previously explained the difference of opinion among those who differ regarding the meaning of Hanaf, and the evidence for the correct statement regarding that is sufficient, so there is no need to repeat it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Among those who said this was also Al-Dahhak. Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, Yazid told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: God preferred Islam over every religion, saying: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God while being a doer of good? until His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend. And no deed is accepted in it other than Islam, which is the Hanafi school. Abu Jaafar said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And God took Abraham as a friend. If someone says: What is the meaning of the friendship that was given to Abraham? It was said: That from Abraham, peace be upon him: enmity for the sake of God and hatred for Him, and allegiance for the sake of God and love for Him, based on what is known from the meanings of friendship. As for God’s favor to Abraham: His victory over those who tried to harm him, like what He did to him when Nimrod wanted to burn him with fire, but he saved him from it, or based on his argument against him when he argued with him, and as He did to the king of Egypt when he wanted to separate him from his family - and enabling him to do what he loved - and making him an imam for those of His servants who came after him, and a role model for those who came after him in obeying and worshipping Him. So that is the meaning of His friendship with him. It was said: God named him Khalil because drought struck the people of his area, so he traveled to a friend of his from Mosul - and some said: from Egypt - to choose food for his family from before him, but he did not find what he needed there. When he approached his family, he passed by a sandy desert, and said: If I filled my buckets with this sand, so that I would not upset my family by returning to them without provisions, and so that they would think that I had brought them what they love! So he did that, and the sand in his buckets turned into flour. When he reached his home, he slept. His family got up, opened the buckets, and found flour, so they kneaded some of it and baked bread. He woke up and asked them about the flour they had baked from, and they said: From the flour that you brought from your friend! He knew and said: Yes! It is from the two friends of God! They said: So God named him Khalil with that.
4:126: Abu Ja'far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And God took Abraham as a friend, for his obedience to his Lord, his sincerity in worship, and his hastening to please Him and love Him, not because he needed Him or His friendship. How could He need Him or His friendship, when He owns whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, little or much, as a kingdom, and the owner is the one who needs His kingdom, not because of his need for Him? He says: So likewise, Abraham needed Him, not because he needed Him so that he would take him as a friend because of his need for Him, but rather He took him as a friend because of his hastening to please Him and love Him. He says: So likewise, hasten to please Me and love Me, so that I may take you as allies for Me. And God encompasses all things, and God has always been counting everything that His servants do, good and evil, knowing that, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom of it escapes Him.
4:127: Abu Ja`far said: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: And they ask you concerning women, is that your companions ask you, O Muhammad, to give them a fatwa concerning the matter of women, and what is obligatory for them and upon them. So He was satisfied with mentioning women rather than mentioning their affair, because what appeared from the speech indicates what was intended by it. “Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them.” Say to them: O Muhammad, God gives you a ruling concerning them, meaning: concerning women, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His statement: And what is recited to you in the Book. Some of them said: He means by his saying: And what is recited to you, say: God gives you a fatwa regarding them, and regarding what is recited to you. They said: Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Qais, on the authority of Ata, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book.’” He said: The people of ignorance did not give an inheritance to a newborn until he grew up, nor did they give an inheritance to a woman. Then when Islam came, He said: “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book.’” At the beginning of the surah, regarding the inheritance laws, those to whom you do not give what God has decreed for them. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha: And what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and you desire to marry them, she said: This is about the orphan girl who is with a man, perhaps she will be his partner in his wealth, and he is more deserving of her than anyone else, so he is reluctant to marry her and prevents her from marrying him because of her wealth, and they do not marry her to anyone other than him out of a fear that anyone else will share her wealth with him. Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: In the pre-Islamic era, women and young men were not to bequeath until they reached puberty. Then God revealed: “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God instructs you about them and what is recited to you in the Book about orphan women.’” at the beginning of Surat al-Nisa’ from the chapter on inheritance. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: In the pre-Islamic era, they did not give an orphan girl an inheritance, nor did they marry her off, and they were preventing her from getting married. Then God revealed: “And they ask you concerning women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning them.’” to the end of the verse. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Al-Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah bin Katheer narrated to me: He heard Saeed bin Jubair say about the verse: “And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book about orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry,” the verse, he said: Only the man who has reached puberty inherits, neither the young man nor the woman inherits. Then when the verse of inheritance was revealed in Surat An-Nisa, it was difficult for the people and they said: The young man who does not work with the money nor takes care of it inherits, and the woman who is like that, they inherit as the man who works with the money inherits! So they hoped that something would happen from the sky about that, so they waited. But when they saw that something would not happen, they said: If this happens, then it is obligatory and there is no escape from it! Then they said: Ask! So they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: “And they ask you concerning women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book’” at the beginning of the surah, Concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry. Saeed bin Jubair said: If the guardian had beauty and wealth, he would desire her and marry her and keep her for himself. If she did not have beauty and wealth, he would marry her off but not marry her. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: “And they ask you concerning women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry.” He said: If a female slave was an orphan and ugly, they would not give her her inheritance, and they would prevent her from being married until she died, then they would inherit from her. So God revealed this. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, “And they ask you concerning women. Say, ‘God gives you a ruling concerning them,’” he said: A man among them would have an orphan girl who was ugly and had something that he did not like about her, and she had money. He said: So he would not marry her or give her in marriage until she died and he could inherit from her. He said: So God forbade them from that. Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik: And what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry, he said: If a woman was with a guardian who did not want her, he would keep her if he did not marry her, and he would not let anyone marry her. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: For the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, he said: The people of the Age of Ignorance did not give women or children anything inheritance. They used to say: They do not fight or gain any good booty! So God imposed the right of inheritance on the female orphan so that a man would compete - or: so that a man would compete - for the wealth of his orphan girl if she was not good. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said, my father told us, he said, my uncle told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "And they ask you concerning women. Say, 'God gives you a legal opinion concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book,'" meaning: the obligations that were imposed on women, those to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry, he said: The orphan girl would be in the care of a man and he would desire to marry her or have intercourse with her, but he would not give her her money, hoping that she would die and he would inherit from her. And if her intimate friend died, she would not be given anything from the inheritance. And that was in the pre-Islamic era, so God made that clear to them. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning them,’” until he reached and you desire to marry them. So a man would have an orphan girl in his care who was ugly and had money, but he would not want to marry her and would keep her for her money, so God revealed about her what you hear. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God gives you a ruling concerning them.’” He said: There would be an orphan girl in a man’s care who was ugly, so he would be reluctant to marry her, but he would not marry her out of desire for her money. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And what is recited to you in the Book concerning female orphans to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and you desire to marry them, until his statement: with justice, he said: “Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari then al-Sulami had a blind cousin, and she was ugly, and she had inherited money from her father, so Jabir was reluctant to marry her, and would not marry her for fear that the husband would take her money, so he asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and there were people in whose care there were female slaves also like that, so Jabir kept asking the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Does a female slave inherit if she is ugly and blind? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept saying: Yes!! So God revealed this about them.” Others said: The meaning of this is: And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about them and about what is recited to you in the Book, at the end of Surat An-Nisa. This is His statement: “They ask you about women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about those who are not yet born” to the end of the surah (al-Nisa 4:176). Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Salam bin Saleem told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: The people of ignorance did not give inheritance to children until they reached puberty, so God revealed: And they ask you concerning women, until His saying: For indeed, God is ever Knowing of them. He said: And this verse was revealed: If a man dies and leaves no child, (An-Nisa’: 176), the entire verse. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a fatwa about them and about what is recited to you in the Book, meaning: at the beginning of this surah, and that is His saying: And if you fear that you will not be just toward the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of [other] women (An-Nisa’: 3). Who said that? Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus ibn Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr told me: He asked Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement of God, And if you fear that you will not be able to deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry such women as seem good to you (An-Nisa’: 3). She said: O son of my sister, she is an orphan who is in the care of a man who is her guardian, and shares his wealth. He is pleased with her wealth and her beauty, so her guardian wants to marry her without being just in her dowry, so he gives her the same as someone else. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they were just with them and gave them the highest dowry possible. And they were commanded to marry such women as seem good to them other than them. Urwah said: Aisha said: Then the people asked the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) about them after this verse, so God revealed: “And they ask you about women. Say: God instructs you about them and what is recited to you in the Book about orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry.” She said: What God mentioned as being recited in the Book is the first verse in which He said: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry such women as seem good to you. (An-Nisa’: 3) Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, similarly. Abu Ja`far said: According to these three opinions that we mentioned, the ma in His statement, and what is recited to you, is in the accusative case, meaning that it is in apposition to the ha’ and the nun in His statement, He gives you a fatwa concerning them. So it is as if they directed the interpretation of the verse to: Say, God gives you a fatwa, O people, concerning women, and concerning what is recited to you in the Book. Others said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding some of his companions who asked him about some matters concerning women, and they left out asking about other things they used to do. So God gave them a fatwa regarding what they asked about and what they left out asking about. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us - Sufyan said, ‘Abd al-A’la told us, and Ibn al-Muthanna said, ‘Abd al-A’la told me - he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, regarding this verse: And they ask you about women, he said: They asked the Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about women, and they remained silent about something they used to do, so God revealed: “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book,’” and He gives you a legal opinion about what you have not asked about. He said: They would not marry an orphan girl if she was ugly, nor would they give her money to her so that she could spend, so this verse was revealed: Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book about orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and you desire to marry them,’ he said: And the weak among the children, he said: They used to give the elders an inheritance and not the younger ones an inheritance. Then he gave them a fatwa on what they were silent about, saying: If a woman fears desertion or abandonment from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they reconcile between themselves, and reconciliation is better. The wording of the hadith is from Ibn al-Muthanna. Abu Ja`far said: According to this statement: What is recited to us in the Book, in which God Almighty said: “Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them and what is recited to you”: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, the verse. And what the people asked and were answered about regarding female orphans: those who were not given what God had decreed for them of inheritance from those from whom they inherited it. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these statements that we have mentioned from those we have mentioned from him, and the most similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation, is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of His statement, and what is recited to you in the Book, is what is recited to you from the verses of the obligations at the beginning and end of this surah. Rather, we said that this is more correct, because the dowry is not what was prescribed for women except through marriage, so unless she marries, she has no dowry before anyone. If that was not for her before anyone, it was not what was prescribed for her. If it was not what was prescribed for her, then the statement of one who said: What is recited to you in the Book means fairness in the dowries of orphan women, has no basis. Because God said in the context of the verse, explaining the fatwa that He promised us to issue: Concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, so He informed us that some of what we issue fatwas about regarding women is the matter of the orphan who is prevented from what God has prescribed for her. And the dowry before the marriage contract is not what God has prescribed for her from anyone. So it was known from this that the one meant by this verse is the one who has been prevented from what was prescribed for her from what is recited to us in the Book of God. So if that is the case, then it is known that this is the inheritance that God has made obligatory for them in His Book. As for what was mentioned about Muhammad bin Abi Musa, then despite its departure from the statement of the people of interpretation, it is far from what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation. That is because he claimed that what God meant by His statement: And what is recited to you in the Book, is: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion. And if the speech is directed to the meaning that he interpreted, then the speech becomes a beginning from His statement: In the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, thus translating His statement: In them, and the meaning of the speech becomes: Say, God gives you a ruling concerning them, in the orphan women to whom you do not give. There is no evidence in the verse for what he said, nor is there any trace from someone who knows that his statement is correct. And since that is the case, then connecting the meanings of the speech to each other would be more appropriate, as there is no way to do so. If the matter is as we have described, then his saying: in the orphan women is more appropriate for it to be a connection to his saying: and what is recited to you, than for it to be a translation of his saying: “Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them,” because of its proximity to his saying: and what is recited to you in the Book, and its disconnection from his saying: He gives you a ruling concerning them. Since this is the case, the interpretation of the verse: And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about them and about what is recited to you in the Book of God which He revealed to His Prophet in the matter of orphan women to whom you do not give what was prescribed for them, meaning: what God has prescribed for them of inheritance from those whom they inherit, as: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: Do not give them what was written for them. He said: Do not give them an inheritance. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement: Do not give them what is written for them, he said: Of the inheritance. He said: They did not give women an inheritance, and you desire to marry them. The interpreters differed about the meaning of his saying: And you desire to marry them. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And you are reluctant to marry them. We have already mentioned a group of those who said this, and we will mention the saying of others whom we did not mention. Humaid bin Mas`ad Al-Sami told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Ubaid God bin Awn told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And you desire to marry them, he said: You desire to avoid them. Yaqub and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah, he said: Aisha said regarding the statement of God, and you desire to marry them, it is the desire of one of you to marry off his orphan girl who is in his care when she is of little wealth and beauty, so they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whose wealth and beauty they desired except in a fair manner, because of their desire to marry them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us - meaning Ibn Salih - he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Urwah said, Aisha said, and he mentioned something similar. Others said: The meaning of this is: And you desire to marry them. A group of those who said this have already been mentioned, and we will mention the statement of those we have not mentioned among them. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Ibn `Aun told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of `Ubaydah: And you desire to marry them, he said: And you desire them. Yaqub bin Ibrahim and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: I said to Ubaydah: And you desire to marry them, he said: You desire them. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: In the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and you desire to marry them, then in the days of ignorance a man would have an orphan girl with him and he would throw his garment over her. If he did that to her, no one would ever be able to marry her. If she was beautiful and he desired her, he would marry her and eat her money. If she was ugly, the man would keep her away forever until she died. When she died, he would inherit her. So God forbade that and prohibited it. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the one that says: The meaning of this is: And you are reluctant to marry them. Because their withholding their money from them, along with their preventing them from marrying them, was only so that they would inherit their money, without a husband if they married. If those who withheld their money from them only withheld it from them out of a desire to marry them, then there would be no known reason for withholding it from them, because they were their guardians, and nothing prevented them from marrying them, so there would be a need to withhold her money from her, so that her withholding it from her would be used as a reason for her to marry herself to him. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a fatwa about them - and about what is recited to you in the Book - and about the weak among children, and about you standing up for orphans with justice. We have mentioned the narration of that from those who said it from the Companions and Followers in the past, and those who issued fatwas regarding the matter of the weak children, that they should be given their rights of inheritance, because they did not give inheritance to the young children of the deceased, and he ordered them to be fair to them, to be just and give them their shares according to what God divided for them in His Book, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding the statement: and the weak among children, they were not to bequeath a girl or a young boy, so God commanded them to act justly towards the orphans. Justice means giving each one of them his right, whether male or female, the young among them is like the old. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: “And they ask you concerning women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them,’” he said: Do not give them any money as an inheritance, and that you deal justly with orphans, he said: So women, the young, and the old were included in the inheritance, and the inheritance abrogated that first one. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And that you stand up for orphans with justice, they commanded that orphans be just, fair. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Saddī, on the authority of Abu Malik: And the weak among children and that you deal justly with orphans, he said: They would not inherit except the oldest, then the oldest. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the weak among children, that in the pre-Islamic era, they did not give inheritance to the young or the girls, so that is what He said: Do not give them what was written for them, so God forbade that, and explained to each person with a share his share, and He said: For the male is equal to the share of two females (An-Nisa’: 11, 176), whether young or old. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: And the weak among children and that you deal justly with orphans, that is because they did not give the young and weak anything inheritance, so God commanded that they be given their share of the inheritance. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hisham told us, Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim: That when the guardian of an orphan girl came to Omar bin Al-Khattab, if she was beautiful and rich, Omar would say to him: Marry her to someone other than you, and look for someone better than you. But if she was ugly and had no money, he would say: Marry her, for you have more right to her! Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, Hisham narrated, Yunus bin Ubaid informed us, on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Al-Faraj, who said: A man came to Ali bin Abi Talib and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is my affair and what is the affair of my orphan girl? He said: What is the matter with you? He said: Then Ali said: Will you marry her, you who are rich and beautiful? He said: Yes, by God! He said: Then marry her, she is ugly and has no money! Then Ali said: Choose for her, and if someone other than you is better for her, then include her in what is good. Abu Jaafar said: Their taking care of orphans fairly was justice in what God commanded them to do. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Whatever you, O believers, do with the wealth of orphans, which God has commanded you to do with them in justice, and to adhere to God’s command in that and other matters and to obey Him, then God is ever Knowing of it. He has always been Knowing of what will happen from you, and He is recording all of that for you, preserving it, until He rewards you for it with your reward on the Day of Resurrection.
4:128: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And if a woman fears from her husband, he says: she knows from her husband, disobedience, meaning: his arrogance towards her and towards someone else, his preference for her, and his elevation of her over her, either because of his hatred for her, or because he dislikes some of her reasons: either her ugliness, or her age and old age, or other matters of hers, or turning away, meaning: turning away from her with his face or with some of the benefits that she had from him, “there is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves”, he says: There is no blame upon them, meaning: upon the woman who fears her husband’s disobedience or his turning away from her, “that they make peace between themselves”, which is that she leaves her day for him, or waives some of her duty towards him from a right that he owes her, thereby seeking his sympathy and continuing to stay in his bonds, and adhering to the contract between them of marriage, he says: And reconciliation is better, meaning: and reconciliation by giving up some of the right is the continuation of the sanctity. Holding on to the marriage contract is better than seeking separation and divorce. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara: That a man came to Ali, may God be pleased with him, to ask him about a woman who feared her husband’s disobedience or neglect. He said: A woman may be with a man and his eyes may turn away from her because of her ugliness, her old age, her bad character, or her poverty, so she hates to leave him. If she gives him something from her dowry, it is permissible for him, but if she gives him something from her days, there is no blame. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak Ibn Harb, on the authority of Khalid Ibn Ar`arah, he said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked: If a woman fears from her husband desertion or disdain, there is no blame upon them if they reconcile between themselves. He said: The woman is old, or ugly, or the one her husband does not love, so they reconcile. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah, Hammad bin Salamah, and Abu Al-Ahwas told us, all of them, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid ibn Arara: That a man asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, about his saying: “There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves.” He said: A woman may be ugly to a man, and his eyes turn away from her because of her ugliness or her age, but if she gives him some of her days or her money, there is no blame upon him. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: A man came to Umar and asked him about a verse, and he disliked that and hit him with a whip. Then another asked him about this verse: And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or evasion, so he said: Ask about something like this! Then he said: This woman is with a man who has outgrown her age, so he marries a young woman in order to seek her child, so whatever they agree upon is permissible. Amr bin Ali told us, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, Ata bin Al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, he said: It is the woman who stays with the man until she grows old, and he wants to marry another woman, so they make peace between themselves, on the condition that she has one day, and she has two or three days. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in a similar manner - except that he said: until she gives birth or grows up - and he also said: There is no blame upon them if they reconcile on one night and the other two nights. Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hameed told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Concerning a woman who has been with a man for a long time and has grown old, so he wants to replace her, but she is reluctant to leave him, so he marries another woman and he reconciles with her on the condition that he gives her some days, and the other the days and the month. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If a woman fears from her husband desertion or disdain, he said: She is the woman who is with a man and he wants to separate from her, so she hates for him to separate from her, and he wants to marry and he says: I cannot swear to you what I swear to her, so she makes peace with him on the condition that she will have one day of the days, and they agree on that, and they are on what they agreed upon. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, my father narrated, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha: If a woman fears desertion or abandonment on the part of her husband, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best. She said: This is about a woman who is with a man, and perhaps he will become arrogant towards her? And she does not have a child and has no companion, so she says: Do not divorce me, and you are free to have anything to do with me. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, she said: This man may have two wives, one of whom is impotent, or she is ugly, and he does not like her much, so she says: Do not divorce me, and you are free to deal with me. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, something similar, except that he said: So she says: I absolve you of my responsibility! So this verse was revealed regarding that. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, that is, that woman is with the man, and he does not see from her much of what he likes, and he has another woman who is more beloved to him than her, so he prefers her over her. So when that happens, God commanded him to say to her: O woman, if you wish to remain in what you see of self-interest, then I will comfort you and spend on you, then remain, and if you dislike it, I will set you free, and if she agrees to remain after he gives her the choice, then there is no blame upon him, and this is His statement: And reconciliation is best, and it is the choice. Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman and Bahr bin Nasr told us, they said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said: God revealed this verse about a woman who has reached old age, so she devotes her day to another woman. She said: It was about this that the verse was revealed: “There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves.” Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, he said: I asked him about the statement of God: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, he said: He sees a woman being with her husband, and he wants to marry another woman, so she reconciles with him from that day on a peace treaty. He said: So they are on what they agreed upon. If it is violated by him, he must change his mind about it or leave her. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim: that he used to say that. Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Mujahid: that he used to say that. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion to the end of the verse, he said: He may reconcile with her on what she is satisfied with, without her right, and he may do that as long as she is satisfied. But if she denies it, or says: I was jealous, then she has the right to be just with her, or to appease her, or to divorce her. Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said: Abdul Wahhab narrated, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: I asked Ubaidah about the statement of God: {And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion}, he said: It is a man who has a wife who has passed away, so she makes peace with him for something, then it is his as long as she is satisfied. But if she is displeased, then he has the right to treat her justly, or satisfy her with her right, or divorce her. Ibn Wakee' narrated, he said: Jarir narrated, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: I asked Ubaidah about the statement: {And if a woman fears desertion or evasion from her husband}, he mentioned something similar to that, except that he said: If she is displeased, then he has the right to satisfy her, or give her all her right, or divorce her. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheera, he said, Ibrahim said: If she wants, she is entitled to her right, and if she refuses and rejects the reconciliation, then that is in her hand. If he wants, he can divorce her, and if he wants, he can keep her in her right. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mugheera, on the authority of Ibrahim: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, there is no blame upon them. He said, Ali said: A woman may be with a man for a long time, and she fears that he will divorce her, so she makes peace with him on a settlement as he and she wish, he spends the night with her on such and such a night, and with another, whatever they agree upon, and her expenses should be less than they were before. And whatever she makes peace with him on is permissible. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hakam: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or disdain, he said: She is the woman who is with the man, and he wants to release her. So if she fears that from him, then there is no blame upon them if they come to an agreement between themselves, and she gives up some of her days if he marries. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, to his statement: And reconciliation is better, which is a man who has an older woman under him, so he marries a younger woman in addition to her, and he hates to leave the mother of his child, so he reconciles with her on the basis of a gift from his money and himself, and that reconciliation is good for him. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, then he recited until he reached then indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted. This is about a man who has a woman who has become old and some of her affairs seem easy to him, so he says: If I am satisfied with myself and my wealth without what you were satisfied with before today, then if they agree on something about that, then God has made that permissible for them. But if she refuses, then it is not right for him to keep her in a state of destitution. Narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Yahya, who said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, who said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Sulaiman bin Yasar: That Rafi bin Khadij had a wife who had passed away, so he married a younger woman, and preferred the younger woman over her. But his first wife refused to continue in that condition, so he divorced her once. When she had a short life left, he said: If you wish, I will take you back and be patient with the preference, and if you wish, I will leave you until your time is up! She said: Rather, take me back and I will be patient with the preference! So he took her back, then preferred her, but she could not be patient with the preference, so he divorced her again and preferred the younger woman over her. He said: That is the reconciliation that we have been told that God revealed about it: And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or desertion, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves. Al-Hasan said, Abd al-Razzaq said, Muammar said, and Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, with a hadith similar to that of al-Zuhri, and he added to it: If he harms her a third time, then he must pay her her due, or divorce her. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: From her husband’s disobedience or neglect, he said: A man saying to his wife: You are old, and I want to replace you with a young, beautiful woman, so be kind to your children, and I will not give you anything of myself. That is the reconciliation between them, and he is Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba’kak. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh: From her husband who is disobedient or ignorant, then he mentioned something similar. Shibl said: So I said to him: So if you have a wife, then you divide your time for her and do not divide it for this one? He said: If you agree on that, then there is nothing wrong with him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, he said: I asked Amer about a man who has a wife whom he wants to divorce, and she says: Do not divorce me, and allocate one day for me, and two days for the one he married. He said: There is nothing wrong with it, it is a reconciliation. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi: “If a woman fears desertion or disdain from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves, and peace is best.” He said: A woman sees some good fortune in her husband, and she has grown old, or is not able to bear children, so her husband wants to marry someone else, so he comes to her and says: I want to marry a young woman who is younger than you, perhaps she will bear children for me, and I will prefer her in terms of time and maintenance. If she is satisfied with that, I will divorce her, and they will agree to what they like. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, he said: Desertion from her, the man intending to have two wives with her, or evasion, by leaving her, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, either he pleases her so that she may release him, or she pleases him so that she may be kind to him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, meaning: hatred. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, it is a man who has an older woman, so he marries a younger woman in addition to her, and he is inclined towards her, and she is more pleasing to him than the older woman, so he makes peace with the older woman on the condition that he gives her from his money and allocates to her a known portion of himself. Amr bin Ali and Zaid bin Akhzam told us, Abu Dawud told us, Sulayman bin Muadh told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Sawdah feared that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would divorce her, so she said: Do not divorce me from your wives, and do not divide your time for me. So he did, and this verse was revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or desertion. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: That they may reconcile between them. This was read by most of the people of Medina and some of the people of Basra with the opening of the ya’ and the emphasis on the sad, meaning: that they should reconcile with each other, then the ta’ was assimilated into the sad, so they became a stressed sad. The majority of the people of Kufa read it as: that they reconcile between them, with a damma on the ya’ and a light sad, meaning: the husband and wife reconciled between them. Abu Jaafar said: The most amazing of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads that they reconcile with each other with a fat-ha on the ya’ and a shaddah on the sad, meaning: they reconcile. Because reconciliation in this context is more famous and has a clearer meaning, and is more eloquent and more common on the tongues of the Arabs than reform. And reform in the opposite of corruption is more famous than it is in the meaning of reconciliation. If someone thinks that his statement, reconciliation, indicates that the reading of those who read it, they reconcile with a damma on the ya, is more correct, then the matter in that is contrary to what he thought. That is because reconciliation is a noun and not a verb, so it is used as evidence for the more correct of the two readings in his statement, they reconcile between them a reconciliation. Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And the women’s souls became greedy with regard to their shares of their husbands’ souls and money. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’eed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the souls are overcome by greed, he said: their share of it. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, they both said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’eed ibn Jubayr: And the souls are overcome by greed, he said: in the days. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’: And the souls were overcome by greed, he said: in terms of days and expenses. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi and Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: Regarding spending. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ruh told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: Regarding spending. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’: And the souls were overcome by greed, he said: in the days. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse: And the souls are overcome by greed, he said: The soul of a woman is concerned about her share of her husband, of his soul and his wealth. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, similarly. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Regarding spending. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Bakir ibn Al-Akhns, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: In the days and the expenses. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: In the days and the expenses. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And the souls are overcome by greed, he said: The woman is stingy with her husband’s money and his soul. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: When this verse was revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or evasion, the woman came and said: I want you to share some of yourself for me! She had been satisfied that he would leave her and not divorce her or have intercourse with her, so God revealed: And the souls are overcome by greed. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And the souls are averse to greed, he said: They yearn for their husbands and their expenses. He said: And it was claimed that it was revealed about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about Sawdah bint Zam’ah: She had grown old, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to divorce her, so they agreed that he would keep her and give her day to Aishah, but she was averse to her place with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: The meaning of this is: And the soul of each one of the man and the woman is averse to his right before the other. Those who said this are mentioned: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, I heard Ibn Zayd say about His statement, And the souls are overcome with greed, he said: His soul is not content for him to give her something, so she forgives him, nor is his soul content for him to give him something from her money, so she feels sorry for him. Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: What he meant by that is: Women’s souls have become stingy with regard to their shares from their husbands in terms of days and expenses. And greed: is excessive eagerness for something, and in this context it is: the excessive eagerness of a woman for her share of her days from her husband and her expenses. So the interpretation of the statement is: and the souls of women brought their desires, from excessive eagerness for their rights from their husbands, and the greed with that towards their co-wives. In a similar vein to what we said about the meaning of stinginess, it was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to say: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the souls have become greedy, and greed is his desire for something that he is keen on. We said that this statement is more correct than the statement of the one who said: What is meant by that is: And the souls of men and women have become greedy, according to what Ibn Zayd said, because a man reconciling with his wife by giving her from his money as a reward on the condition that she forgives him for dividing her time is not permissible. This is because there is no compensation for the reward that he gave her. And compensation is not valid except for compensation: either a substance or a benefit. And when a man gives a woman a reward on the condition that she forgives him for a day and a night, then he does not own anything or a benefit from her. Since that is the case, that is one of the meanings of consuming wealth unjustly. Since that is the case, it is known that there is no basis for the statement of the one who said: What is meant by that is a man and a woman. If someone thinks that since this was a right of the woman and she has the right to demand it, then the man has the right to redeem it from her for a fee, then the pre-emption right of the one seeking pre-emption is for a share of a house that a man bought from a partner who has a right to it and he has the right to demand it, then the one sought must have the right to redeem it from him for a fee. And in the consensus of all that the settlement in this for compensation is not permissible, since the one sought in pre-emption was not compensated for in kind or benefit, what indicates the length of a man’s settlement with his wife for compensation, on the condition that she forgives her demand of him to divide it for her. If that is corrupted, then the interpretation of the verse is what we said. The report that we mentioned on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Sulayman bin Yasar has made clear that his statement, And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, the verse, was revealed regarding the matter of Rafi bin Khadij and his wife, when he married a young woman and preferred the young woman over her. The older woman refused to accept his preference, so he divorced her once and left her. When her waiting period was about to end, he gave her the choice between separation, returning to her, and patience with his preference, so she chose returning to her and patience with his preference. So he took her back and preferred her over him, but she could not be patient, so he divorced her and she chose. In that is clear evidence that his statement, And greediness has seized upon the souls, only meant: And greed has seized upon the souls of women with regard to their rights from their husbands, as we have described. Abu Ja`far said: As for his statement, And if you do good and fear God, it means: And if you do good, O men, in your actions towards your women, if you dislike their ugliness or character or some of what you dislike in them, by being patient with them, fulfilling their rights and treating them kindly, and fear God, meaning: and fear God in dealing with them by refraining from being unjust towards them in what is due to those of them whom you dislike, such as dividing for them, spending on them, and treating them kindly, then indeed God is, of what you do, All-Aware, meaning: All-Knowing, All-Aware of what you do in the affairs of your women, O men, of treating them kindly and treating them kindly, and being unjust towards them in what is required of you and obligatory for them, All-Aware, meaning: All-Knowing, All-Aware, nothing is hidden from Him, rather He is All-Aware of it, and He has a test against you, until He gives you the reward for that: the one among you who does good for his good, and the one who does evil for his evil.
4:129: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: And you will never be able to be equal between women, is that you will never be able, O men, to treat your wives and your husbands equally in your hearts until you treat them equally in that, so that there will not be in your hearts for some of them any love except what is for their companions, because that is something that you do not possess and is not up to you, even if you should strive to do so, meaning: Even if you should strive to treat them equally in that, as: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, he said: It is obligatory, that you will not be able to be equal between them. So do not incline completely towards her, meaning: do not incline with your desires towards those among them whom you do not possess the full love for, until that leads you to wrong their wives by neglecting to fulfill your duty towards them, which is a right that you owe them: in dividing your time with them, spending on them, and treating them kindly. and leave her as one in suspense, meaning: leave the one who is not the one you inclined with your desires towards, as one in suspense, meaning: like the one who has no husband, nor is she a widow. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said what we said about His statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so. Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, he said: in himself in love and sexual intercourse. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, he said: on his own authority. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath and Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, he said: I asked him about his statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, and he said: In sexual intercourse. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, who said: In love and sexual intercourse. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: About love. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, who said: In love and sexual intercourse. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, regarding his statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, he said: In affection, as if he meant love. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, meaning: You will not be able to be equal in desire between them, even if you should strive to do so. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, and Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: O God, as for my heart, I do not control it, but as for other than that, I hope to be just! Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, meaning: in love and intercourse.
