Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, and Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, they both said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to divide his time among his wives fairly, then he would say: O God, this is my division of what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hussain bin Ali told us, on the authority of Zaida, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Maleka, he said: This verse was revealed about Aisha: And you will never be able to be equal between wives. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: Concerning desire and intercourse. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: In sexual intercourse. Ali bin Sahl told us, Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa told us, Sufyan said regarding his statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, he said: In love and sexual intercourse. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told me, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so, he said: What is from his body and heart, that is something he cannot control. Mention of those who said what we said in the interpretation of his saying: So do not incline completely. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: I recited to Ubaydah: So do not incline completely, he said: To himself. Sufyan told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah: So do not incline completely, Hisham said: I think he said: in love and sexual intercourse. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, regarding his statement: all the way, he said: by himself. Bahr bin Nasr Al-Khawlani told us, he said, Bishr bin Bakr told us, he said, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: I asked Ubaidah about the statement of God: So do not incline completely, he said: By himself. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Do not incline completely, he said: in covering oneself and swearing. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So do not incline completely, do not intentionally do wrong. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: It reached me on the authority of Mujahid: So do not incline completely, he said: He deliberately does wrong and wrongs. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: So do not incline completely, he said: This is in the work of spending the night with her, and in what she receives from his goodness. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: So do not incline completely, meaning: incline towards her, not spending on her, nor allocating a day for her. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said: So do not incline completely, he said: He deliberately does wrong, he says: Do not incline completely, he said: It has reached me that it means sexual intercourse. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to divide his time among his wives fairly, and he would say, O God, this is my division of what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not! Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yazid, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Yahya, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Anas, on the authority of Bashir bin Nahik, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever has two wives and is inclined towards one of them over the other, will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of him hanging down. Mention of those who said what we said in the interpretation of his statement: Then leave it hanging. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then leave her hanging, he said: Leave her, she is neither a widow nor married. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: Then leave her hanging, he said: Neither single nor married. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Then leave her as if she is in suspense. He said: Neither divorced nor married. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sahl bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, the same. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then leave her as if she were suspended, meaning as if she were imprisoned or detained. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Then leave her hanging, he said: Like a prisoner. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of al-Rabi`, regarding his statement: Then leave her as if she were in suspense, he said: Neither divorced nor married. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, regarding his statement: So do not incline completely towards her, leaving her hanging, neither divorced nor married. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: It reached me on the authority of Mujahid: Then leave her hanging, he said: Neither single nor married. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh: Then leave her as if she is hanging, neither widowed nor married. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Maharibi, Abu Khalid, and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: Do not leave her as if she has no husband. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Then leave her hanging, he said: Neither divorced nor married. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Then leave her as one in suspense, he said: The one in suspense is the one who is not alone with herself so that she may seek for herself, and she is not prepared as a woman is for her husband, neither with her husband nor separated, so that she may seek for herself. So that is the one in suspense. Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty commanded men with His words: So do not incline completely towards her, leaving her hanging, to be just between their husbands in whatever they are able to do, such as dividing the time between them and spending, and to refrain from injustice in that by sending one of them over the other in what He has imposed upon them to be just between them, since He has pardoned them for what they cannot do justly between them in, due to the love and passion in their hearts. Abu Ja`far said: By that, He, the Most High, means: And if you amend your deeds, O people, and be just in your division between your wives, and what God has imposed upon you of maintenance and good treatment, so do not be unjust in that, and fear God, meaning: and fear God in the inclination that He has forbidden you from, by inclining towards one of them over the other, so you do not wrong her in her right from what God has imposed upon her, then indeed God is Forgiving, meaning: for God will conceal from you what you have done in the past of your inclination and injustice towards them before that, by leaving you alone in punishing you for it, and He will cover that for you by His pardon of what you have done in that before, Merciful, meaning: and He was Merciful to you, as He repented to you, so He accepted your repentance from what you have done in the past of your injustice towards them, and in His permission for you to reconcile between you and them, by their pardoning you of their rights to you in the division on the condition that they not be divorced.
4:130: Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: If the woman whose husband has rebelled against her, since he has turned away from her by inclining towards her co-wife because of her beauty or youth, or something else that people tend towards, refuses to make peace by forgiving her husband for her day and night, and asks him for her right from him in terms of the division and maintenance, and what God has obligated upon her, and the husband refuses to take from her the kindness that God has urged him to do in His saying: But if you do good and fear God, then indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted, to include her in the division, maintenance, and companionship with that to which he is inclined, so they separate by divorcing her by marrying her, God will enrich each from His abundance, meaning: God will enrich the husband and the divorced woman from the abundance of His grace. As for this one, then with a husband who is better for her than the first divorced man, or with more abundant provision and protection. As for this, he has ample provision and a wife who is better for him than a divorced woman, or chastity. And God is Bountiful, meaning: God was bountiful to them, in His provision for them and for others of His creation, Wise, in what He decreed between him and her of separation and divorce, and all the other meanings that we have come to know of the judgment between them in these verses and others, and in other than that of His rulings, management, and decrees in His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And if they separate, God will enrich each from His abundance, he said: Divorce. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
4:131: Abu Ja'far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: To God belongs all the dominion of what the seven heavens and the seven earths contain of all things. And He, may His praise be exalted, mentioned that after His statement: And if they separate, God will enrich each from His abundance, as a reminder from Him to His creation of the place of desire when one of them is separated from his wife, so that they may flee to Him when they are distressed by need, poverty, and loneliness due to separation from his home and his wife, and as a reminder from Him to them that He is the One who owns all things, and that He who owns all things, it is not impossible for Him to enrich him and everyone in need and want, and to comfort everyone in loneliness. Then He, the Most High, returned to the reproach of those who sought to harm the Banu Ubayraq and to their rebuke, and to the threat of doing what the apostate among them did, so He said: And We have enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you and upon you, meaning: And We have enjoined upon the People of the Scripture, and upon the People of the Torah and the Gospel, and upon you, meaning: And We have enjoined upon you and said to you and to them: Fear God, meaning: Beware of God lest you disobey Him and go against His commands and prohibitions, and if you disbelieve, meaning: And if you deny His command to you, O believers, and go against it, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning: You do not harm anyone by disobeying His command except yourselves, and do not count in your disbelief that you will be like the Jews and Christians, in the descent of His punishment upon you and the coming of His wrath upon you, as it happened to them when they changed His covenant and broke His pact, so He changed what they were in of a comfortable life and security of the flock, and made of them monkeys and pigs. This is because He owns all that the heavens and the earth contain, and nothing He wills with all of it and with any of it is impossible for Him, from honoring whomever He wills to honor, and humiliating whomever He wills to humiliate, and other than that of all matters, because the creation created Him, and they are in need and want of Him, and through Him is their strength and their survival, and their destruction and their annihilation, and He is the Rich One who has no need of anything, and no need befalls Him that would compel Him to you, O people, or to anyone else, and the Praiseworthy One who has made it obligatory for you, O creation, to praise Him for His praiseworthy deeds to you and His beautiful favors to you. So continue that, O people, by fearing Him and hastening to obey Him in what He commands you to do and forbids you from doing, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: And God is Rich and Praiseworthy, he said: Rich from His creation, Praiseworthy, he said: Praised by them.
4:132: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: To God belongs the kingdom of all that the heavens and the earth contain, and He is the Guardian of all of it, and the Preserver of all of it. Nothing of it escapes Him, and He is not burdened by its preservation and management, as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: And sufficient is God as a Disposer of affairs, he said: A Guardian. If someone says: What is the reason for repeating His statement: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in two verses, one after the other? It was said: He repeated that, because the meaning of the two reports about what is in the heavens and the earth in the two verses differs. That is because the report about him in one of the two verses: mentioning his need for his Creator, and his Creator’s independence from him - and in the other: his Creator’s preservation of him and his knowledge of him and his contemplation of him. If he says: Why was it not said: And God is Rich and Praiseworthy, and God is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs? It is said: What is in the verse in which He said: And God is Rich and Praiseworthy, is something that is suitable to conclude what was concluded with in describing God as Rich and that He is Praiseworthy, and what is not mentioned in it is suitable to conclude with describing Him with preservation and management. Therefore, He repeated His statement: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
4:133: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: If God wills, O people, He will take you away, that is, He will take you away by destroying and annihilating you, and bring others, that is, He will bring other people other than you to support and aid His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God is able to do that, that is, God is able to destroy you, annihilate you, and replace you with others other than you, and He is able, that is, He has the power to do that. Rather, God, the Most High, rebuked with these verses the traitors who betrayed the shield whose status we have described, whom God mentioned in His saying: And be not an advocate for the traitors (An-Nisa’: 55), and warned the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, not to be like them, and not to do what the apostate among them did in his apostasy and joining the polytheists, and He informed them that whoever among them did what he did, he will only harm himself, and no one will perish by his apostasy except himself, because he is the one in need - along with everything in the heavens and on the earth - of God, and God is independent of them. Then He threatened them in His saying: If He wills, He will do away with you, O mankind, and bring others, with destruction and extermination, if they did what the apostate Ibn Ubayriq Ta’mah did, and with replacing them with others other than them, to support His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and be his companions and support him in his religion, as He said in the other verse: But if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you (Muhammad 47:38). It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when it was revealed, he struck Salman’s back with his hand and said: They are the people of this, meaning the Persians. Likewise: It was narrated on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Saleh, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatada said about this: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: “If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others. And ever is God over that competent,” God, our Lord, is capable of that: to destroy whomever He wills of His creation, and bring others after them.
4:134: Abu Ja`far said: By that, the Most High means: Whoever wants, from among the hypocrites who show faith in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who conceal disbelief while they show faith, the reward of this world, meaning: the worldly life, by showing what he showed of faith with his tongue, then with God is the reward of this world, meaning: his reward in this world and his reward in it, which is what he gets from the spoils if he witnesses a scene with the Prophet, and he is safe for himself, his children, his wealth, and the like. As for his reward in the Hereafter, it is the fire of Hell. The meaning of the verse is: Whoever among the hypocrites works in this world, seeking through his work the reward of this world and its recompense from his work, then God will reward him with his reward in this world from this world, and his reward in the Hereafter from the Hereafter of punishment and chastisement. This is because God is capable of all of that, and He is the Owner of all of it, as He said in the other verse: “Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire. And what they did therein will be in vain, and what they used to do will be in vain.” (Hud 11:15, 16) Rather, what He, the Most High, meant by that were those who were involved in the affair of Banu Ubayraq, and those whom He described in His statement: “And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, God does not like anyone who is a traitor and sinful. They hide themselves from the people but do not hide themselves from God, and He is with them when they spend the night saying things that do not please Him.” (An-Nisa’: 107-108) and those who were similar to them in their actions and hypocrisy. And His statement: And God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, meaning: And God is All-Hearing of what these hypocrites say who want the reward of this world through their deeds, and their showing to the believers what they show to them when they meet the believers, and their saying to them: We believe, All-Seeing, meaning: And He has insight into them and into what they are doing, concealing from the believers, in what they conceal and do not show to them of the deceit and rancor that is in their hearts toward them.
4:135: This is what God Almighty has presented to His believing servants in Him and His Messenger: that they should do what those who sought out the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the matter of Banu Ubayraq, that he should excuse them for his companions, defend them, and improve their situation because they are people of need and poverty. God says to them: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, meaning: let it be among your morals and characteristics to stand firm in justice - meaning: in fairness - witnesses for God. Martyrs is the plural of martyr. The word witnesses is used to indicate that it is in the statement of God, who are guardians from the mention of those who believe. Its meaning is: “Be just to God when you testify - or: when you testify. “Even if it is against yourselves,” meaning: Even if your testimony is against yourselves, or against your parents or relatives, then be just and fair in it, and establish it on its basis by saying the truth in it, and do not favor a rich person over a poor person because of his wealth, nor favor a poor person over a rich person because of his poverty, lest you commit injustice. Indeed, God, who has made the judgment of the rich and the poor equal in what He has obligated you, O people, to establish the testimony for each of them with justice, is more deserving of them and more entitled to them than you, because He is their Owner and more deserving of them than you. He knows best what is in the interest of each of them in that and in all other matters than you. Therefore, He has commanded you to establish equality between them in testifying for and against them. So do not follow your own desires to be just, meaning: Do not follow your own desires in leaning in your testimony when you give it—for a rich person against a poor person, or for a poor person against a rich person—to one of the two parties, so that you say something other than the truth. Rather, establish it with justice, and testify to what God has commanded you to give, with justice to the one for and against whom you testify. If someone says: How can a witness testify against himself with justice? Does a witness testify against himself? It is said: Yes, and that is if he has a right due to someone else and he acknowledges it to him, so that is his establishing his testimony against himself. Abu Ja`far said: This verse, in my opinion, is a lesson from God, the Most High, to His believing servants, that they should do what the religion did, excuse the Banu Ubayraq, in their theft of what they stole, and their betrayal of what they betrayed of those mentioned before, in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their testimony for them before him of righteousness. So he said to them: If you stand to testify for or against a person, then speak in it with justice, even if your testimony is against yourselves, your fathers, and your relatives. And do not let the wealth of the one for whom you testify, or his poverty, or his kinship and blood relation to you, lead you to testify falsely for him, nor to abandon testifying against him with truth and concealing it. It was said that it was revealed as a lesson to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God, he said: It was revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and two men disputed before him: a rich man and a poor man. His side was with the poor man, and he believed that the poor man should not wrong the rich man. But God refused except that he should be just with the rich man and the poor man, so He said: “Whether he is rich or poor, God is more worthy of both of them. So follow not desire, lest you be just,” the verse. Others said something similar to what we said: It was revealed regarding testimony, as a command from God to the believers to treat those who testify equally, whether rich or poor, in their testimony. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God, even if it be against yourselves or your parents and relatives, he said: God commanded the believers to speak the truth even if it be against themselves or their parents or their children, and not to favor the rich because of his wealth, nor to have mercy on the poor because of his poverty, and that is His statement: “Whether he is rich or poor, God is more worthy of both of them. So follow not desire, lest you be just,” so that you abandon the truth and become unjust. Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, regarding the testimony of a father for his son and a relative. He said: This was the Sunnah of the early Muslims in the past, and they used to interpret the words of God in this regard: “O you who believe! Be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether he is rich or poor, God is more worthy of both of them.” The righteous early Muslims were not accused of the testimony of a father for his son, nor a son for his father, nor a brother for his brother, nor a man for his wife. Then people entered after that, and matters appeared among them that led the rulers to accuse them, so the testimony of those who were accused was abandoned, if it was from their relatives, and this became from the son and the father, the brother, the husband and the wife. Only these were accused at the end of time. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God, to the end of the verse, he said: Do not let the poverty of this man lead you to have mercy on him and not bear witness against him. He said: He says this to the witness. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God (al-Baqarah 2:170). This is about testimony. So establish testimony, O son of Adam, even if it is against yourself, or your parents, or your relatives, or the honor of your people. Indeed, testimony is for God, not for people. God is pleased with justice for Himself, and equity and justice are God’s scales on earth. By it, God responds to the harsh with the guest, the liar with the truthful, and the one who falsifies with the truth. And by justice, the truthful is believed, the liar is called a liar, the aggressor is repelled and humbled, our Lord, the Most High and Blessed. And by justice, people are set right, O son of Adam. Whether he be rich or poor, God is more worthy of both of them. He says: He is more worthy of your rich and your poor. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, which thing You have placed on earth is the least? He said: Justice is the least thing You have placed on earth. So do not let the wealth of a rich man or the poverty of a poor man prevent you from testifying against him with what you know, for that is the truth upon you. And the Most High said: God is more worthy of them both. It was said: Whether he is rich or poor, the verse, meaning: God is more deserving of the richness of the rich and the poverty of the poor. Because that is from Him and not from someone else, so He said: by them, and did not say by him. Others said: It was said: By them because he said: If he is rich or poor, so he did not mean a specific poor person or a specific rich person, and he is unknown. And if he is unknown, it is permissible to respond with the singular, dual, or plural. Those who said this statement mentioned that in Abu’s reading: God is more deserving of them. Others said: Or it means the letter waw in this place. Others said: It is permissible to dualize his statement: with them, because they have been mentioned, as was said: And if he has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a son (An-Nisa’: 12). It was said: It is permissible, because he implied from in it, as if it was said: If the one who disputed was rich or poor - meaning: rich or poor - then God is more deserving of them. The interpretation of his statement: So do not follow your own desires lest you deviate from the truth, is: from the truth, so that you transgress by not establishing the testimony of truth. If it was directed to its meaning: So do not follow your own desires to escape from deviating from the truth in establishing the testimony of justice, then that would be a correct interpretation. It has been said: The meaning of this is: Do not follow desires in order to be just, just as it is said: Do not follow your desires in order to please your Lord, meaning: I forbid you from it, just as you please your Lord by leaving it. Abu Jaafar said: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: He meant: And if you twist, O judges, in ruling for one of the two opponents over the other, or turn away, then God is ever, with what you do, Aware. They directed the meaning of the verse to the fact that it was revealed about the rulers, similar to the statement we mentioned from Al-Suddi, who said: The verse was revealed about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as we mentioned before. Who said that? Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus ibn Abi Thabyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, And if they distort or turn away, he said: They are two men sitting in front of the judge, and the judge has the right to have one of them turn away from the other. Others said: The meaning of that is: And if you, O witnesses, distort your testimonies and change them and do not establish them, or turn away from them and abandon them. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And if you twist or turn away, he said: If you twist with your tongues the testimony, or turn away from it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God, to His statement: But if you twist or turn away, he said: twist your tongue unjustly, which is stuttering, so you do not establish the testimony properly. Turning away means abandoning. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And if you distort, meaning, change the testimony, or turn away, he said: conceal it. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And if they distort, he said: by changing the testimony, or turning away, by concealing it. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And if they distort or turn away, he said: if they distort or leave it. Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And if they twist or turn aside, he said: They stutter or conceal. And this is in testimony. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And if they twist or turn away. As for twist, it means twisting the testimony and distorting it so that you cannot establish it. As for turn away, it means turning away from it and concealing it, and saying: I do not have testimony! Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: And if you twist, so you conceal the testimony, twisting some of it, or turning away from it and concealing it, and he refuses to have it testify against him, saying: I will conceal it from him because he is poor, so have mercy on him! He says: I will not establish the testimony against him. And by saying: This is a rich man, I will keep him and hope for what comes before him, so I will not testify against him! That is his saying: whether he is rich or poor. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And if you distort, they distort, or turn away, they leave. Muhammad bin Amara told us, he said, Hasan bin Atiyah told us, he said, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah, regarding his statement: And if you twist, he said: If you hesitate in the testimony and corrupt it, or turn away, he said: If you leave it. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And if they twist or turn away, he said: If they twist in the testimony, that is, that they do not present it correctly, or turn away, he said: Conceal the testimony. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said, Shaiban told us, that he used to say: And if they twist or turn away, meaning: they stuttered, or turned away, he said: leave it and do not bear witness. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And if they twist or turn away, as for twist, it means that a man twists his tongue unjustly. He means: in testimony. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in this regard is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it, that it is for the witness to testify for and against whom he testifies, and that is his distortion of it with his tongue, and his failure to establish it, in order to invalidate his testimony for whom he testified for, and against whom he testified. As for his turning away from it, it is his failure to perform it and carry it out, so he does not bear witness to it. We said: This interpretation is more correct, because God Almighty said: Be upholders of justice, witnesses, so He commanded them to uphold justice as witnesses. The most obvious meaning of the martyrs is what we mentioned of their description as witnesses. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And if you twist. This was read by most of the reciters of the cities except Kufa: And if they twist with two waws: from: lawani al-rajul haqqi and al-qawm yaluni din - that is, if they delay it - liya. A group of Kufa reciters read it: And if you twist with one waw. And for the one who reads this as well, there are two aspects: One of them: That the reciter intended to hamza the waw because it is a dhammah, then he dropped the hamza, so the i'rab of the hamza was in the lam because he dropped it, and one waw remained. It is as if he intended: talawu then he dropped the hamza. If this is the meaning, then its meaning is the meaning of the one who recited: wa-in-talawu with two waws, except that it contradicts what is known from the speech of the Arabs. That is because the second waw in his saying talawu is a plural waw, and it is a definite noun for a meaning, so it is not correct to hamza it, then he dropped it after hamza, so the definite noun for which the deleted waw was inserted is invalidated. The other aspect: that its reader is like that, he meant: that you follow from the state, so its meaning is: and that you follow the affairs of the people and leave. And this meaning - if the reader directs his reading to what we have described, to it - is outside the meanings of the people of interpretation, and what the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the followers directed the interpretation of the verse to. Abu Ja`far said: Since the corruption of that is clear from both aspects, the correct reading, which is not suitable to be read in our view, is: And if they twist or expose themselves, meaning: the twisting that is the delay. The interpretation of the statement is: If you refuse to bear witness properly to the one for whom you are obligated to bear witness, then you change it and alter it, or turn away from it and leave bearing witness for him, just as a man twists the debt of another man and pays him back what he owes him, delaying it, as Al-A’sha said: My religion beckons me during the day, and my religion requires me to sleep when sleep overtakes me. As for the interpretation of his statement: Indeed, God is All-Aware of what you do, he meant: Indeed, God is All-Aware of what you do, of your establishing the testimony and your distorting it, and your turning away from it by concealing it, All-Aware, meaning He has experience and knowledge of it, and He preserves that from you against you, until He rewards you with it as you will be rewarded for it in the Hereafter, the good-doer among you for his goodness, and the evil-doer for his evil. He says: So fear your Lord in that.
4:136: Abu Ja`far said: By that, the Most High means: O you who have believed, in the prophets and messengers who came before Muhammad, and believed in what they brought to them from God, Believe in God and His Messenger, meaning: Believe in God and in Muhammad, His Messenger, that he is God’s Messenger, sent to you and to all the nations before you, and the Book which He sent down to His Messenger, meaning: And believe in what Muhammad brought to you of the Book which God sent down to him, and that is the Qur’an, and the Book which He sent down before, meaning: And believe in the Book which God sent down before the Book which He sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is the Torah and the Gospel. If someone says: What is the reason for calling these people to believe in God, His Messenger, and His Books, when He called them believers? It is said: He, the Most High, did not call them believers, but rather described them as believers, and that is a description of them in a specific way of belief. That is because they were of two types: People of the Torah who believed in it and in those who brought it, and they disbelieved in the Gospel, the Qur’an, Jesus and Muhammad, may God’s prayers be upon them both; and a type of People of the Gospel, who believed in it and in the Torah and all the other books, but disbelieved in Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and the Criterion. So God, the Most High, said to them: O you who have believed, meaning: in what they believed of the books and messengers, believe in God and His Messenger, Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and the Book which He sent down to His Messenger, for you have known that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and you find his description in your books, and in the Book that was sent down before which you claim to believe, for you will not be believers in it while you are disbelievers in Muhammad, because your book commands you to believe in it and in what he brought you, so believe in your book in following Muhammad, otherwise you are disbelievers in it. This is the reason for commanding them to believe in what He commanded them to believe in, after He described them with what He described them with His saying: O you who have believed. As for his saying: And whoever disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, its meaning is: And whoever disbelieves in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denies his prophethood, has gone far astray. Rather, the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day, meaning: And whoever disbelieves in Muhammad and what he brought from God, because denying one of these things means denying all of them, and because the faith of any of creation is not valid except by believing in what God has commanded him to believe in, and disbelief in one of them is disbelief in all of them, so He said: And whoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day, after addressing the People of the Book and commanding them to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a threat from Him to them, and they acknowledge the oneness of God, the angels, the books, the messengers and the Last Day, except for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought of the Criterion. As for his saying: He has gone far astray, it means: He has strayed from the right path, and deviated from the straight path, to destruction, going far and unjustly. Because the disbelief of the one who disbelieves in that is his departure from the religion of God which He has prescribed for His servants. And departing from the religion of God is the destruction in which there is ruin, and straying from guidance is misguidance.
4:137: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its interpretation is: Those who believed in Moses, then disbelieved in him, then believed - meaning: the Christians - in Jesus, then disbelieved in him, then increased in disbelief in Muhammad, God will not forgive them nor guide them to a way. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief, they are the Jews and Christians. The Jews believed in the Torah, then disbelieved, and the Christians believed in the Gospel, then disbelieved. Their disbelief in it means that they abandoned it, then they increased in disbelief in the Criterion and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God said: It was not for God to forgive them, nor to guide them to a way, meaning: God would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a path of guidance, and they disbelieved in the Book of God and in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, he said: These are the Jews, they believed in the Torah, then disbelieved. Then he mentioned the Christians, then he said: Then they believed, then they disbelieved, then they increased in disbelief, meaning: They believed in the Gospel, then they disbelieved in it, then they increased in disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that were the hypocrites, who believed then apostatized, then believed then apostatized, then increased in disbelief by dying in disbelief. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief, he said: We used to think that they were hypocrites, and that includes those who were like them, and then increased in disbelief, he said: They remained in their disbelief until they died. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Then they increased in disbelief, he said: They died. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Then they increased in disbelief, he said: until they died. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: Those who believed and then disbelieved, the verse, he said: These are the hypocrites, they believed twice, disbelieved twice, then they increased in disbelief after that. Others said: Rather, they are the people of the two books, the Torah and the Gospel. They committed sins in their disbelief and then repented, but their repentance was not accepted from them, while they remained in their disbelief. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief, he said: They are the Jews and Christians. They sinned in their polytheism, then repented, but their repentance was not accepted. If they had repented from polytheism, it would have been accepted from them. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these statements in interpreting the verse is the statement of the one who said: What is meant by that are the People of the Book who acknowledged the ruling of the Torah, then denied it by contradicting it, then those among them who acknowledged Jesus and the Gospel, then denied it by contradicting it, then denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Criterion, so their denial of it increased their disbelief upon their disbelief. We said that this is more correct in interpreting this verse, because the verse before it is in the stories of the People of the Two Books - I mean His statement: O you who have believed, believe in God and His Messenger - and there is no evidence that His statement: Indeed, those who believed and then disbelieved is disconnected! Its meaning is from the meaning of what came before it, so it is more appropriate to attach it to what came before it, until there comes evidence that it is disconnected from it. As for his statement: God would not forgive them, it means: God would not conceal their disbelief and sins by pardoning them from punishment for it, but rather He would expose them before all witnesses. Nor would He guide them to a way, he says: He would not direct them to the path of truth and grant them success in it, but He would abandon them from it, as a punishment for their great crime and their audacity towards their Lord. Some people have said that the apostate should be given three times to repent, based on this verse, and others have disagreed with them on this, mentioning those who said: He should be given three times to repent. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ali, peace be upon him, who said: If I were to ask the apostate to repent three times. Then he recited this verse: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: The apostate is given three times to repent. Then he recited: Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said: The apostate is given three times to repent. Others said: He is called to repentance every time he apostatizes. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, on the authority of someone who heard Ibrahim say: The apostate is asked to repent every time he apostatizes. Abu Ja`far said: In establishing the argument that the apostate should be given the opportunity to repent the first time, there is clear evidence that the ruling for each time he apostatizes from Islam is the same as the ruling for the first time, in that his repentance is accepted and his conversion to Islam makes his blood inviolable. This is because the reason for which his blood was inviolable the first time was his conversion to Islam. It is not permissible for the reason for which his blood was inviolable in the first case to exist, and then for his blood to be permissible despite its existence, unless there is a distinction between the ruling for the first time and all other times, which must be accepted as a firm principle, and in this case it is excluded from the ruling of analogy.
4:138: Abu Jaafar said: By His saying, may His praise be glorified: Give good tidings to the hypocrites, He informed the hypocrites. We have explained the meaning of evangelism in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. That they will have a painful punishment, meaning: that on the Day of Resurrection they will have from God, for their hypocrisy, a painful punishment, which is the painful punishment, and that is the punishment of Hell.
4:139: Abu Ja'far said: As for the words of God, the Most High: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, this is a description of the hypocrites. God says to His Prophet: O Muhammad, give glad tidings to the hypocrites who take the people of disbelief in Me and atheism in My religion as friends - meaning: supporters and friends - instead of the believers, meaning: from the non-believers. Do they seek honor with them? He says: Do they seek protection and strength from them, by taking them as allies instead of the people of faith in Me? For indeed, all honor belongs to God, He says: For those whom they took from the disbelievers as allies, seeking honor with them, are the humiliated and few. So why did they not take the believers as allies, so that they might seek honor, protection, and victory from God, who has honor and protection, who honors whomever He wills and humiliates whomever He wills, so He honors them and protects them? The root of honor is severity. Hence, the word ‘Azzaz refers to hard, solid ground. It is also said: It is difficult for the patient, if his illness is severe and he is about to recover. It is also said: The meat is difficult, if it is severe. Hence, it is said: It is difficult for me that such and such should be, meaning: It is difficult for me.
4:140: Abu Ja`far said: By that, the Most High means: Give good tidings to the hypocrites, who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, and it has already been revealed to you in the Book, meaning: He informed those of these hypocrites who took the disbelievers as supporters and allies after what was revealed to them of the Qur’an, that when you hear the verses of God being denied and ridiculed, then do not sit with them until they engage in a different conversation, meaning: after they learned that God forbade sitting with the disbelievers who disbelieve in the proofs of God and the verses of His Book and ridicule them - until they engage in a different conversation, meaning by His saying: engage, they talk about a different conversation, that they will have a painful punishment. And His statement: Indeed, then you are like them, means: It has been revealed to you that if you sit with someone who disbelieves in the verses of God and mocks them while you are listening, then you are like him, meaning: If you do not leave them in that situation, then you are like them in their actions, because you have disobeyed God by sitting with them while you are listening to the verses of God being disbelieved in and mocked, just as they disobeyed Him by mocking the verses of God. So you have committed a disobedience to God similar to what you were averse to, so you are like them in your committing the disobedience to God and your doing what God has forbidden you from. This verse clearly indicates the prohibition of sitting with people of falsehood of all kinds, including innovators and immoral people, when they engage in their falsehood. In a similar vein, a group of past imams said, interpreting this verse as meaning the prohibition of watching every falsehood when its people engage in it. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: A man may say a false word in a gathering to make his companions laugh, and God will be angry with them. He said: So I mentioned that to Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and he said: Abu Wa’il is right. Is it not in the Book of God: “When you hear the verses of God being denied and ridiculed, then do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation. If you do, then you will be like them”? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Munhal, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, he said: Umar bin Abdul Aziz took some people for drinking and beat them, and among them was a fasting person. They said: This one is fasting! Then he recited: “So do not sit with them until they engage in a talk other than that. If you do, you will be like them.” Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: That when you hear the verses of God being denied and ridiculed, and his statement: And do not follow other paths, for they will separate you from His path (al-An’am 6:53), and his statement: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein (al-Shura 42:13), and similar to this from the Qur’an. He said: God commanded the believers to remain in congregation, and forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them: Those who came before you were destroyed only by disputation and disputes in the religion of God. And His statement: Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell, all together, means: God will gather the two groups of people of disbelief and hypocrisy on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire, so He will reconcile between them in His punishment in Hell and His painful torment, just as they agreed in this world and gathered in enmity against the believers, and cooperated in discouraging people from the religion of God - and from that which He was pleased with and commanded - and its people. There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And it has been revealed to you in the Book. The majority of readers read this with a damma on the letter noon and a heavy and shaddah on the letter zay, in a way that does not name the doer. Some of the Kufians read it with a fatha on the noon and a shaddah on the zay, meaning: And God has sent down upon you. Some of the Meccans read: And He has sent down upon you, with a fatha on the noon and a shaddah on the zay, meaning: And it has come to you from God that if you hear. Abu Ja`far said: There is no meaning in these three readings that is far removed from what the speech implies. However, the reading I have chosen is the reading of the one who reads: And it was revealed with a damma on the nun and a shaddah on the zay, in the manner of what its agent is not named. Because the meaning of the speech is to precede what I described before, in the sense of: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of God they are denied to His saying: A hadith other than His, Do you seek honor with them? So his saying: For honor belongs to God entirely, means to delay, and therefore the damma of the nun in His saying: It was revealed is more correct in our view in this place. They also differed in the reading of his statement: And the Book which He sent down to His Messenger and the Book which He sent down before. Most of the readers read it with the opening of nazal and anzal, meaning: the book that God revealed to His Messenger, and the book that was revealed before. Some of the Basran reciters read it with a damma on both letters, meaning that whose agent is not named. They are close in meaning. However, the fatha in this is more pleasing to me than the damma, because the mention of God had occurred before that in His statement: Believe in God and His Messenger.
4:141: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: those who lie in wait for you, is those who wait, O believers, for you, so if you have a victory from God, meaning: if God grants you a victory from your enemy, and gives you spoils of war, they will say, to you, were we not with you, fighting your enemy and raiding them with you, so give us a share of the spoils, for we have witnessed the fighting with you, and if the disbelievers have a share, meaning: if your enemies from the disbelievers have a share of you, by inflicting harm on you, they will say, meaning: these hypocrites will say to the disbelievers, did we not gain control over you, did we not overcome you until you overpowered the believers, and protect you from them, by discouraging them until they resisted you and turned away, then God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, meaning: so God will judge between the believers and the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, and will decide between you. By the decisive judgment, by admitting the people of faith into His Paradise, and the people of hypocrisy with their allies from the infidels into His Hellfire, And God will not give the infidels a way over the believers, meaning: an argument on the Day of Resurrection. This is a promise from God to the believers that He will not let the hypocrites enter Paradise as they did, nor will the believers enter Paradise as the hypocrites did. Thus, the disbelievers will have an argument against the believers, saying to them, if they enter as they did: “Here you are, you were our enemies in this world, and the hypocrites were our allies, and now you have gathered in the Fire, and He has gathered you with our allies! So where is that for which you claimed you were fighting us in this world?” This is the way that God has promised the believers that He will not make it for the disbelievers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: If you have a victory from God, he said: The hypocrites lie in wait for the Muslims. If you have a victory, he said: If the Muslims take spoils from their enemy, the hypocrites say: Were we not with you, we were with you, so give us spoils like what you take. And if the disbelievers have a share, they take from the Muslims, the hypocrites say to the disbelievers: Did we not gain control over you and protect you from the believers, we were discouraging them from you. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of His statement: Did We not gain control over you? Some of them said: It means: Did we not defeat you? Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: Have We not gained control over you? He said: We have overcome you. Others said: The meaning of this is: Did we not make clear to you that I am with you in what you are doing? Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Did We not gain control over you? Did We not make it clear to you that I am with you in what you are upon. Abu Ja`far said: These two statements are close in meaning. That is because whoever interpreted it to mean: Did we not make clear to you, what he meant - God willing - is: Did we not overcome you with what we made clear to you that I am with you? The root of the word istihsala in the speech of the Arabs, as far as we have been informed, is to prevail, and from this is the statement of God Almighty: Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of God (Al-Mujadilah: 9), meaning: overcame them. It is said from this: haza’a ‘alayhi and istihdha’a, yahidh and lamjtih, and ahaza’a yahidh. From the language of those who say haza’a, is the statement of Al-`Ajjaj in describing a bull and a dog: He has a coachman Some of them chanted: He owns them and I own them They are close in meaning. From the language of those who say ahadh, is the saying of Labid in describing a donkey and a female donkey: If I meet and I take its sides and bring it on a long crooked path He means by his saying: And I take control of both sides of it, he overcame it and subdued it until he took control of both sides of it, and nothing of it deviated from it. The analogy in his saying: The devil has gained control over them (al-Mujadilah 58:9) is that it should come: He gained control over them, because if the waw is the root of the verb and it is moved with a fatha and what precedes it is still, the Arabs put its movement in the fa of the verb before it, and they change it to an alif, following the movement of what precedes it, like their saying: This thing has changed from what it was, from Hala yahwul he changes, and so-and-so is enlightened by the light of God, from ash-Shura consultation, and he sought refuge with God from the tormentor of huwadh he is tormented. And perhaps this is based on its origin, as Labid said: And I gain control over them, and he did not say And I gain control over them. And with this language came the Qur’an in his saying: The devil has gained control over them (al-Mujadilah 58:19). As for his saying: Then God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. There is no disagreement among them that its meaning is: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers on that Day. Mention the report about who said that: Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Jarir narrated, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Dhirr, on the authority of Yasee’ Al-Hadrami, he said: I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, when a man said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you think of the words of God: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers, while they fight us and are victorious and killed? Ali said to him: Come closer, come closer! Then he said: And God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers, on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Ath-Thawri narrated, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Dhir, on the authority of Yas’i’ al-Kindi, regarding the statement of God, And never will God grant the disbelievers a way over the believers, he said: A man came to Ali bin Abi Talib and said: How is this verse: And never will God grant the disbelievers a way over the believers? Ali said: Bring him closer, For God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never grant on the Day of Resurrection, the disbelievers a way over the believers. Ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Dhir, on the authority of Yas’i’ al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ali, similarly. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, he said: I heard Sulayman narrating, on the authority of Dhir, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said regarding this verse: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers, he said: In the Hereafter. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik: And God will not give the disbelievers a way over the believers, on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And God will not give the disbelievers a way over the believers, he said: That is on the Day of Resurrection. As for the way, in this place, it is the argument, as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers, he said. An argument.
4:142: Abu Ja`far said: We have previously demonstrated the meaning of the hypocrite’s deception of his Lord, and the way God deceived them, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place, despite the differences of those who differ on that. The interpretation of this is: The hypocrites deceive God by securing their blood and wealth through their hypocrisy. God deceives them by what He has decreed concerning them of preventing their blood from being shed because of what they have shown with their tongues of faith, while He knows what is in their innermost thoughts and their belief in disbelief, as a means of His luring them into this world, until they meet Him in the Hereafter, and He will cause them to enter the fire of Hell because of what they have concealed of disbelief, as: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: The hypocrites deceive God, but He deceives them. He said: He will give them on the Day of Resurrection a light with which they will walk with the Muslims as they were with them in the world, then He will take that light away from them and extinguish it, and they will stand in their darkness, and a wall will be placed between them. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj said: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but He is the One who deceives them. He said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy and Abu Aabir bin Al-Nu’man, and about the hypocrites, They seek to deceive God, but He is the One who deceives them. He said: Like His statement in Surat al-Baqarah 2:They seek to deceive God and those who believe, but they deceive none but themselves. He said: As for His statement, And He is the One who deceives them, He says: Regarding the light that the hypocrites are given along with the believers, so they are given the light, and when they reach the wall it is taken away, and what God mentioned in His statement, Wait for us that we may take from your light. He said: His statement, And He is the One who deceives them. Ibn Wakee’ narrated that Yazid ibn Harun narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn on the authority of Al-Hasan that when he recited: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but it is He who deceives them, he said: A light will be cast upon every believer and hypocrite by which they will walk, until when they reach the path, the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished, and the believers will proceed with their light, and they will call out to them: Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light, until His statement: But you tempted yourselves (al-Hadid 57:13-4). Al-Hasan said: That is how God deceived them. As for his statement: And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to people, it means that the hypocrites do not do any of the deeds that God has imposed on the believers in order to draw closer to God, because they are not certain of the afterlife, nor reward, nor punishment. Rather, they do the outward deeds that they do in order to preserve themselves, and to beware of the believers being killed or their money stolen. So when they stand for prayer, which is one of the outward obligations, they stand lazily to it, showing off to the believers so that they think they are among them, but they are not, because they do not believe in its obligation and necessity upon them. So they are lazy in their standing for it, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, he said: By God, if it were not for the people, the hypocrite would not have prayed, and he only prays for show and to be heard. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, he said: They are the hypocrites. If it were not for showing off, they would not have prayed. As for his saying: And they do not remember God except a little, perhaps someone might say: Is there anything little in remembering God? It was said to him: The meaning of that - contrary to what you have said - is: They do not remember God except for hypocrisy, to ward off from themselves killing, captivity, and the theft of money, not a remembrance that is certain and believes in the Oneness of God, sincerely devoting itself to Him as Lord. That is why God called it little, because it is not intended for God, nor is it sought to draw near to God, nor is it intended for the reward of God and what is with Him. So, even if it is frequent, from the aspect of the accusative of its agent and its mentioner, it is in the meaning of a mirage that has an appearance without the reality of water. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, he said: Al-Hasan recited: And they do not remember God except a little, he said: It is only a little because it was for someone other than God. Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they do not remember God except a little, he said: The hypocrite is only mentioned because God did not accept him. And everything that God rejects is little, and everything that God accepts is much.
4:143: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty means by His saying: wavering, hesitating. The origin of oscillation is movement and disturbance, as Al-Nabigha said: Have you not seen that God has given you a surah, and every king is weak before it? God meant by that: that the hypocrites are confused in their religion, and do not return to relying on anything as correct. They are neither with the believers in insight, nor with the polytheists in ignorance, but they are confused between that. Their example is the example that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them, which is: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated it, he said: Ubaydullah narrated it, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The example of the hypocrite is that of a stray sheep between two flocks, it goes to this one one time and to that one another time, it does not know which of them to follow! Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us a second time, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab, and he attributed it to Ibn Umar, but he did not trace it back to the Prophet. He said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated it to us twice likewise. Imran bin Bakkar told me, he said, Abu Ruh told us, he said, Ibn Ayyash told us, he said, Ubaidullah bin Omar told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Omar, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Wavering between that, neither with these nor with those, meaning: They are not polytheists who show polytheism, and they are not believers. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Wavering between that, neither with these nor with those, meaning: They are not sincere believers, nor openly polytheists. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, used to give an example for the believer, the hypocrite, and the disbeliever, like a group of three who were pushed into a river. The believer fell and was cut off, then the hypocrite fell until he was about to reach the believer, then the disbeliever called out to him: Come to me, for I fear for you! And the believer called out to him: Come to me, for I have you and you have me! He counted for him what he had. So the hypocrite continued to waver between them until he was overcome by harm and drowned. And the hypocrite continued to be in doubt and suspicion until death came upon him while he was in that state. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: The example of a hypocrite is like that of a she-goat between two sheep. It saw a sheep on a high ridge and approached it but did not recognize it. Then it saw a sheep on a high ridge and approached it and sniffed it but did not recognize it. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: wavering, he said: the hypocrites. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Wavering between that, neither with these nor with those, meaning: neither with the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor with these Jews. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement: wavering between that, he said: They did not purify their faith so that they would be with the believers, and not with the polytheists. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: wavering between that, between Islam and disbelief, neither with these nor with those. As for his statement: And he whom God leaves astray, you will never find for him a way, it means: he whom God lets down from the path of guidance, which is Islam to which God has called His servants. He says: he whom God lets down from it and does not guide him to it, you will never find for him, O Muhammad, a way, meaning: a path to take to the truth other than Islam. And what path can he have to the truth other than Islam? God, the Most High, has informed us that whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will not be accepted from him, and he whom God leads astray from it has gone astray and has no guide other than Him.
4:144: Abu Jaafar said: This is a prohibition from God to His believing servants from adopting the morals of the hypocrites, who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, and thus be like them in committing what He prohibited them from, which is befriending His enemies. God Almighty says to them: O you who believe in God and His Messenger, do not befriend the disbelievers and support them instead of the believers who are your people and religion, lest you be like those hypocrites who are obligated to Hell. Then He, the Most High, said, threatening those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, if they do not refrain from their friendship and refrain from their opposition, that He will include them with the people of their alliance from the hypocrites whom He ordered His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give them the good report that they will have a painful punishment: Do you want, O you who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers who have believed in Me and My Messenger, to make for God a clear authority over you, meaning: an argument, by taking the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, so that you deserve from Him what the hypocrites deserved, whose description He described to you and informed you of their place with Him, clear, meaning: clarifying its truth and reality. He says: Do not expose yourselves to the wrath of God by making an argument against yourselves in your precedence over what your Lord has forbidden you from, which is friendship with His enemies and the people of disbelief in Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention who said that. Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada: “O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to make for God a clear authority over you?” He said: God has authority over His creation, but He says: a clear excuse. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Whatever authority is in the Qur’an, then it is proof. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: a clear authority, he said: an argument. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
4:145: Abu Jaafar said: God Almighty means by His saying: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of Hell, that the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of Hell. Each of the levels of Hell is a darak. There are two pronunciations for it: darak, with the ra pronounced with a fatha, and darak, with a sukoon on it. Whoever pronounces the ra with a fatha, the plural of adrak in the rare case, and daruk in the many case, if he wishes. Whoever pronounces the ra with a sukoon, says three adrak, and for the many, daruk. There are different readings of this: The majority of the people of Medina and Basra read it in the Darak with the opening of the Ra.
