The majority of the people of Kufa read it with a sukoon on the letter ra. Abu Ja`far said: They are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites is correct, because the meaning is the same, and the recitation with each of them is widespread in the Islamic recitation. However, I have seen scholars of Arabic mention that the opening of the ra’ in it is more common among the Arabs than its sukoon. And they have narrated that they heard it say: Give me a dirham by which I can connect my rope, and that is when he asks for something to connect his rope that is unable to reach the well. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of Abdullah: The hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of Hellfire. He said: In iron coffins, covered over them. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The hypocrites are in iron coffins locked around them in the Fire. Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Dhakwan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: The hypocrites are in the lowest depths of Hell. He said: In coffins that shake over them. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, meaning: in the lowest depths of the Fire. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abdullah bin Katheer told me regarding his statement: In the lowest depths of Hellfire, he said: We heard that Hell has levels, levels. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of Abdullah: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, he said, coffins of fire that will close over them. As for his statement, And you will never find for them a helper, it means: And you will never find for these hypocrites, O Muhammad, from God - if He places them in the lowest depths of the Fire - a helper who will support them from Him, save them from His punishment, and ward off from them His painful chastisement.
4:146: Abu Ja'far said: This is an exception from God, the Most High. He has made an exception for those who repent from their hypocrisy if they reform, and sincerely dedicate their religion to God alone, and disavow all gods and rivals, and believe in His Messenger, that they will be with those who persist in their hypocrisy until their deaths come to them - in the Hereafter - and that they will enter their entrances into Hell. Rather, the Most High has promised them that He will place them with the believers in a place of honor, and that He will make them dwell with them in their dwellings in Paradise. He has promised them a great reward for their repentance, saying: And God will give the believers a great reward. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the verse is: Except those who repent, meaning: they return to the truth, and return to acknowledging the Oneness of God and believing in His Messenger and what he brought from his Lord from their hypocrisy, and reform, meaning: and reform their actions, so they do what God has commanded them to do, and perform His obligations, and refrain from what He has forbidden them from, and are deterred from His disobedience, and hold fast to God, meaning: and hold fast to the covenant of God. We have previously demonstrated that holding fast means adhering to and clinging to God. Holding fast to God means holding fast to His covenant and pledge that He has entrusted to His creation in His Book, to obey Him and refrain from disobeying Him. And they sincerely devoted their religion to God, meaning: And they sincerely devoted their obedience and the deeds they do to God, so they intended Him by them, and they did not do them to show off to people, nor out of doubt about their religion, nor out of suspicion that God would take account of what they did, so He will reward the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil. Rather, they did them with certainty in the reward of the doer of good for his good, and the recompense of the doer of evil for his evil, or that his Lord would be gracious to him and forgive him, drawing closer to God by them, intending thereby the face of God. So that is the meaning of: their sincerely devoted their religion to God. Then He, the Most High, said: Then those will be with the believers. He said: So those whose characteristics He described among the hypocrites after their repentance, reform, adherence to God, and sincerity in their religion, that is: with the believers in Paradise, not with the hypocrites who died in their hypocrisy, whom He promised the lowest level of Hell. Then he said: And God will give the believers a great reward, meaning: And God will give those who have this description, for their repentance, reform, adherence to God, sincerity in their religion to Him, and their faith, a great reward, and that is: degrees in Paradise, just as He gave those who died in hypocrisy homes in Hell, which is the lowest part of it. Because God, may He be glorified and praised, promised His believing servants that He would give them that for their faith, just as He threatened the hypocrites for their hypocrisy with what He mentioned in His Book. This statement is the meaning of the statement of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, they said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Hudhayfah said: A people who were hypocrites will enter Paradise! Abdullah said: How do you know that? Hudhayfah became angry, then he stood up and stepped aside. When they dispersed, Alqamah passed by him and called him and said: Your companion knows what you said! Then he recited: “Except for those who repent, amend, hold fast to God and are sincere in their religion to God. Those will be with the believers. And God will give the believers a great reward.”
4:147: Abu Ja`far said: What God Almighty means by His saying: What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? What would God do, O hypocrites, with your punishment if you repent to God and return to the right that is due to God upon you, and thank Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon you in yourselves, your families, and your children, by turning to His Oneness, holding fast to Him, and making your actions sincere for His sake, and abandoning showing off to people, and believing in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in him, and acknowledging what he brought to you from Him and acting upon it? He says: God has no need to place you in the lowest level of Hell if you return to His obedience and return to doing what He has commanded you to do and abandoning what He has forbidden you to do, because He does not bring any benefit to Himself through your punishment, nor does He ward off any harm from Himself. Rather, His punishment is from those He punishes among His creation, as a reward from Him for their boldness towards Him, for their disobedience to His command and prohibition, and their ingratitude for His blessings upon them. If you thank Him for His blessings, and obey Him in His commands and prohibitions, then He has no need to punish you. Rather, He will thank you for your obedience and gratitude to Him, by rewarding you for that with what your hopes and dreams fall short of, and your aspirations do not reach. And God is ever Appreciative of you and His servants for their obedience to Him by giving them a generous reward for it, and by giving them a great compensation for it. Knowing of what you do, O hypocrites, and others like you, of good and evil, righteous and wicked. He has measured all of that against you, encompassing all of it, until He rewards you with your reward on the Day of Resurrection, the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil. And: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And God is ever Appreciative and Knowing. He said: God, may His praise be glorified, does not punish a grateful or a believing person.
4:148: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of that differed. So I read it as most of the countries read it with a damma on the letter dhaal. Some of them read it: Except for those who wrong, with the letter dhaal open. Then those who read it with the dhammah of the Ḍā’ differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of this is that God Almighty does not like any of us to supplicate loudly against anyone, and that, according to them, is slandering someone, except for someone who has been wronged. He says: except for someone who has been wronged, so he supplicates against his oppressor, for God Almighty does not dislike that for him, because He has given him permission to do so. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: God does not like the public mention of evil, meaning: God does not like for a person to supplicate against someone, except if he is wronged, for He has permitted him to supplicate against the one who wronged him, and that is His statement: Except for the one who has been wronged, and if he is patient, then it is better for him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged, for He likes the public mention of evil. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: “God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And ever is God Hearing and Knowing.” God excuses the wronged as you hear: that he should supplicate. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abu Ubaid told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: It is a man who wrongs another man, so he should not supplicate against him, but rather he should say: O God, help me against him, O God, extract my right for me, O God, come between him and what he wants, and similar supplications. So, according to Ibn Abbas, the word min is in the nominative case. Because he directed it to the fact that speaking evil aloud is in the sense of supplication, and he excluded the oppressed from it. So the meaning of the speech according to his statement was: God does not like evil to be spoken aloud, except by the oppressed, so there is no blame on him for speaking it aloud. This is a doctrine that Arabists consider to be an error in Arabic. That is because, according to them, it is not permissible for a nominative to be with a voiced letter, because it is in the connection of an and has not been denied, so it is not permissible to connect it with it. According to them, it is an error to say: I do not like it if anyone stands up except Zaid. It may be possible that it is from the accusative, according to the interpretation of the statement of Ibn Abbas, and his statement: God does not like the public mention of evil speech, is a complete statement, then it was said: except for one who is wronged, then there is no blame upon him, so it is from an exception from the action, even if there was nothing apparent before the exception from which an exception could be made, as God, the Most High, said: You have no control over them, except for he who turns away and disbelieves (al-Ghashiyah 88:22-23), and like their statement: I hate argumentation and dispute, O God, except for a man who intends God by that, and nothing of the names was mentioned before it. And min, according to this statement of Al-Hasan, is in the accusative case, as it is an exception to the meaning of the statement, not to the noun, as we mentioned before in the interpretation of the statement of Ibn Abbas, if min is directed to the accusative case, and like the statement of the speaker: It was such and such of the matter, O God, except that so-and-so, may God reward him with good, did such and such. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: God does not like the public mention of evil, except for someone who has been wronged, so he tells what has been done to him. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It is a man who visits a man and does not treat him well, so he leaves him and says: He treated me badly and did not treat him well! Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Except for he who has been wronged, he said: Except for he who has been affected by what was said to him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. He said: He is the guest who has moved his luggage, for he speaks evil to his companion. Others said: What he meant by that is that a man descends upon a man and does not acknowledge him, so he is harmed by the one who did not acknowledge him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Except for he who has been wronged, he said: Except for he who has been wronged and then takes revenge, he speaks out against evil. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, the same. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid: God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. He said: It is the man who comes to another man and does not treat him well, so God has given him permission to say something about him. Ahmad bin Hammad Al-Dulabi told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mujahid, God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. He said: It is in hospitality. A man comes to the people and stays with them, but they do not host him. God has given him permission to speak about them. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Muthanna bin al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: God does not like that evil be spoken aloud, the verse, he said: A man hosted another man but did not fulfill his hospitality. When he left, he told the people and said: I hosted so-and-so but he did not fulfill my hospitality! That is speaking ill of others, except for one who has been wronged, when his hospitality was not fulfilled. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: Except for the one who has been wronged and then takes revenge, he speaks ill of others. Mujahid said: It was revealed about a man who hosted a man in a deserted area, so he refused to host him, so the verse: Except for the one who has been wronged was revealed. It was mentioned that he did not host him, he did not do more than that. Others said: The meaning of this is: except for the one who is wronged and takes revenge on his oppressor, for God has permitted him to do so. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: God does not like the public mention of evil except by someone who has been wronged. He says: God does not like the public mention of evil by anyone among creation, but if someone is wronged and takes revenge in the same way as he was wronged, then there is no blame upon him. So, according to these sayings that we mentioned, except for the saying of Ibn Abbas, it is in the accusative case because it is disconnected from the beginning. And it is the custom of the Arabs to put what comes after the accusative except in the disconnected exception. The meaning of the speech on these sayings, except for the saying of Ibn Abbas: God does not like the public mention of evil speech, but if someone is wronged, there is no blame on him for telling what was done to him, or for taking revenge on the one who wronged him. Others read it with the opening of the Dhad: except for the one who wrongs, and they interpreted it as: God does not like the public mention of evil, except for the one who has been wronged, so there is no problem with the public mention of evil to him. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: My father used to recite: God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. Ibn Zayd said: He means: Except for one who persists in that hypocrisy, so he speaks ill of him until he desists. He said: This is like: “And do not insult one another by nicknames. Evil is the name of immorality” (al-Hujurat 49:11), that you call him immoral, after believing (al-Hujurat 49:11), after he had been a believer, and whoever does not repent (al-Hujurat 49:11), from that action for which he was told, then it is those who are the wrongdoers (al-Hujurat 49:11). He said: He is worse than those who said that. Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement: God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged, so he recited: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire until he reached And God will give the believers a great reward. Then he said after he said: They are in the lowest depths of the Fire, What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And ever is God Appreciative and Knowing. God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. He said: God does not like it to be said to this one: Were you not a hypocrite? Were you not the hypocrite who wronged and did and did? after he has repented, except by one who has been wronged, except by one who persists in hypocrisy. He said: My father used to say that to him, and he recited it: except by one who has been wronged. So, according to this interpretation, it is an erection because it is related to the loudness. The interpretation of the statement, according to the one who said this statement: God does not like anyone to speak ill of any of the hypocrites, except for one of them who has been wronged and persists in his hypocrisy, then there is no harm in speaking ill of him. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: except for the one who wrongs with a dhammah on the dhal, due to the consensus of the proof of the readings and the people of interpretation on its correctness, and the anomaly of the reading of the one who reads it with a fathah. Since this is the more correct of the two readings, then the correct interpretation of this is: God does not like, O people, for anyone to speak ill of anyone, except for one who has been wronged, meaning: except for one who has been wronged, so there is no blame on him for telling what has been wronged to him. If that is what it means, then it includes informing someone who has not acknowledged him, or has been treated badly, or has been wronged in his person or money, other than him from among all people. Likewise, his supplication against someone who has been wronged: that God will grant him victory over him, because in his supplication against him is an announcement from him to whoever hears his supplication against him of evil for him. Since this is the case, then min is in the accusative case, because it is disconnected from what precedes it, and because there are no names before it from which to exclude, so it is similar to His statement: You have no control over them, except for those who turn away and disbelieve (al-Ghashiyah 88:22-23). As for His statement: And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, it means: And God is All-Hearing, of what you say aloud of evil to those to whom you say it aloud, and other than that of your voices and speech, All-Knowing, of what you conceal of evil speech and speech to those to whom you conceal it but do not say it aloud to them. He has recorded all of that against you, until He recompenses you for all of that with your recompense, the evildoer for his evil, and the gooddoer for his good.
4:149: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying, If you disclose, O people, good, is that if you say something nice to someone who has done you good, and you show that out of gratitude to him for what he did to you of good, or conceal it, is that if you refrain from showing that and do not show it, or pardon an evil, is that if you forgive someone who has done you evil, and you do not speak ill of him in the manner that you have been permitted to speak ill of him, then indeed, God is Forgiving, is that He has always been forgiving of His creation, pardoning those who disobey Him and go against His command, Powerful, is that He has the ability to take revenge on them. What he means by this is that God has always been forgiving of His servants, even though He has the ability to punish them for their disobedience to Him. He says: So forgive, you too, O people, whoever comes to you unjustly, and do not speak ill of him, even if you are able to offend him, just as your Lord forgives you, even though He is able to punish you, even though you disobey Him and go against His command. In the words of God the Most High: Whether you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an offense - indeed, God is ever Pardoning and Powerful, there is a clear indication that the interpretation of His words: God does not like that evil be uttered aloud except by one who has been wronged, is contrary to the interpretation given by Zayd ibn Aslam, who claimed that it means: God does not like that evil be uttered aloud to the hypocrites, except by one who persists in his hypocrisy, for there is no harm in speaking ill of him aloud. This is because God the Most High said after that: Whether you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an offense, and it is reasonable that God the Most High did not command the believers to pardon the hypocrites for their hypocrisy, nor did He forbid them from calling those among them who openly commit hypocrisy a hypocrite. Rather, pardoning that is something that has no rational basis, because the pardon that is understood is a person’s overlooking of what he has against another of rights. Calling a hypocrite by his name is not a right for anyone against him, so he is commanded to pardon him, but it is only a name for him. It is not clear what is meant by calling something by its name.
4:150: Abu Ja`far said: What is meant by the words of God, the Most High: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers, from the Jews and Christians, and wish to make distinction between God and His messengers, is that they belie the messengers of God whom He sent to His creation with His revelation, and they claim that they have fabricated lies against their Lord. This is the meaning of their desire to make distinction between God and His messengers, by attributing lies and slander to them, and their false claims against them, and they say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ meaning that they say, We believe in this and disbelieve in that, just as the Jews did when they belied Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them and grant them peace, and believed in Moses and all the prophets before him, according to their claim. And as the Christians did by denying Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in Jesus and all the prophets before him, according to their claim, and they want to take a way in between, He says: And those who differentiate between God and His messengers, who claim that they believe in some and disbelieve in others, want to take a way in between their saying: We believe in some prophets and disbelieve in others, a way, meaning: a path to the misguidance that they created, and the innovation that they invented, to which they call the ignorant among the people.
4:151: Then the Most High said to His servants, alerting them to their misguidance and disbelief: Those are the disbelievers in truth. He says: O people, those whose description I have described to you are the people of disbelief in Me, who truly deserve My punishment and eternity in My Fire. So be certain of that, and do not let their fabrication of lies and their claim that they acknowledge what they claim they acknowledge of the Books and Messengers cause you to doubt, for what they claim of that is a lie. That is because the one who believes in the Books and Messengers is the one who believes in all that is in the Book that he claims to believe in, and in what the Messenger brought that he claims to believe in. As for the one who believes in some of that and denies some of it, then he is a prophet. Whoever denies some of what he brought is a denier, and whoever denies the prophethood of a prophet is a liar. Those who denied the prophethood of some of the prophets and claimed to believe in others are disbelievers in those whom they claim to believe in, because they deny some of what their Lord brought them. They are disbelievers in God and His messengers, whom they claim to believe in, and those who claim to deny them are disbelievers. They are the ones who truly deny the Oneness of God and the prophethood of His prophets and truly disbelieve in that. So beware of being deceived by them and their innovations, for We have prepared for them a humiliating punishment. As for his statement: And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment, he means: And We have prepared for those who deny God and His Messenger with the denial of those whose command I have described to you, O people, from the People of the Book, and for others from all other races of disbelievers, a humiliating punishment in the Hereafter, meaning: it humiliates the one who is punished with it by his eternity in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers and wish to make distinction between God and His messengers and say, “We believe in some and disbelieve in others, and wish to adopt a way in between - those are the disbelievers, truly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.” Those are the enemies of God, the Jews and the Christians. The Jews believed in the Torah and Moses, but disbelieved in the Gospel and Jesus. The Christians believed in the Gospel and Jesus, but disbelieved in the Qur’an and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they adopted Judaism and Christianity, which are two innovations that are not from God, and they abandoned Islam, which is the religion of God with which He sent His messengers. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers and wish to make distinction between God and His messengers, say: Muhammad is not a messenger of God! And the Jews say: Jesus is not a messenger of God! They have made distinction between God and His messengers, and they say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others.’ So these people believe in some and disbelieve in others. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers to His statement: a way between that, he said: The Jews and the Christians. The Jews believed in Ezra and disbelieved in Jesus, and the Christians believed in Jesus and disbelieved in Ezra, and they believed in the Prophet and disbelieved in the other, and they wish to adopt a way between that, he said: A religion by which they worship God.
4:152: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And those who believed in the Oneness of God, and acknowledged the prophethood of all His Messengers, and believed them in what they brought to them from God of the laws of His religion, and made no distinction between any of them, meaning: and they did not disbelieve some of them and believe others, but they acknowledged that everything they brought from their Lord was true. Those, meaning: those who are of this description from the believers in God and His Messengers, He will give them, meaning: He will give them, their reward, meaning: their reward and recompense for their belief in the Messengers in the Oneness of God and the laws of His religion, and what they brought from God, and God is Forgiving, meaning: He forgives whoever among His creation did that for his past sins, so He covers it for him by pardoning him for it, and leaving punishment for him, for He has always been Forgiving of the sins of those among His creation who turn to Him, Merciful, meaning: and He has always been Merciful to them, by His favor. They should be guided to the path of truth and guided to what will save them from the Fire.
4:153: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: The People of the Book ask you, O Muhammad, meaning by that: the People of the Torah from among the Jews, to send down to them a book from heaven. The people of interpretation differed: about the book that the Jews asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to send down to them from heaven. Some of them said: They asked him to send down to them a written book from heaven, just as Moses brought the Torah to the Children of Israel written from God. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. The Jews said: If you are truthful that you are the Messenger of God, then bring us a written book from the heaven, as Moses brought it. Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, he said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Moses came with the tablets from God, so bring us the tablets from God so that we may believe you! So God revealed: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven, until His saying: And their saying about Mary is a great slander. Others said: Rather, they asked him to send down a book to them, especially for them. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven, meaning a book, specifically, and they asked Moses for something greater than that, and they said, ‘Show us God plainly.’ Others said: Rather, they asked him to send down books to specific men among them ordering them to believe in him and follow him. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: The statement, The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven, is that the Jews and Christians came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We will not follow you in what you call us to until you bring us a book from God to so-and-so that you are the Messenger of God, and a book to so-and-so that you are the Messenger of God! God Almighty said: “The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. And they asked Moses even greater than that, saying, ‘Show us God plainly.’” Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: The people of the Torah asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask his Lord to send down to them a book from heaven, a miraculous sign that would prevent all creation from producing anything like it, bearing witness to the truthfulness of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and commanding them to follow him. It is possible that what they asked of him was a written book sent down to them from the sky to their group, and it is possible that it was books to specific individuals. Rather, what is more appropriate according to the apparent meaning of the recitation is that their asking him of that was a question about sending down a single book to their group, because God Almighty mentioned in His report about them the book in the singular form in His saying: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the sky, and He did not say books. As for His statement: They asked Moses for something greater than that, it is a rebuke from God, the Most High, to those who asked the Book that they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to send down to them from the heaven, for their asking him for that, and a rebuke from Him to them. God says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do not let their asking that be too great for you, for because of their ignorance of God, their audacity towards Him, and their being deceived by His forbearance, if you sent down to them the Book that they asked you to send down to them, they would disobey God’s command as they disobeyed it after God revived their first ones from their swoon, so they worshipped the calf and took a god to worship instead of their Creator and Maker who showed them of His power and great authority what He showed them, because they will not be like their first ones and ancestors. Then God related from their story and the story of Moses what He related. God says: They asked Moses for something greater than that. He did not mean: The ancestors of these Jews and their forefathers asked Moses, peace be upon him, for something greater than what they asked you about sending down a book to them from heaven. They said to him: Show us God plainly, meaning: clearly so that we may see Him and look at Him. We have already discussed the meaning of al-Jahra, including the narration and evidence for the correctness of what we said about its meaning previously, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to say about this, including: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abu Ubaid told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun bin Musa, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Muawiyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, he said: If they see Him, they have seen Him. They only said out loud: Show us God. He said: He is the one who advances and the one who delays. Ibn Abbas interpreted this as meaning that their question to Moses was made public. As for his statement, So the thunderbolt seized them, he means that they were struck dumb, due to their wrongdoing to themselves. And their wrongdoing to themselves was that they asked Moses to show them their Lord publicly, because that was something they had not asked for. We have previously explained the meaning of thunderbolt with the differences of opinion among those who differed in its interpretation, and the evidence for the first of what was said about it being correct. As for his saying: Then they took the calf, it means: Then those who asked Moses what they asked of him, to see their Lord openly, after God revived them and raised them from their stunned state, took the calf that the Samaritan had thrown away from the handful that he had taken from the trace of Gabriel’s horse, peace be upon him, as a god to worship instead of God. We have already mentioned the reason for which they took the calf, and how their affair and his affair were, sufficiently in the past. His saying: After the clear proofs had come to them, means: After the proofs from God and clear indications that they would not see God clearly and openly came to those who asked Moses what they asked. What is meant by clear proofs is that they are signs that show that they will not see God openly during their life in this world. And those clear signs were for them that this was the case: God’s striking them down when they asked Moses to show them his Lord openly, then His bringing them back to life after their death, along with all the other signs that God showed them as evidence of that. God says, condemning their action and explaining to His servants their ignorance, lack of intelligence and lack of dreams: Then they acknowledged to the calf that it was their god, while they saw it clearly and looked at it openly, after their Lord had shown them clear signs that they did not see their Lord openly and clearly in their worldly life. So they devoted themselves to worshipping it, believing in its divinity!! And His saying: So We pardoned that, meaning: So We pardoned the worshippers of the calf for their worship of it, and for those among them who believed that it was their god after God showed them that they would not see their Lord in their lives of the signs that He showed them, for their belief in that, through the repentance that their father completed to their Lord by killing themselves, and their patience in that upon the command of their Lord, And We gave Moses a clear authority, meaning: And We gave Moses an argument that clarifies his truthfulness and the reality of his prophethood, and that argument is: the clear signs that God gave him.
4:154: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: And We raised above them the Mount, meaning: the mountain, and that was because they refused to act according to what was in the Torah and to accept what Moses brought them in it, according to their covenant, meaning: with what they gave God the covenant and promise: We will act according to what is in the Torah, “and We said to them: Enter the gate in prostration,” meaning the Gate of Repentance, when they were ordered to enter it in prostration, so they entered crawling on their buttocks, “and We said to them: Do not transgress on the Sabbath,” meaning by His statement: Do not transgress on the Sabbath, do not go beyond what was permitted to you on the Sabbath to what was not permitted to you, like: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And We said to them, ‘Enter the gate bowing down,’ he said: We were told that it was one of the gates of the Holy House. And We said to them, ‘Do not transgress on the Sabbath,’ the people were commanded not to eat whales on the Sabbath or expose themselves to them, and everything beyond that was permitted to them. There are different readings of this. The general reading of the Islamic countries is: Do not transgress on the Sabbath, with a lightened ‘ayn, from the saying of the speaker: I transgressed in the matter, if you exceeded the truth in it, I transgressed, enemy, aggression, and hostility. Some of the people of Medina read it: And we said to them, ‘Do not transgress,’ with a sukoon on the ‘ayn and a shaddah on the dal, and combining two sukoon letters, meaning: transgress. Then the ta’ is assimilated into the dal, so it becomes a shaddah and damma on the dal, as was read by those who read Aman la yahdi (Yunus 10:35), with a sukoon on the ha’. His statement: And We took from them a firm covenant, meaning: a strong, confirmed promise that they would do what God commanded them to do and refrain from what God forbade them from, as mentioned in this verse and in the Torah. We have previously explained the reason why they were ordered to enter the gate in prostration, and what happened to them in that regard, and their story and their account, and the story of the Sabbath, and what their aggression was in it, so that it is unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
4:155: Abu Ja`far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: By the breaking of these people of the Book whose description you have described, their covenant, meaning: their covenants that they pledged to God to act according to what is in the Torah, and their disbelief in the signs of God, meaning: their denial, of the signs of God, meaning: in the signs and evidence of God that He used against them to prove the truthfulness of His prophets and messengers, and the truth of what they brought to them from Him, and their killing of the prophets without right, meaning: and their killing of the prophets after the proof was established against them regarding their prophethood, without right, meaning: without their deserving that for a major sin that they committed, nor a sin for which they deserved to be killed, and their saying, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ meaning: and by their saying, Our hearts are covered, meaning: they say: there is a covering and veil over them from what you are calling us to, so we do not understand what you are saying nor do we comprehend it. We have explained the meaning of the uncircumcised, and we have mentioned what is related to that in the narration previously. Rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief. God Almighty says: They lied when they said, Our hearts are covered. They are not covered, nor are they covered, but God Almighty placed a seal upon them because of their disbelief in God. We have already explained the nature of the seal on the heart, in what has happened, so there is no need to repeat it. So they do not believe except a little, meaning: So they do not believe - those whom God has described as His seal on their hearts, so they believe in God and His messengers and what they brought to them from God - except a little faith, meaning: a little belief. It became little because they did not believe in what God commanded them to do, but they believed in some of the prophets and some of the books, and disbelieved in others. So their belief in what they believed in was little, because even if they believed in it in one respect, they disbelieved in it in another respect, and that is from the aspect of their disbelieving in those whom they disbelieved in from the prophets and what they brought from the books of God, and the messengers of God confirm each other. And thus every prophet ordered his nation. And likewise the books of God confirm each other, and verify each other. So the one who disbelieves in some of them disbelieves in all of them, from the aspect of his denial of what the book confirms that it is true. Therefore, their belief in what they believed in of that became little. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Because they broke their covenant, he said: Because they broke their covenant, we cursed them, and because they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ meaning, we do not understand, rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief, and He cursed them when they did that. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his statement: Because of their breach of the covenant, the verse. Is it a continuation of the statement before it, or is it separate from it? Some of them said: It is separate from what preceded it, and its meaning is: Because they broke their covenant, disbelieved in the signs of God, killed the prophets unjustly, and said, Our hearts are covered, God sealed them because of their disbelief and cursed them. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So they do not believe except a few, when the people abandoned God’s command, killed His messengers, disbelieved in His signs, and broke the covenant that He had taken from them, God sealed it with their disbelief and cursed them. Others said: Rather, it is a continuation of what came before it. They said: The meaning of the statement is: So the thunderbolt seized them because of their injustice, because of their breaking their covenant, their disbelief in the signs of God, and their killing of the prophets unjustly, and with this and that the thunderbolt seized them. They said: So the statement follows one another, and its meaning is returned to its beginning. The interpretation of their injustice, for which the thunderbolt seized them, is what the Most High explained, from their breaking the covenant, their killing of the prophets, and the rest of what was mentioned of their affair in which they wronged themselves. Abu Ja`far said: The correct statement in this regard is that his statement, Because they broke their covenant, and what follows it, is separate in meaning from the meaning of what preceded it, and that the meaning of the statement is: Because they broke their covenant, and disbelieved in the signs of God, and thus and thus, We cursed them and became angry with them. So He omitted mentioning their curse, because His statement, Rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief, indicates the meaning of that. For whoever has his heart sealed, He has cursed and become angry with him. We think that this is more correct, because those who were struck by lightning were only in the time of Moses, and those who killed the prophets, and those who accused Mary of the great slander and said: We killed the Messiah, were a long time after Moses. Those who accused Mary of the great slander did not live in the time of Moses, nor did those of his people who were struck by lightning. Since this is the case, it is known that those who were struck by lightning were not punished for accusing Mary of a great slander, nor for saying: We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary. Since this is the case, it is clear that the people who said this statement were not the ones who were punished by the lightning. Since this is the case, it is clear that the meaning of His statement, Because they broke their covenant, is separate from the meaning of His statement, So the lightning struck them because of their wrongdoing.
4:156: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And by the disbelief of those whose description He described, And their saying against Mary a great slander, meaning: By their slander against her, and their accusing her of adultery, which is a great slander, because they accused her of that, and she was innocent of what they accused her of without proof or evidence, so they slandered her with falsehood. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And their saying against Mary is a great slander, meaning: that they accused her of adultery. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And their saying against Mary a great slander, when they accused her of adultery. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ya`la bin Ubayd told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, regarding the statement: And their saying against Mary a great slander, he said: They said: She committed adultery.
4:157: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He meant: And by their saying, We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of God. Then God denied their claim, saying: And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared so to them, meaning: And they did not kill Jesus, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared so to them. The interpreters differed regarding the nature of the likeness that was given to the Jews in the matter of Jesus. Some of them said: When the Jews surrounded him and his companions, they surrounded them without confirming that they knew Jesus specifically, because they all changed into the form of Jesus. So it became unclear to those who wanted to kill Jesus who Jesus was from the others among them, and some of those who were in the house with Jesus came out to them, so they killed him while they thought he was Jesus. Who said that? Ibn Hamid narrated, saying, Yaqub al-Qummi narrated, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Jesus was brought with seventeen of his disciples in a house, and they surrounded them. When they entered upon them, God made them all in the image of Jesus. They said to them: You have bewitched us! Either you bring Jesus to us or we will kill you all! Jesus said to his companions: Who among you will buy himself today for Paradise? One of them said: I will! So he went out to them and said: I am Jesus, and God made him in the image of Jesus. So they took him, killed him, and crucified him. From there, he appeared to them, and they thought that they had killed Jesus. The Christians thought the same that he was Jesus, and God raised Jesus from that day. It was narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih something other than this statement, which is: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying, Ishaq narrated to us, Ismail bin Abdul Karim narrated to us, Abdul Samad bin Maqal narrated to me: He heard Wahba say: When God informed Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, that he would leave this world, he was terrified by death and it was difficult for him. So he called his disciples and made food for them, and said: Bring me here tonight, for I have a need of you. So when they gathered around him at night, he had dinner for them and stood up to serve them. When they finished eating, he began to wash their hands and perform ablution with his own hand, and wipe their hands with his clothes. They were astonished by that and hated it. So he said: Whoever rejects anything I do tonight, is not from me and I am not from him! So they acknowledged him, and when he had finished, he said: As for what I did to you tonight, in serving you food and washing your hands with my own hand, let me be an example for you, for you see that I am the best of you. So do not be arrogant towards one another, and let some of you offer themselves to others, as I offered myself to you. As for my need for which I have sought your help, you should supplicate to God for me and strive hard in supplication, that He may delay my death. When they set themselves up to supplicate and wanted to strive hard, sleep overcame them until they were unable to supplicate. So he began to wake them up and say: Glory be to God, can you not be patient with me for one night to help me? They said: By God, we do not know what is wrong with us! We used to spend a lot of time talking, but tonight we cannot stand to spend a lot of time talking, and we do not want to supplicate except that we are prevented from doing so! So he said: The shepherd will go and the sheep will scatter! And he began to say words similar to this, denouncing himself. Then he said: The truth is that one of you will disbelieve in me before the rooster crows three times, and one of you will sell me for a few dirhams and eat my price! So they went out and dispersed, and the Jews were looking for him. They took Simon, one of the disciples, and said: This is one of his companions! But he denied it and said: I am not his companion! Then they left him, then others took him and he denied likewise, then he heard the sound of a rooster and he cried and was saddened, and when morning came one of the disciples came to the Jews and said: What will you give me if I lead you to the Messiah? So they gave him thirty dirhams, so he took them and led them to him. Before that, he had appeared to them as though he were the Messiah, so they took him and made sure of him, and tied him with a rope, and they led him and said to him: You used to raise the dead, and rebuke the devil, and heal the insane, so will you not save yourself from this rope?! And they spat on him, and threw thorns at him, until they brought him to the wood on which they wanted to crucify him, so God raised him to Him and they crucified what appeared to them, and he remained for seven days. Then his mother and the woman whom Jesus had treated and whom God had cured of madness came crying to the place where he had been crucified. Jesus came to them and said, Why are you crying? They said, For you! He said, “God has raised me up to Himself, and nothing has befallen me except good. This is something that appeared to them, so they ordered the disciples to meet me at such-and-such a place.” Eleven of them met him at that place. He lost the one who had sold him and had guided the Jews to him, so he asked his companions about him. They said, He regretted what he had done, so he choked and killed himself. He said, If he had repented, God would have accepted his repentance. Then he asked them about a young boy who was following them and was called Yahni. He said, He is with you, so go, for each one of you will come in the morning speaking the language of a people, so let him warn them and leave them. Others said: Rather, Jesus asked those who were with him in the house to cast his likeness on some of them, so a man from among them volunteered for that, and his likeness was cast on him, so that man was killed, and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, was raised up. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of God. But they killed him not, nor did they crucify him,” until His statement: And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Those were the enemies of God, the Jews, who plotted to kill Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of God, and they claimed that they had killed him and crucified him. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, Jesus, the son of Mary, said to his companions: Which of you will cast my likeness upon him, for he will be killed? A man from his companions said: I will, O Prophet of God! So that man was killed, and God protected His Prophet and raised him up to Himself. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement: And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them, he said: His resemblance was cast on a man from among the disciples, so he was killed. And Jesus, son of Mary, had presented that to them, and he said: Which of you shall I cast my resemblance on, and for him Paradise? A man said: Ali. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: The Children of Israel besieged Jesus and nineteen of the disciples in a house. Jesus said to his companions: Who will take my image so that he may be killed and have Paradise? So one of them took it and ascended with Jesus to heaven. When the disciples came out, they saw that they were nineteen, so they told them that Jesus, peace be upon him, had ascended with him to heaven. So they began to count the people and found that they were missing one man from the number, and they saw the image of Jesus among them, so they doubted him. Based on that, they killed the man, thinking that he was Jesus, and crucified him. That is what God Almighty said: And they killed him not, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared to them so, until His saying: And ever is God Exalted in Might and Wise. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Abi Bazza: That Jesus, son of Mary, said: Who among you will be cast upon my likeness so that he may be killed in my place? A man from his companions said: I will, O Messenger of God! So his likeness was cast upon him and they killed him. That is what His statement means: They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared to them so. Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: The name of the king of the Children of Israel who was sent to Jesus to kill him was a man from among them called Dawud. When they decided to do that to him, no servant of God was terrified by death - as I have been told - as he was, nor was he distressed by it as he was, nor did he call upon God to turn it away from him as he did, to the point that he would say, as they claim: O God, if you are going to turn this cup away from one of your creation, then turn it away from me! And his skin was bleeding from the distress of that. So he entered the entrance where they decided to enter to kill him and his companions, who were thirteen, with Jesus. When he was certain that they were coming to him, he said to his companions from the disciples, who were twelve men: Peter, James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Kenaniah, and Judas Zechariah. Ibn Humayd said, Salamah said, Ibn Ishaq said: And among them, as I was told, was a man named Sarjis, and they were thirteen men besides Jesus. The Christians denied him, and that was because he was the one who appeared to the Jews to be in the place of Jesus. He said: I do not know who he was. Was he one of these twelve, or was he a thirteenth, and they denied him when they acknowledged to the Jews the crucifixion of Jesus, and they disbelieved in what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought of the report about him. So if they were thirteen, then they entered the entrance when they entered and they were with Jesus fourteen, and if they were twelve, then they entered the entrance when they entered and they were with Jesus thirteen. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that a man who was a Christian and then converted to Islam narrated to me that when Jesus came to him, God said: I will raise you up to me. He said: O group of disciples, which of you would like to be my companion in Paradise, on condition that he appears to the people in my image so that they may kill him in my place? Sarjis said: I will, O Spirit of God! He said: Then sit in my seat. So he sat in it, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised. So they entered upon him, took him, and crucified him. It was he whom they crucified and who appeared to them to him. Their number when they entered with Jesus was known. They had seen them and counted their number. So when they entered upon him to take him, they found Jesus, as they saw, and his companions, but they were missing a man from the number, and he was the one about whom they differed. They did not know Jesus, until they offered Judas Zachariah thirty dirhams on condition that he would guide them to him and introduce him to them. So he said to them: When you enter upon him, I will kiss him, and he is the one who kissed, so take him. When they entered upon him and Jesus had been lifted up, he saw Sergius in the form of Jesus, and he had no doubt that it was Jesus. He leaned over him and kissed him, and they seized him and crucified him. Then Judas Zachariah regretted what he had done, so he strangled himself with a rope until he killed himself. He is cursed among the Christians, and he was one of those counted among his companions. Some Christians claim that Judas Zachariah was the one who appeared to them, so they crucified him while he was saying: I am not your companion! I am the one who showed you him! And God knows which of them it was. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: It has reached us that Jesus, son of Mary, said to his companions: Who among you will volunteer so that my likeness may be cast upon him and he may be killed? A man from among his companions said: I will, O Prophet of God. So my likeness was cast upon him and he was killed, and God raised His Prophet to Himself. Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: It appeared to them, he said: They crucified a man other than Jesus, thinking he was him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: But it was made to appear to them, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They crucified a man whom they likened to Jesus, thinking he was him, and God raised Jesus to Him alive. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of these sayings is one of the two sayings that we mentioned on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: that the likeness of Jesus was cast on all those who were in the house with Jesus when he and they were surrounded, without Jesus asking them to do so. But God would thereby disgrace the Jews, and save His Prophet, peace be upon him, from the evil that they intended to kill him, and test with it whomever He wanted to test from among His servants in what He said about Jesus, and the truth of the report about his affair. Or: the statement narrated by Abd al-Samad on his authority. We said that this is the more correct of the two statements, because those of the disciples who witnessed Jesus, if they had been in the state when Jesus was raised and his likeness was cast on the one upon whom his likeness was cast, would have seen him being raised from among them, and they would have confirmed the one upon whom his likeness was cast, and they would have seen him transformed in his form after the form he had of himself in their presence. This would not have been hidden from them regarding the matter of Jesus and the matter of the one upon whom his likeness was cast, despite their witnessing all of that, and it would not have been confused or difficult for them, even if it was difficult for others of their enemies from among the Jews that the one who was killed and crucified was not Jesus, and that Jesus was raised from among them alive. How could it have been possible that this was difficult for them, when they had heard Jesus say: Who will cast my likeness upon him, and be my companion in Paradise, if he had said that to them, and they had heard the answer of the one who responded to him among them: I, and they had witnessed the transformation of the one who responded into the form of Jesus following his answer? But that was - God willing - in the manner described by Wahb ibn Munabbih: Either the people who were with Jesus in the house from which he was raised from his disciples, God transformed them all into the form of Jesus when God wanted to raise him, so they did not recognize Jesus specifically from others because the forms of all of them were similar, so the Jews killed those they killed while they saw him in the form of Jesus, and they thought he was him, because they had known him before that. And those who were in the house with Jesus thought the same as the Jews thought, because they did not distinguish the person of Jesus from someone else, because his person was similar to the person of someone else who was with him in the house. They all agreed - meaning: the Jews and Christians - that the one killed was Jesus, and it was not him, but it was made to appear to them, as God Almighty said: And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared to them. Or the matter in that was as narrated by Abd al-Samad ibn Maqal, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih: That the people who were with Jesus in the house dispersed from him before the Jews entered upon him, and Jesus remained, and his resemblance was cast on some of his companions who were with him in the house after the people dispersed, except for Jesus and the one upon whom his resemblance was cast. And Jesus was raised, and the one who had transformed into the form of Jesus from among his companions was killed, and his companions and the Jews thought that the one who was killed and crucified was Jesus, because they saw his resemblance to him, and the matter of Jesus was hidden from them. Because his raising and the transformation of the murdered man into his form was after his companions had dispersed from him, and they had heard Jesus at night lamenting himself, and grieving over what they thought was about to befall him from death, so they narrated what was true in their view, and the matter with God in reality is different from what they narrated. So those of his disciples who narrated that did not deserve to be liars, because they narrated what was true in their view on the surface, even though the matter with God in reality was different from what they narrated. Abu Ja`far said: What God Almighty means by His statement, And those who differed therein, are the Jews who surrounded Jesus and his companions when they wanted to kill him. This is because they had known the number of those in the house before they entered, as mentioned. But when they entered upon them, they were missing one of them, so the matter of Jesus became confusing to them because they were missing one of the number they had counted, and they killed those they killed because of their doubts about the matter of Jesus. This interpretation is based on the statement of those who said: The disciples did not leave Jesus until he was taken up and the Jews entered upon them. As for its interpretation according to the saying of the one who said: They dispersed from him at night, then it is: And those who differed about Jesus, whether he was the one who remained in the house after those who had left from the number that was in it had left, or not? They are in doubt about him, meaning: who killed him, because they had counted from the number when they entered the house more than those who had left from it and those who were found in it, so they doubted about the one they killed: was he Jesus or not? Because they had lost those they had lost from the number they had counted, but they said: We killed Jesus, because the one killed resembled Jesus in appearance. God Almighty says: They have no knowledge of him, meaning: that they killed the one they killed with doubt and disagreement about him, was he Jesus or someone else? Without them having knowledge of who they killed, who he was? Was he Jesus or someone else? Except following conjecture, meaning, may His praise be glorified: They had no knowledge of whom they killed, but they followed their conjecture and killed him, thinking that he was Jesus, and that he was the one they wanted to kill, but he was not. And they did not kill him for certain, meaning: And they did not kill - this which they followed in the murdered man whom they killed while they thought he was Jesus - for certain that he was Jesus or someone else, but they were based on conjecture and suspicion about him. This is like a man saying to another man: I did not kill this man knowingly, and I did not kill him for certain, if he spoke about it based on conjecture without certain knowledge. So the ha’ in his statement: and they did not kill him refers back to conjecture. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what you said about that. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And they did not kill him for certain, he said: meaning they did not kill him for certain. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ya`la bin Ubayd told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, regarding his statement: And they did not kill him, for certain, he said: They did not kill him, they thought it was for certain. Al-Saddī said about this: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And they did not kill him for certain, and they did not kill him for certain, that the man was Jesus, but God raised him up to Himself.
4:158: Abu Ja`far said: As for His Most High saying: Rather, God raised him up to Himself, he means: Rather, God raised the Messiah up to Himself. He says: They did not kill him or crucify him, but God raised him up to Himself and purified him from those who disbelieved. We have previously explained how God raised him to Himself, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differed on that, and the correct statement on it with evidence attesting to its correctness, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. As for his saying: And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, it means: And God has always taken revenge on His enemies, as He took revenge on those who were struck by lightning for their injustice, and as He cursed those whose story He related in His saying: Because they broke their covenant and disbelieved in the signs of God, “Wise,” meaning: He has wisdom in His management and the way He directs His creation in His judgment. He says: So beware, O you who ask Muhammad, that a book be sent down upon you from the heaven, of My punishment coming upon you, as it came upon your predecessors who did what you did, in their denial of My messengers and their fabrications about My friends. And: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Abi Sarah al-Ru’asi told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, he said: The meaning of that is: He is like that.
4:159: Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that: Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him, meaning: in Jesus, before his death, meaning: before the death of Jesus. This indicates that all of them will believe in him when he descends to kill the Antichrist, so all religions will become one, and it is the pure religion of Islam, the religion of Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: before the death of Jesus, son of Mary. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: before the death of Jesus. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding his statement: Except that he will believe in him before his death, he said: That is when Jesus, son of Mary, descends, and no one from the People of the Book will remain except that he will believe in him. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Before his death, he said: Before Jesus, son of Mary, died. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: Before the death of Jesus. By God, he is now alive with God, but when he descends, they will all believe in him. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: before the death of Jesus. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: before the death of Jesus. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: Before the death of Jesus, when he descends, all religions will believe in him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Before the death of Jesus. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Except that he will believe in him before his death, Isa said, and he had not yet died. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: Not one of them will remain when Jesus descends except that he will believe in him. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisain, on the authority of Abu Malik, he said: Before the death of Jesus. Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: When Jesus, son of Mary, descends and kills the Antichrist, there will not remain a Jew on earth who will not believe in him. He said: That will be when faith will not benefit them. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will surely believe in him before his death, meaning: that some people from the People of the Scripture will come to see Jesus when he is sent, and they will believe in him, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur ibn Zadhan, on the authority of al-Hasan, that he said regarding this verse: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. Abu Ja`far said: I think he only said: When Jesus comes out, the Jews will believe in him. Others said: He means by that: There is none from the People of the Book but will believe in Jesus, before the death of the People of the Book. This is based on the fact that if he sees the truth he will know what is false, because everyone who is about to die will not leave his soul until the truth is clear to him from falsehood in his religion. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: No Jew will die until he believes in Jesus. Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: His soul will not depart until he believes in Jesus, even if he drowns, or falls from a wall, or whatever death it may be. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: except that he will believe in him before his death, every possessor of the Book will believe in him, in Jesus, before his death, the death of the possessor of the Book. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: He will believe in him, every person with a book who believes in Jesus, before his death, before the death of the person with the book. Ibn Abbas said: If his neck were struck, his soul would not depart until he believed in Jesus. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Abu Tamila Yahya bin Wadh told us, he said, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Jew will not die until he testifies that Jesus is the servant of God and His Messenger, even if he hastens to do so with a weapon. Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me, he said, Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: In my father’s reading it is: before their death. No Jew will ever die until he believes in Jesus. It was said to Ibn Abbas: What do you think if he falls from the top of a house? He said: He speaks it while falling. It was said: What do you think if one of them is beheaded? He said: His tongue will stutter. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: No Jew will die until he believes in Jesus, son of Mary. He said: Even if he is struck with the sword, he will speak about it. He said: Even if he falls, he will speak about it while he is falling. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told me, he said, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Ghanawi, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, that he said regarding this verse: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: If a Jew were to fall from the top of this house, he would not die until he believed in him, meaning: in Jesus.
