Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Samad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of a client of Quraysh, he said: I heard Ikrimah say: If a Jew fell from the top of a palace, he would not reach the ground until he believed in Jesus. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim al-Ramani, on the authority of Mujahid: He will believe in him before his death. He said: Even if he falls from the top of the house, he will not die until he believes in him. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And there is none from the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: No man from the People of the Book will die until he believes in him, even if he drowns, or falls, or dies of something. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: His soul will not depart until he believes in him. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. He said: None of them will die until he believes in him - meaning: in Jesus - even if he falls from the top of a house, he will believe in him while he is falling. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, he said: No Jew will leave this world until he believes in Jesus. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: None of them will die until he believes in Jesus, peace and blessings of God be upon him, before he dies, meaning: the Jews and the Christians. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Furat, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: None of them will die until he believes in Jesus before he dies. Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, al-Hakam ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: The death of a man from the People of the Scripture. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: Ibn Abbas said: There is no Jew who dies until he believes in Jesus, son of Mary. One of his companions said to him: How can that happen, when a man drowns, burns, a wall falls on him, or a wild animal eats him? He said: His soul will not leave his body until faith in Jesus is cast into him. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: None of the Jews will die until he bears witness that Jesus is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ya’la told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, regarding his statement: They will believe in him before his death, he said: In my father’s reading: before their death. Others said: The meaning of this is: There is none from the People of the Book but will believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before the death of the People of the Book. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hamid, he said, Ikrimah said: The Christian and the Jew will not die until he believes in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning in his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. Abu Jaafar said: The most correct and sound of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: The interpretation of that is: There is none from the People of the Book but will believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus. We said that this is more correct than any other statement, because God, the Most High, has ruled that every believer in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, shall be subject to the ruling of the people of faith, in inheritance, praying for him, and including his young children under his ruling in the religion. If every People of the Book believed in Jesus before his death, then it would be necessary that if a People of the Book died in his religion, no one would inherit except his young children, or those of them who are Muslims, if he had a young or adult Muslim child. If he had no young or adult Muslim child, then his inheritance would be spent where the money of a Muslim is spent if he dies without an heir, and his ruling would be the ruling of the Muslims in praying for him, washing him, and burying him. Because whoever dies believing in Jesus, has died believing in Muhammad and all the Messengers. That is because Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to confirm Muhammad and all the Messengers, may God bless them and grant them peace. So whoever believes in Jesus and believes in him, believes in Muhammad and all the Prophets and Messengers of God. Just as whoever believes in Muhammad believes in Jesus and all the Prophets and Messengers of God. It is not permissible for someone who disbelieved in Muhammad to be a believer in Jesus. If someone thinks that the meaning of the Jew’s belief in Jesus, which God mentioned in His saying: There is none from the People of the Scripture but will surely believe in him before his death, is only his acknowledgment that he is a prophet sent by God, without his belief in everything he brought from God, then he has made a mistake. This is because it is not permissible for it to be attributed to the acknowledgement of the prophethood of a prophet, if he denied some of what he brought of God’s revelation and sending down. Rather, it is not permissible for it to be attributed to the acknowledgement of the prophethood of any of God’s prophets, because the prophets came to the nations with the confirmation of all of God’s prophets and messengers. So the one who denies some of God’s prophets in what he brought to his nation from God, denies all of God’s prophets in what they called to of God’s religion, servants of God. And since this was the case, and all the people of Islam were unanimously agreed that every person of the Book who died before acknowledging Muhammad, may God’s prayers be upon him, and what he brought from God, is governed by the ruling of the religion he was upon during his lifetime, and nothing of his rulings regarding himself, his wealth, and his children, young and old, is transferred by his death from what he was upon during his lifetime, the evidence indicates that the meaning of God’s statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death, only means: that he will believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus, and that this is specific to the People of the Scripture, and what is meant by it is the people of their time, not the people of all the times that came after Jesus, and that this will occur when he descends, like that which: Bishr bin Muadh told me, he said, Yazid told me, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Adam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The prophets are brothers by bloodline, their mothers are different but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him, for he is a man of medium build, reddish and white, with straight hair, as if his head were dripping even if it was not wet, between two cities. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and wealth will be abundant, and people will fight for the sake of Islam until God destroys in his time all religions except Islam, and God destroys in his time the false Messiah of misguidance, the Antichrist, and security will prevail on earth in his time, until lions will graze with camels, tigers with cows, and wolves with sheep, and boys - or: children - will play with snakes, and they will not harm each other. Then he will remain.” On earth as long as God wills - and he may have said: forty years - then he dies, and the Muslims pray over him and bury him. As for the one who said: “He meant by his saying: ‘They will believe in him before his death’, that they will believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before the death of the People of the Book,” this has no clear basis, because – in addition to its corruption from the aspect that we have demonstrated the corruption of the saying of the one who said: “He meant by it: They will believe in Jesus before the death of the People of the Book” – it is further corrupted by the fact that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not mentioned in the verses before that, so it is permissible to divert the ha in his saying: They will believe in him to the fact that it is from his mention. Rather, his saying: They will believe in him is in the context of mentioning Jesus, his mother, and the Jews. So it is not permissible to divert the speech from what it is in its context to something else, except with an argument that must be accepted from the apparent meaning of the revelation, or a report from the Messenger that constitutes an argument. As for the claims, they are not difficult for anyone. Abu Ja`far said: The interpretation of the verse - since the matter is as we have described - is: There is none from the People of the Book but will believe in Jesus, before the death of Jesus. And after that, except was omitted, because the speech indicates it, so its indication dispensed with its manifestation, like all the other similar examples that we have already explained. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And on the Day of Resurrection, Jesus will be a witness over the People of the Book, meaning: a witness over them by disbelieving those who disbelieved him among them, and confirming those who believed him among them, in what he brought them from God, and by conveying the message of his Lord, like the one who: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them, that he had conveyed to them what he was sent with to them. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them, meaning: He will be a witness against them on the Day of Resurrection that he had conveyed the message of his Lord and acknowledged servitude to himself.
4:160: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: So We forbade the Jews who broke their covenant which they had pledged to their Lord, and disbelieved in the signs of God, and killed their prophets, and said slander against Mary, and did what God described them to do in His Book, good foods and other things that were lawful for them, as a punishment for their injustice, which God informed us about in His Book, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then because of the wrongdoing of the Jews, We prohibited to them certain good things which had been lawful to them verse. The people were punished for the wrong they committed and the transgression they committed. Things were prohibited to them because of their transgression and injustice. His statement: And they often turn away from the path of God, meaning: And they often turn away the servants of God from His religion and the paths that He has prescribed for His servants. And their turning away from the path of God was: by their false statements about God, and their claim that this is from God, and their altering the Book of God, and distorting its meanings from their intended meanings. And among the gravest of that was: their denial of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their failure to explain what they knew about him to those among the people who were ignorant of his matter. Mujahid used to say something similar. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told me, he said, Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: And they avert many from the way of God, he said: themselves and others from the truth. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
4:161: And his saying: And they took usury, which is their taking what they preferred over their capital, due to the advantage of delaying the term after its due date. I have explained the meaning of usury previously, so there is no need to repeat it. And they were forbidden from it means: from taking interest. And His statement: And their consuming people’s wealth unjustly means what they used to take as bribes for judgment, as God described them in His statement: “And you will see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and their consuming of what is unlawful. Evil is that which they used to do” (al-Ma’idah 5:62). And from their consuming people’s wealth unjustly was what they used to take from the prices of the books that they used to write with their own hands, then they would say: This is from God (al-Baqarah 2:79), and other similar vile and filthy foods. So God punished them for all of that, by forbidding them what He had forbidden them of the good things that had been lawful for them before that. God described them as having eaten people’s money unjustly, because they ate it without right and took their money from them without right. And His statement: And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment, meaning: And We have prepared for the disbelievers in God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, among these Jews, the painful punishment - which is the most painful - of the punishment of Hell with Him, which they will burn in the Hereafter, when they come to their Lord, and He will punish them with it.
4:162: Abu Ja`far said: This is an exception from God, may His praise be glorified. He made an exception from the People of the Book, the Jews, whose characteristics He described in these verses that have passed, from His saying: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. Then He, the Most High, said to His servants, explaining to them the ruling on those among them whom He has guided to His religion and granted success in His right path: Not all the People of the Book are described as you have been described, but those among them who are firmly grounded in knowledge, and they are those who have been firmly grounded in knowledge of the rulings of God that His prophets brought, and have mastered that, and have known its truth. We have explained the meaning of being firmly rooted in knowledge, so there is no need to repeat it here. And the believers means: And the believers in God and His Messengers, they believe in the Qur’an that God revealed to you, O Muhammad, and in the books that He revealed to those before you of the prophets and messengers, and they do not ask you as these ignorant ones among them asked you: to send down to them a book from the heaven, because they have learned from what they read of the books of God and what their prophets brought them, that you are a messenger of God, and it is obligatory upon them to follow you, and they have no choice but that, so they have no need to ask you for a miraculous sign or proof other than what they have learned of your matter with the knowledge firmly established in their hearts from their prophets informing them of that, and with what I gave you of the evidence of your prophethood, so they, from their knowledge and their firmness in it, believe in you and in what was revealed to you of the book, and in what was revealed before you of all the books, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: But those firmly grounded in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you, God made an exception for the Athbiyyah from the People of the Book, and among them were those who believed in God and what was revealed to them, and what was revealed to the Prophet of God, believing in it and confirming it, and knowing that it is the truth from their Lord. Then there was a difference of opinion about those who establish prayer. Are they those who are firmly grounded in knowledge, or are they someone else? Some of them said: They are them. Then those who said that differed about the reason for their grammar being different from the grammar of those firmly grounded in knowledge, and they are both descriptions of a type of people. Some of them said: This is a mistake by the writer. Rather, it is: But those among them who are firmly grounded in knowledge and establish prayer. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr, he said: I said to Abaan bin Uthman bin Affan: What is the matter with you that you wrote: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you and those who establish prayer? He said: When the scribe wrote: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, until he reached the end, he said: What should I write? He was told: Write: and those who establish prayer, so he wrote what he was told. Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father: that he asked Aisha about his statement: and those who establish prayer, and about his statement: Indeed, those who believe and those who are Jews and the Sabians (al-Ma’idah 5:69), and about his statement: Indeed, these two are magicians (Ta-Ha: 63), so she said: O son of my sister, this is the work of the writer, they made a mistake in the book. He mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ibn Masoud and those who establish prayer. Others said, and this is the saying of some grammarians of Kufa and Basra: Those who establish prayer is an attribute of those firmly rooted in knowledge. However, when the speech became long and interrupted between those firmly rooted in knowledge and those who establish prayer what interrupted the speech and became long, those who establish prayer was put in the accusative case as a compliment. They said: The Arabs do that when describing and describing one thing, if they are prolonged in praise or blame, they sometimes differ between the grammatical analysis of the beginning and middle, then they return the last to the grammatical analysis of the beginning. And sometimes they make the grammatical analysis of the last the same as the grammatical analysis of the middle. And sometimes they make that one type of grammatical analysis. They cited as evidence for their saying that the verses that I mentioned in His statement: And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made a covenant, and the patient in poverty and hardship (al-Baqarah 2:177). Others said: Rather, those who establish prayer are among the attributes of those who are not firmly grounded in knowledge in this context, even though those firmly grounded in knowledge are among those who establish prayer. All the authors of this article said: The position of the residents in the grammar is lowered. Some of them said: Its position is in the accusative case, in apposition to what in His statement: They believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and they believe in those who establish prayer. Then the interpreters of this interpretation differed in the meaning of the words. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And the believers believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and in establishing prayer. They said: Then His statement: And those who give zakat was raised, in apposition to what is in believe of mentioning the believers, as if it was said: And the believers believe in what was revealed to you, they and those who give zakat. Others said: Rather, those who establish prayer are the angels. They said: By establishing prayer, glorifying their Lord, and asking forgiveness for those on earth. They said: The meaning of the statement is: And the believers believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and by the angels. Others among them said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And the believers believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and they believe in those who establish prayer, they and those who give zakat, as God Almighty said: He believes in God and believes in the believers (al-Tawbah 9:61). The proponents of this article denied that al-Muqeem is an accusative of praise. They said: The Arabs only place an accusative of praise for the description of someone they mentioned after completing his predicate. They said: The predicate of those firmly rooted in knowledge is His statement: Those - We will give them a great reward. He said: It is not permissible to place al-Muqeem in the accusative of praise, as it is in the middle of the sentence, and the predicate of the beginning has not been completed. Others said: The meaning of this is: But those who are firmly grounded in knowledge among them, and among those who establish prayer. And they said: The place of the establishers is in the accusative case. Others said: Its meaning is: The believers believe in what was revealed to you, and in those who establish prayer. Abu Jaafar said: This aspect and the one before it are not found among the Arabs, and the Arabs hardly ever use a noun in the accusative case, even though it has occurred in some of their poetry. Abu Ja`far said: The most correct of the sayings, in my opinion, is that the residents are in the accusative case, in accordance with what is in His statement: With what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and that the meaning of the residents of prayer is directed to the angels. The interpretation of the statement is: And the believers believe in what has been revealed to you, O Muhammad, of the Book, and what was revealed before you, of My Books, and in the angels who establish prayer. Then he returns to the description of those firmly rooted in knowledge, saying: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them and the believers in the Book and the givers of zakah and the believers in God and the Last Day. We chose this over others because it was mentioned that it is in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and those who establish prayer, and it is also in his copy of the Qur'an, according to what they mentioned. If that was a mistake by the writer, it should have been in all the copies of the Qur'an, except for our copy of the Qur'an that was written for us by the writer who made a mistake in his writing, unlike what is in our copy of the Qur'an. And the agreement between our copy of the Qur'an and the copy of Ubayy in that is what indicates that what is in our copy of the Qur'an of that is correct and not wrong. Although if that was a mistake in writing, those from whom the Qur'an was taken from among the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would not have taught those who taught it from the Muslims in the manner of a mistake, and they would have corrected it with their tongues, and taught it to the nation in a correct manner. And in the transmission of all Muslims of that reading, as it is written in the script, the most conclusive evidence of the correctness and correctness of that, and that the writer had no role in that. As for those who attribute this to the accusative case as a way of praising those firmly grounded in knowledge, even though this may be possible in the speech of the Arabs, for what I mentioned before of the reason, which is that the Arabs do not deviate from the case of a noun described by an adjective in its description except after its predicate is complete. And the speech of God, may His praise be exalted, is the most eloquent speech, so it is not permissible to direct it except to that which is most deserving of it of eloquence. As for the one who directed that to link it to the ha’ and the mim in his saying: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, or: to link it to the kaf in his saying: With what was revealed to you, or: to the kaf in his saying: And what was revealed before you, then it is further from eloquence than placing it in the accusative case for praise, because of what I mentioned before about the ugliness of returning the apparent to the implied in the accusative. As for the direction of those who direct the residents to reside, it is a claim for which there is no evidence from the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor is there any report that proves its argument. It is not permissible to transfer the apparent meaning of the revelation to its hidden meaning without proof. As for his saying: And those who give zakat, it is connected to his saying: And the believers believe, which is one of their characteristics. Its interpretation: And those who give the zakat of their wealth to those whom God has made it for and spent it on, and the believers in God and the Last Day, meaning: and those who believe in the oneness of God and His divinity, and the resurrection after death, and reward and punishment, those - We will give them a great reward, meaning: those who are like this, We will give them, meaning: a reward for what they did of obeying God and following His command, and a great reward, and that is Paradise.
4:163: Abu Ja`far said: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah, is that We have sent to you, O Muhammad, with the prophethood as We sent to Noah, and to all the prophets whom I have named for you after him, and those whom I have not named for you, such as: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mundhir Al-Thawri, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim, regarding his statement: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, he said: It was revealed to him as it was revealed to all the prophets before him. He mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because when God exposed some of the Jews with the verses that He revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace - and that is from His saying: The People of the Scripture ask you to send down to them a book from the heaven - and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited that to them, they said: God has not sent down anything to any human being after Moses! So God sent down these verses, to deny them, and He informed His Prophet and the believers in Him that something had been revealed to him after Moses and to those whom He named in this verse, and to others whom He did not name, such as: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, he said, Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said, Sakin and Adi bin Zaid said: O Muhammad, we do not know of God sending down anything to any human being after Moses! So God sent down in that regard from their statement: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him to the end of the verses. Others said: Rather, they said - when God revealed the verses before this one in their mention -: God did not reveal anything to any human being, nor to Moses, nor to Jesus! So God, the Most High, revealed: And they did not estimate God with His true estimate when they said, ‘God has not revealed anything to any human being’ (al-An’am 6:91), nor to Moses nor to Jesus. Who said that? Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka`b Al-Qurazi, he said: God revealed: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven until His saying: And their saying about Mary is a great slander. So when he recited it to them - meaning: to the Jews - and informed them of their evil deeds, they denied everything that God revealed, and said: God did not reveal anything to any human being, nor to Moses nor to Jesus!! And God did not reveal anything to any prophet! He said: So he untied his camel and said: Not to anyone!! So God, the Most High, revealed: And they did not estimate God with true estimate when they said, God has not revealed anything to any human being (Al-An`am: 91). As for his saying: And We gave David the Psalms, the readings differed in its reading. The majority of the people of the Islamic countries read it, except for a few of the Kufans: And We gave David the Psalms, with the opening of the zay for monotheism, meaning: And We gave David the book called the Psalms. Some of the Kufians read it as: And We gave David the Psalms, with a damma on the zay, the plural of zabar. As if they had interpreted it: And We gave David written books and scrolls. From their saying: I wrote the book, azbaru zabaran, and I wrote it, azbaru dhabaran, meaning I wrote it. Abu Ja`far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of the one who reads: And We gave David the Psalms, with the opening of the zay, as the name of the book that David was given, just as the book that Moses was given was called the Torah, and the book that Jesus was given was called the Gospel, and the book that Muhammad was given was called the Criterion, because that is the name by which what David was given is known. The Arabs say: the Psalms of David, and by that they know his book to all nations.
4:164: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: We have revealed to you, just as We revealed to Noah and to messengers We have told you about, and messengers We have not told you about. Perhaps someone will say: If that is its meaning, then why is his saying: and messengers in the accusative case, not in the genitive case? It was said: It was made accusative because it did not refer to what lowered the nouns before it, and the nouns before it, even if they were lowered, were in the meaning of accusative. Because the meaning of the speech is: We sent you as a messenger just as We sent Noah and the prophets after him, so the messengers were connected to the meaning of the nouns before it in the syntax, because they were cut off from it and not its words, because what lowered them did not refer to it, as the poet said: If I brought him bread spread out, eggs cooked together, and sugar He was not satisfied until he got drunk. It may be possible that the Messengers were placed in the accusative case, because the waw is attached to the verb, meaning: And We told you about messengers before, as the Most High said: He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment (al-Insan 76:31). It was mentioned that this was in the reading of Abu and the messengers We have told you about before and the messengers We have not told you about, so this was raised, since it was read in this way, with the male referring back in his saying: We told you about them. As for his saying: And God spoke to Moses directly, He means by that, may His praise be glorified: God addressed Moses directly with His speech, and: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Noah bin Abi Maryam told us, and he was asked: How did God speak to Moses? He said: Orally. And: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Mubarak, on the authority of Muammar and Yunus, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham, he said, Juzi bin Jaber Al-Khathami told me, he said: I heard Ka’b say: When God, the Most High, spoke to Moses, He spoke to him in all the languages before speaking to him - meaning: the speech of Moses - so he kept saying: O Lord, I do not understand! Until He spoke to him in His tongue, the last of the languages, so he said: O Lord, is this your speech? He said: No, and if you had heard my speech - meaning: as it was - you would have been nothing! Ibn Wakee’ said: Abu Usamah said: Abu Bakr Al-Sagani added to me in this hadith that Moses said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that resembles Your speech? He said: No, and the most similar of My creations to My speech are the most severe thunderbolts that people hear from God. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Omar bin Hamza bin Abdullah bin Omar, he said, I heard Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi say: Moses was asked: What did you liken the speech of your Lord to among what He created? Moses said: The thunder of God is Sakib. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman told me: that he told him on the authority of Juz' ibn Jabir al-Khathami, he said: When God spoke to Moses in all languages before his tongue, he began to say: By God, O Lord, how ignorant this is!! Until He spoke to him in his tongue, the last of the languages, with a voice like his own. Moses said: O Lord, is this your speech? He said: No. He said: Is there anything in your creation that resembles your speech? He said: No, and the creation that is closest in resemblance to my speech is the most intense thunderbolt that people hear. Abu Yunus Al-Makki told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uways told us, he said, my brother told me, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Harith ibn Hisham: that Juz’ ibn Jabir Al-Khathami told him: that he heard Ka’b Al-Ahbar say: When God spoke to Moses in all the languages before his tongue, Moses began to say: O Lord, by God, how ignorant this one is!! Until the last of the languages spoke to him in his tongue in a voice like his, so Moses said: O Lord, is this how you speak? He said: If I spoke to you with My speech, you would be nothing! He said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that resembles Your speech? He said: No, and the most similar of My creations to My speech is the most severe of the thunderbolts that you hear. Ibn Abd al-Rahim told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, on the authority of Juz’ ibn Jabir: that he heard Ka’b say: When God spoke to Moses in tongues before His tongue, Moses began to say: O Lord, I do not understand this!! Until God spoke to him in the last tongues with a tongue like his, and Moses said: O Lord, is this Your speech? God said: If I spoke to You with My speech, You would be nothing! He said: O Lord, is there anything among Your creation that resembles Your speech? He said: No, and the closest of My creations to resembling My speech is the most unusual of what is heard of thunderbolts.
4:165: Abu Ja`far said: By that, He, the Most High, means: Indeed, We have revealed to you, just as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and to those mentioned among the messengers, messengers, so He put the messengers in the accusative case to separate from the names of the prophets whose names He mentioned, bearing good tidings, meaning: I sent them as messengers to My creation and My servants, bearing good tidings of My reward to those who obey Me and follow My command and believe My messengers, and warning of My punishment to those who disobey Me and oppose My command and deny My messengers, so that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers, meaning: I sent My messengers to My servants bearing good tidings and warnings, so that those who disbelieved in Me and worshipped rivals besides Me, or went astray from My path, would not argue by saying, if I wanted to punish him: Why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced? (Ta-Ha: 134). He cut off the argument of every falsifier who denied His monotheism and disobeyed His command, with all the meanings of the arguments that cut off his excuse, as an excuse from Him to them, so that God would have the conclusive argument against them and against all of His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: So that people will have no argument against God after the messengers, and they will say: You did not send messengers to us. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise, meaning: God has always been Exalted in Might and Wise in His vengeance upon those of His creation who took vengeance upon Him for their disbelief in Him and their disobedience to Him, after He had established His proof against them through His messengers and His evidence. Wise, in His management of what He managed for them.
4:166: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: If the Jews who asked you to send down to them a book from the heaven disbelieve in what We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, and said to you, God has not sent down anything to any human being, then they have denied you, then they have lied. The matter is not as they said, but God bears witness to His revelation to you and to what He has sent down of His book and revelation. He sent that down to you with His knowledge that you are the best of His creation and the chosen one of His servants, and His angels bear witness to that for you, so do not be saddened by the denial of those who lie about you, or the opposition of those who oppose you. And sufficient is God as a witness, meaning: God is sufficient for you as a witness to your truthfulness, not anyone else from His creation, for if your Lord bears witness to your truthfulness, then the denial of those who lie about you will not harm you. It has been said that this verse was revealed about a group of Jews whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to follow him and informed them that they knew the truth of his prophethood, but they denied his prophethood and rejected knowing him. The report mentioned that: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, he said, Saeed ibn Jubayr - or Ikrimah - told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to them: By God, I know best that you know that I am the Messenger of God! They said: We do not know that! So God revealed: ‘But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And sufficient is God as Witness.’” Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah and Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then he mentioned something similar. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is God as Witness.” Witnesses, and God is not accused.
4:167: Abu Ja`far said: By that, the Most High means: Those who denied, O Muhammad, your prophethood after knowing it, from the People of the Book whose story I have related to you, and denied that God, the Most High, revealed His Book to you, and turned away from the path of God, meaning: from the religion with which God sent you to His creation, which is Islam. And their turning away from it was their saying to the people who asked them about Muhammad from the polytheists: We do not find the description of Muhammad in our book! And their claim that they were entrusted with the fact that prophethood would only be in the descendants of Aaron and the descendants of David, and other similar matters with which they discouraged people from following the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in him and what he brought from God. His saying: They have gone far astray, means: They have deviated greatly from the right path and strayed from the right path. Rather, what He, the Most High, means by their injustice and their deviation from the right path is their deviation from the religion of God, which He has chosen for His servants and with which He sent His messengers. He says: Whoever denies the message of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and turns away from the religion with which he was sent, has gone astray and departed from the religion which is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets, a far-off misguidance.
4:168: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Those who denied the message of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and disbelieved in God by denying that, and were unjust by remaining in unbelief, knowing that they were unjust to God’s servants, and out of envy of the Arabs, and out of malice towards His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would not forgive them, meaning: God would not pardon their sins by not punishing them for them, but He would disgrace them by punishing them for them, nor would He guide them to a path, meaning: God, may His praise be glorified, would not guide these disbelievers and wrongdoers, whose characteristics we have described, and would guide them to a path from the paths by which they would attain God’s reward, and reach Paradise by adhering to it, but He would let them down from that, until they took the path to Hell.
4:169: And he only mentioned the path in reference to religion. The meaning of the speech is: God would not guide them to Islam, but He would let them down from it to the path of Hell, which is disbelief, meaning: until they disbelieve in God and His Messengers, and enter Hell, abiding therein forever, meaning: residing therein forever, and that is easy for God, meaning: and the eternal confinement of those whose description I have described to you in Hell was easy for God, because the one who wanted that for him would not be able to prevent it, and he would not have anyone to prevent him from it, and what he wanted to do to him would not be difficult for Him, and that was easy for God, because the creation is His creation, and the command is His command.
4:170: Abu Ja`far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: O mankind, the polytheists of the Arabs and all other types of disbelief, There has come to you the Messenger, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has come to you, with the truth from your Lord, meaning: with Islam which God has chosen for His servants as a religion. He says: From your Lord, meaning: from your Lord. So believe, it is better for you, meaning: so believe in him and believe in what he has brought to you from your Lord of religion, for belief in that is better for you than disbelief in it. And if you disbelieve, meaning: even if you deny his message and belie him and what he has brought to you from your Lord, then your denial of that and your belying of it will not harm anyone but you, and the dislike of that will only return to you, not to the One who commanded you with what He sent to you His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with. That is because God owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth, dominion and creation, and your disbelief will not diminish what you have disbelieved in. Of His command, and your disobedience to Him in what you disobeyed Him in, of His kingdom and authority, And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, He says: And God is All-Knowing, of what you are going to do of obeying Him in what He commanded you to do and what He forbade you from doing, and disobeying Him in that, with His knowledge of that from you, your command and your prohibition, Wise, meaning: Wise in His command to you with what He commanded you to do, and in His prohibition of you from what He forbade you from doing, and in other than that of His management of you and others of His creation. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning for which the phrase better for you was used. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The accusative of khayran is to exclude what preceded it from the statement, because what preceded it from the statement was complete, and that is His statement: So believe. He said: You have heard the Arabs do that in every complete statement, then a statement is connected to it after its completion, in the same way that khayran is connected to what preceded it. So you say: It is better for you to stand up and if you did that, it is better for you, and Fear God, it is better for you. He said: But if the statement is incomplete, it can only be in the nominative case, like your saying: If you fear God, it is better for you, and If you are patient, it is better for you (An-Nisa’: 25). Another of them said: The accusative case came in Khair because the original sentence was: So believe, it is better for you. So when he was dropped, which is a metaphor and a verbal noun, the sentence was connected to what came before it, and what came before it was definite, and Khair was indefinite, so it was in the accusative case because it was connected to the definite... because the omission is from the verb qama, so standing is better for you, and do not stand, so leaving standing is better for you. So when qama was dropped, it was connected to the first. And he said: Don’t you see that you see that the metaphor for the command is appropriate before the report, so you say to the man: Fear God, it is better for you, meaning: Fearing God is better for you. And he said: Its accusative case is not based on the omission of yakan, because that comes with an analogy that invalidates this. Don’t you see that you say: Fear God, you will be a doer of good, and it is not permissible to say: Fear God, a doer of good, while you are implying kan, and it is not appropriate to say: Insarna Akhana, while you mean: You will be our Akhana? And the one who said this claimed that this is not permissible except in af’al specifically, so you say: Do this, it is better for you, and Do not do this, it is better for you. Do not say: It is better for you. He claimed that it was said with af’al because af’al indicates that this is better than that. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Khairan is in the accusative case because when he said to them: Believe, he ordered them to do what is best for them, so it is as if he said: Do what is best for you, and likewise: Stop, it is best for you (An-Nisa’: 71). He said: This only occurs in commands and prohibitions, and not in report. You do not say: It is best for me to stop, but it is in the nominative case in two statements, because commands and prohibitions are implied in them, so it is as if you took it from one thing to another, because when you said to it: Stop, it is as if you said to it: Get out of this and enter another. He cited as evidence the words of the poet Omar bin Abi Rabi’ah: Promise me that you will let go of your wealth or that interest will be easier between them As you say? And promise him good for you. He said: I have heard this accusative in the report. The Arabs say: I come to the house for good for me, and I leave it for good for me, and it is as I explained to you in the command and prohibition. Another of them said: He put good in the accusative case with an implied verb, and he was satisfied with that implied verb by saying: Do not do this or do good, and he permitted it in something other than I do, so he said: Do not do that for your own good. Another of them said: The word khayran is in the accusative case as a pronoun in response to yakan khayran lakum. He said: This is the case with every command and prohibition.
4:171: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: O People of the Book, O People of the Gospel from among the Christians, do not go to extremes in your religion, is that do not exceed the truth in your religion, so that you are excessive in it, and do not say about Jesus other than the truth, for if you say about Jesus that he is the son of God, then you are saying about God other than the truth. Because God did not take a son, so that Jesus or anyone else among His creation would be His son, and do not say about God except the truth. The root of exaggeration is in everything, exceeding its limit, which is its limit. It is said of it in religion: he has gone too far, so he is going too far, and he went too far with the girl, her bones and flesh, if she hastens her youth and exceeds her pleasure, he goes too far for her with exaggeration, and exaggeration, and from that is the saying of Al-Harith bin Khalid Al-Makhzumi: Khamsana, worried, her scarf is full of young men's dreams, her price is great And: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, he said: They became two groups: a group that went to extremes in religion, and their extremism in it was doubt in it and aversion to it, and a group of them fell short of it, so they disobeyed the command of their Lord. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: The Messiah is only Jesus, the son of Mary, is not the Messiah, O you who are extremists in their religion from the People of the Book, the son of God, as you claim, but he is Jesus, the son of Mary, and no other of creation, and he has no lineage other than that. Then God, the Most High, described him with His description and described him with His attribute, saying: He is the Messenger of God, sent by God with the truth to whomever He sent him to from His creation. The root of the word Christ is the anointed one, which was changed from a passive participle to a fa’il. God called him this because He purified him from sins. It was said: He was anointed from the sins and filth that are in humans, just as something is anointed from the harm that is in it, so it is purified from it. That is why Mujahid and those who said the same thing said: The Messiah, the Truthful One. Some people have claimed that the origin of this word is Hebrew or Syriac, Messiah, and it was Arabized and said: The Messiah, just as the names of the other prophets in the Qur’an were Arabized, such as: Ishmael, Isaac, Moses, and Jesus. Abu Ja`far said: The example given for the Messiah has no parallel. This is because Ishmael, Isaac, and the like are names, not attributes, and the Messiah is an attribute. It is not permissible to address the Arabs, or any other race of creation, regarding a description of something except in the manner that they understand from the one addressing them. If the Messiah was not from the language of the Arabs, and the Arabs did not understand its meaning, they would not have been addressed with it. We have already provided sufficient clarification of similar examples of this in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. As for the Antichrist, it also means: the one whose eye is anointed, changed from maf’ul to fa’il. So the meaning of the Messiah in Jesus, peace be upon him, is: the one whose body is anointed from filth and sins, and the meaning of the Messiah in the Antichrist is: the one whose right or left eye is anointed, as was narrated from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, in that regard. As for his saying: And His word which He cast into Mary, he means by the word the message that God commanded His angels to bring to Mary, good report from God to her, which God, the Most High, mentioned in His saying: When the angels said, ‘O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him’ (Al Imran 3:45), meaning: a message from Him, and good report from Him. Qatada said about this: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And His word which He cast into Mary, he said: It is His saying: Be, and it was. We have previously explained the differences of opinion among the Muslims on this matter, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. His saying: He cast it to Mary, means: He informed her of it and told her, just as one says: I cast a good word to you, meaning: I informed you of it and spoke to you about it. As for his saying: And a spirit from Him, the scholars differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of his saying: And a spirit from Him is a breath from Him, because he spoke about Gabriel’s breath, peace be upon him, into Mary’s armor by God’s command to him to do so, so it was attributed to him being a spirit from God, because it was by His command. He said: And the breath was called a spirit because it is a wind that comes out of the spirit, and they cited as evidence for that their saying the words of Dhu al-Rummah in describing a fire, which he described: When her shroud was revealed, she was a child, with a veil that was not even a cubit long. And I said to him, Raise it to you, revive it with your spirit, and buy it for her a proper price. And make it appear to her from the dry she-camel, and seek help from the youth on it, and make your hands a cover for it. And when it grows, it eats the poison. It leaves nothing withered from what they gather, nor green. When it flowed in abundance like lightning, we expressed our gratitude to its Creator. They said: What he meant by his saying: Bring it to life with your spirit is: Bring it to life with your breath. Some of them said that what he meant by his saying: and a spirit from Him is that he was a human being by God bringing him to life by saying: Be. They said: Rather, the meaning of his saying: and a spirit from Him and life from Him, is in the sense that God brought him to life by creating him. Others said: The meaning of his saying: and a spirit from Him is: and a mercy from Him, as God Almighty said in another place: And supported them with a spirit from Him (al-Mujadilah 58:22). They said: Its meaning in this place is: and a mercy from Him. They said: So God made Jesus a mercy from Him to those who followed him, believed in him, and confirmed him, because he guided them to the path of righteousness. Others said: The meaning of this is: A spirit from God created her and formed her, then sent her to Mary, so she entered her mouth, and God Almighty made her the spirit of Jesus, peace be upon him. Who said that? Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Sa`d told us, he said, Abu Ja`far told us, on the authority of al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b, regarding His statement: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-A`raf: 172), he said: He took them and made them into spirits, then He formed them, then He made them speak, and the spirit of Jesus was among those spirits from whom He took the covenant and pledge, so He sent that spirit to Mary, and it entered her mouth, so she carried the one who spoke to her, and he was the spirit of Jesus, peace be upon him. Others said: The meaning of the spirit here is Gabriel, peace be upon him. They said: The meaning of the speech is: And His word that He cast into Mary, and a spirit from God also cast it into her. They said: So the spirit is connected to what is in His statement: He cast it of the mention of God, meaning: That the casting of the word into Mary was from God, then from Gabriel, peace be upon him. Abu Jaafar said: All of these sayings have a point and a doctrine that is not far from the truth. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: So believe in God and His messengers, is that you, O People of the Book, believe in the oneness of God and His Lordship, and that He has no son, and believe in His messengers in what they brought to you from God, and in what they informed you of, that God is One, with no partner, no companion, and no son, and do not say, ‘Three,’ meaning: and do not say: the lords are three. The three were raised by an omitted word indicated by the apparent meaning, which is they. The meaning of the statement is: And do not say they are three. This is permissible because a statement is a narration, and the Arabs do that in a narration. From this is the statement of God: They will say, ‘Three,’ their dog being the fourth. (al-Kahf 18:22). Likewise, everything that comes after a statement that does not have a raiser with it, then it contains an implied name that raises that name. Then He, the Most High, said to them, threatening them for their great statement that they said about God: Stop, O you who say: God is the third of three, from what you say of falsehood and polytheism with God, for stopping that is better for you than saying it, because you will have immediate punishment from God for what you said, if you persist in it and do not turn to the truth to which I have commanded you to turn, and the term in your resurrection. Abu Ja`far said: What he means by his saying, God is but one God, is what God is, O you who say: God is the third of three, as you say, because whoever has a son is not a god. Likewise, whoever has a wife, it is not permissible for him to be a god who is worshipped. But God, to whom belongs divinity and worship, is one God who is worshipped, who has no son, no father, no wife, and no partner. Then He, the Most High, glorified and exalted Himself above what His disbelieving enemies said about Him, saying: Glory be to Him that He should have a son. He says: God, the Most High, the Most Majestic, the Most Great, the Most Great, and the Most Exalted, is far above having a son or a wife. Then He, the Most High, informed His servants: That Jesus, his mother, and all those in the heavens and on the earth are His male and female servants and creation, and that He is their Provider and Creator, and that they are in need and want of Him, as an argument from Him against those who claimed that the Messiah is his son, and that if he were his son as they said, he would not have needed Him, nor would he have been a slave owned by Him. So He said: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of all things, as ownership and creation, and He provides for them, sustains them, and manages them. So how can the Messiah be the son of God, while he is on the earth or in the heavens, other than being in some of these places? And his saying: And sufficient is God as a Disposer of affairs, means: And what is in the heavens and what is on the earth is sufficient for God as a Guardian, Manager, and Provider, so that there is no need for anyone other than Him.
4:172: He, may His praise be glorified, means by His saying: The Messiah will not disdain, the Messiah will not be disdainful or arrogant, to be a servant of God, meaning: to be a servant of God, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The Messiah will not disdain to be a servant of God, nor will the angels brought near. The Messiah will not be ashamed to be a servant of God, nor will the angels. As for his saying: nor the angels brought near, it means: Nor will His close messengers, whom God brought near and raised their status above the rest of His creation, disdain to acknowledge worship of God and submit to Him in that. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak that he used to say about that: Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Bazuri told me, he said, Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, he said: I said to Al-Dahhak: Who are those brought near? He said: The closest of them to the second heaven. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And whoever is too proud to worship his Lord, and is too proud to humble himself and submit to Him in obedience from all of creation, and is too arrogant to do that, He will gather them all together to Himself, meaning: He will resurrect them all on the Day of Resurrection, and will gather them for their appointment with Him.
4:173: Abu Ja`far said: By that, the Most High means: As for the believers who acknowledge the Oneness of God, submit to Him in obedience, humble themselves before Him in servitude, and perform righteous deeds, that is: they return to their Lord having believed in Him and His Messengers, and have done what His Messengers brought them from their Lord, of doing what He commanded them to do, and avoiding what He commanded them to avoid, He will give them their rewards in full, meaning: He will give them the full and complete reward for their righteous deeds, and increase them from His bounty, meaning the Most High: He will increase them over what He promised them of reward for their righteous deeds and recompense for them, of bounty and increase that they do not know its extent and He has not set a limit for it, and that is because God promised to whomever of His believing servants comes with one good deed ten times its like in reward and recompense. This is the reward of every worker for his righteous work from the people of faith, the amount of which is limited, and the increase over that is a favor from God upon them, even though all of that is from His favor upon His servants. However, what He promised His believing servants that He would fulfill for them and not diminish their reward for their righteous works is what He has limited in amount from one-tenth, and the increase over that is unlimited in amount, so He increases whomever He wills from His creation to that as much as He wills, there is no limit to its amount that can be stopped. Some of them said: The increase is up to seven hundred times. Others said: Up to two thousand. I have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on this matter before, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. And His statement: And as for those who disdain and are arrogant, it means: As for those who are too proud to acknowledge God’s worship and submit to Him in obedience, and are too arrogant to humble themselves before His divinity and worship, and surrender to His Lordship and Oneness, He will punish them with a painful punishment, meaning: a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper, meaning: And those who disdain and are arrogant about it, when God punishes them with His painful punishment, will not find for themselves any protector or helper other than God, or helper, meaning: nor a helper who will aid them and rescue them from their Lord, and repel from them with His strength the wrath that has befallen them, like what they used to do to them when others from the people of this world wanted to harm them in this world, by aiding and defending them.
4:174: Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: O mankind, there has come to you a proof from your Lord, is O people of all kinds of religions, Jews, Christians, and polytheists, whose stories He, the Most High, recounted in this Surah, There has come to you a proof from your Lord, meaning: A proof has come to you from God that proves to you the length of your religions and faiths that you have been adhering to, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom God made a proof upon you that cut off your excuse, and conveyed to you the excuse by sending him to you, along with informing you of the truth of his prophethood and the fulfillment of his message, And We sent down to you a clear light, meaning: He shows you the clear path and the guiding paths to what will save you from God’s punishment and painful chastisement, if you follow them and are enlightened by his light. And that clear light is the Qur’an that God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: A proof from your Lord, he said: An argument. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O mankind, there has come to you a proof from your Lord, meaning: a clear proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light, which is this Qur’an. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: There has come to you a proof from your Lord, meaning: an argument. Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Burhan, he said: Evidence, And We have sent down to you a clear light, he said: the Qur’an.
4:175: Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: As for those who believed in God and acknowledged His Oneness, and what He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with from among the people of the religions, and held fast to it, meaning: and held fast to the clear light that He sent down to His Prophet, as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And hold fast to it, he said: to the Qur’an. He will admit them to His mercy and grace, meaning: His mercy will reach them, which will save them from His punishment, and will make His reward, mercy, and Paradise obligatory for them, and He will grant them from His grace what He granted to the people of faith in Him and belief in His messengers, and will guide them to Himself on a straight path, meaning: He will grant them success in attaining His grace with which He has bestowed upon His friends, and He will direct them to follow the path of those upon whom He has bestowed favor from among the people of His obedience, and to follow in their footsteps and adhere to their religion, and that is the straight path, and it is the religion of God that He has chosen for His servants, which is Islam. The straight path is in the accusative case because of the separation of the ha’ in the word to Him.
4:176: God Almighty means by His saying: They ask you for a legal opinion, they ask you, O Muhammad, to give them a legal opinion regarding the inheritance of the deceased. We have previously explained the meaning of kalalah with evidence indicating its validity. We have also mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on it, so there is no need to repeat it. We have explained that kalalah in our view is everything other than the child and the parent. If a man dies and has no children, but has a sister, she shall have half of what he left behind. What he means by his saying, If a man dies, is that a human being dies, such as: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: If a man perishes, he says: he dies. He has no children, male or female, and he has a sister, meaning: the deceased has a sister from his father and mother, or from his father, so she gets half of what he left, meaning: so his sister whom he left behind with the description we described, gets half of his estate as an inheritance from him, without the rest of his agnates. And whatever remains is for his agnates. He mentioned that the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were concerned with the issue of kalalah, so God Almighty revealed this verse about it. Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to one another.” So they asked the Prophet of God about it, and God revealed in the Qur’an: If a man dies and leaves no child, and he recited until he reached: And God is Knowing of all things. He said: And it was mentioned to us that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him said in his sermon: Behold, the verse that God revealed at the beginning of Surat al-Nisa’ concerning the inheritance, God revealed it regarding the child and the parent. And the second verse, He revealed it regarding the husband and the wife and the brothers from the mother’s side. And the verse with which He concluded Surat al-Nisa’, He revealed it regarding the brothers and sisters from the father and the mother. And the verse with which He concluded Surat al-Anfal, He revealed it regarding the relatives, some of them are closer to others in the Book of God than the relatives of the agnates. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, “on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: Omar bin Al-Khattab asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the kalalah, and he said: Has God not made that clear? He said: Then this was revealed: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning the kalalah.” Muammil bin Hisham Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said, Ismail bin Ibrahim narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham Al-Dastawai, he said, Abu Al-Zubayr narrated to us, “On the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: I fell ill and I had nine sisters with me - or seven, I am not sure - so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me and blew in my face, so I regained consciousness and I said: O Messenger of God, should I not bequeath two-thirds to my sisters? He said: That is good! I said: Half? He said: That is good! Then he went out and left me, then he came back to me and said: O Jabir, I do not see you dying from this pain of yours, and God has revealed regarding what is for your sisters and made two-thirds for them. He said: So Jabir used to say: This verse was revealed regarding: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are distantly related.” Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hisham - meaning Al-Dastawai - on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir, “On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: I fell ill, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to visit me, he and Abu Bakr, while they were walking, and they found that I had fainted. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: O Messenger of God, how should I decide on my wealth, or: How should I deal with my wealth? He had nine sisters, and he had no father or son. He said: He did not answer me at all until the verse on inheritance was revealed: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are distantly related to others,” to the end of the surah.” Ibn al-Munkadir said: Jabir said: This verse was revealed about me. Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: This verse is the last verse revealed from the Qur’an. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: I heard him say: The last verse revealed in the Qur’an was: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning the deceased who has no children.” Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said: The last verse revealed in the Qur’an was: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning distant relatives.’” Muhammad bin Khalaf told us, Abd al-Samad bin al-Nu’man told us, Malik bin Mughul told us, on the authority of Abu al-Safar, on the authority of al-Bara’ who said: The last verse revealed in the Qur’an was: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to others.’” Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamdani told us, he said, Mus`ab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said: The last Surah to be revealed in its entirety was Baraa’ah, and the last verse to be revealed was the conclusion of Surat An-Nisa’: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning distant relatives.’” There is a difference of opinion about the place where the verse was revealed. Jabir bin Abdullah said: It was revealed in Medina. I have mentioned the narration of that from him previously, some of it at the beginning of the surah at the beginning of the verse of inheritance, and some of it at the beginning of the report about the reason for which this verse was revealed. Others said: Rather, it was revealed during a journey in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were. Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Hameed narrated, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: “The verse, ‘They ask you for a legal opinion. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not descended from relatives,’ was revealed while the Prophet was on a journey, and beside him was Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, conveyed it to Hudhayfah, and Hudhayfah conveyed it to Umar ibn al-Khattab while he was walking behind him. When Umar became caliph, he asked Hudhayfah about it, hoping that he had its interpretation. Hudhayfah said to him: ‘By God, you are indeed helpless if you think that your leadership will allow me to speak to you that day!’ Umar said: ‘I did not mean that, may God have mercy on you!’” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, something similar, except that he said in his hadith: Then Hudhayfah said to him: By God, you are an idiot if you think so. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said: They were on a journey, and the head of Hudhayfah’s camel was at the rear of the Messenger of God’s camel, and the head of Umar’s camel was at the rear of Hudhayfah’s camel. He said: Then this verse was revealed: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning the deceased who has no children.’” So the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, met Hudhayfah, and Hudhayfah met Umar. Later, Umar asked Hudhayfah about her, and he said: By God, you are foolish if you thought that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, met her, and I met her as he met her. By God, I will never tell you anything more about her! He said: And Umar used to say: O God, whoever I explained it to, it was not explained to me. There is a difference of opinion about Omar regarding the kalalah. It was narrated that he said about it when he died: He is the one who has no children or parents. We mentioned the narration about him regarding that previously at the beginning of this surah in the verse on inheritance. It was narrated that he said before his death: He is everything except the father. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talha Al-Ya’muri, he said, ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was never so harsh with me - or: I never disputed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about anything as I disputed with him about the verse of kalalah, until he struck my chest and said: The verse of the summer that was revealed at the end of Surat An-Nisa’ is sufficient for you: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning kalalah.’ And I will judge in it with a judgment that those who read and those who do not read will know, except for the father - this is what I think Ibn Arafa said - Shababah said: The doubt is from Shu’bah. It was narrated that he said: I am ashamed to disagree with Abu Bakr about it, and Abu Bakr used to say: It is what is left out of the son and the father. We have already mentioned the narration about that from him previously at the beginning of the surah. It was narrated that he said upon his death: I had written a book about the kalalah, and I sought God’s guidance regarding it, and I saw that I should leave you as you were. And that he had wished during his lifetime to have had knowledge of it.
