He mentioned the narration about it: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Ma’mari told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab: That Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote a book about the grandfather and the agnates, and he remained seeking God’s guidance regarding it, saying: O God, if you know there is good in it, then carry it out, until when he was stabbed, he called for a book and it was erased, and no one knew what had been written in it, so he said: I had written a book about the grandfather and the agnates, and I was seeking God’s guidance regarding it, so I decided to leave you as you were. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Umar, something similar. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said, Amr ibn Murrah told us, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, he said, Umar said: Three things that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have been better for us than the world and what is in it: the kalalah, the caliphate, and the doors of usury. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us: I heard them mention - and I do not see Ibrahim except among them - on the authority of Umar, he said: For me to know the kalalah is more beloved to me than to have the equivalent of the tribute of the palaces of the Romans. Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, he said: Umar took a shoulder and gathered the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he said: I will pass a judgment regarding the deceased in a manner that women will talk about in their chambers! Then a snake came out of the house at that moment, and they dispersed. Then he said: If God had wanted to complete this matter, He would have completed it. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Abu Hayyan told us: Al-Sha’bi told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab delivering a sermon on the pulpit of Medina, and he said: O people, there are three things that I wish the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had not left us until he had entrusted us with a covenant concerning them that would be binding upon him: the grandfather, the descendants of the deceased, and the branches of usury. Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ma`dan ibn Abi Talhah: “`Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I did not ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about anything more than I asked about kalalah, until he poked my chest with his finger and said: The verse of summer at the end of Surat al-Nisa will suffice you.” Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us, he said, Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Sahmi told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, on the authority of Ma’dan, on the authority of Umar, who said: I will not leave anything more important to me than the matter of kalalah, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was never harsh with me about anything as he was harsh with me about it, until he stabbed my chest with his finger - or he said: in my side - and said: The verse that was revealed at the end of An-Nisa’ will suffice you. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talha: “Umar bin Al-Khattab addressed the people on Friday and said: ‘By God, I will not leave behind me anything that is more important to me than the matter of the kalalah. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he was never harsh with me about anything as he was harsh with me about it, until he stabbed me in the throat and said: ‘The verse of summer that was revealed at the end of Surat An-Nisa will suffice you, and if I live, I will rule on it with a ruling that no one who recites the Qur’an will disagree about.’” Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, similarly. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us, he said, I heard my father say, Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Masruq, on the authority of his father, he said: I asked Omar while he was delivering a sermon to the people about a relative of mine who had inherited a kalalah, so he said: The kalalah, the kalalah, the kalalah!! And he took hold of his beard and said: By God, for me to know it would be dearer to me than to have everything on earth. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it and he said: Didn’t you hear the verse that was revealed in the summer? And he repeated it three times. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Salamah, he said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about kalalah. He said: Have you not heard the verse that was revealed in the summer: And if a man leaves behind a kalalah (An-Nisa’: 12), to the end of the verse? Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said, Ishaq bin Isa told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Abu al-Khair: That a man asked Uqbah about kalalah, and he said: Are you not amazed by this? He is asking me about kalalah, and nothing has been more difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than kalalah! Abu Ja`far said: If someone were to say: What is the meaning of the statement of God Almighty: If a man dies and leaves no child but has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves, and you know that all the people of the Qiblah agree - except Ibn `Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, may God have mercy on them - that if the deceased leaves a daughter and a sister, his daughter gets half, and what remains goes to his sister, if she is his sister from his father and mother, or from his father? And how does that compare to His statement: If a man dies and leaves no child but has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves, and they inherited half from her along with the son? It was said: The matter in this is contrary to what you have gone to. Rather, God, the Most High, made it in His saying: If a man dies and leaves no child but has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves, if the deceased has no male or female child and he is an inheritor as a kalalah, half of his estate as a specified portion for her. But if the deceased has a female child, she is an agnate with her, and she gets what would have gotten to the agnate other than her, had she not been there. This is not limited by a limit, nor is it imposed on her the share of the inheritors in their inheritance from their deceased. And God did not say in His Book: If he has a son, his sister has nothing with him, so what was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr in this regard has a face to be directed to. Rather, God, the Most High, made clear the amount of her right if the deceased inherits as kalalah, and left out the statement of what she has of right if he does not inherit as kalalah in His Book, and He made it clear by His revelation on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, so He made her an agnate with the female children of the deceased. This is a meaning other than the meaning of the deceased inheriting it, if he was inherited as a distant relative. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: A woman’s brother inherits from her if she dies before him, if she inherits as a kalalah and she has neither a child nor a father. Abu Ja`far said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: If there are two, if the ones left behind are the sisters of his father and mother or of his father, two, then they have two-thirds of what their deceased brother left behind, if he had no children and inherited as kalaalah. And if they are brothers, meaning if those left behind are his brothers, men and women, then for the male among them by their inheritance from his estate, is like the share of two females, meaning like the share of two of his sisters. That is if he inherits as kalaalah, and the brothers and sisters are his brothers and sisters from his father and mother, or from his father. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God explains to you the division of your inheritances, the ruling on those who are not related to him, and how their shares are, lest you go astray, meaning: lest you go astray in the matter of inheritances and their division, that is: lest you deviate from the truth in that and make a mistake in the ruling in it, and thus go astray from the right path, as: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, he said: Concerning inheritance. Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Ma’mari told us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, they both said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: When Umar recited: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, he would say: O God, to whom You have made clear the kalalah, but You have not made it clear to me. Abu Jaafar said: The position of that in His statement, God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, is in the accusative case, according to some Arab scholars, because it is connected to the verb. And in the saying of some of them: It was lowered, meaning: God makes clear to you so that you do not go astray, and so that you do not go astray, and the lām was dropped from the wording, and it is required in the meaning, because the speech indicates it. And the Arabs do that, they say: I came to you so that you do not blame me, meaning: I came to you so that you do not blame me, as Al-Qatami said in describing a she-camel: We saw what the wise men saw in it, so we vowed to follow it. Meaning: not to be sold. Abu Ja`far said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And God is All-Knowing of everything, from the interests of His servants in the division of their inheritances and other things, and all things. He says: He is All-Knowing of all of that.
